en/1-1-body-ddf68909.mp3.text: Dhritarashtra says: O Sanjaya, what did my sons and the sons of Pandu do, assembled on the holy field of Kurukshetra and eager for battle? Mamakah means my own. The Pandavas are his brother's sons, raised in his own house, and with that one word he splits the family into mine and theirs. Sanjaya answers with the king's own son, Duryodhana, looking across at the Pandava army.

en/1-1-intro-73de593a.mp3.text: A blind king waits in his palace and asks a single question about the two armies gathering on the field.

en/1-10-body-1706247a.mp3.text: Our force, guarded by Bhishma, is insufficient; their force, guarded by Bhima, is sufficient. Duryodhana openly calls his own army insufficient and the Pandava army sufficient. He doubts his strength because Bhishma guards his side, while Bhima guards theirs. He then orders his commanders to protect Bhishma from all sides.

en/1-10-body-f6d7d19a.mp3.text: Our force, guarded by Bhishma, is insufficient; their force, guarded by Bhima, is sufficient. Listen to the word अपर्याप्तम्, meaning insufficient. Duryodhana openly states that his own army, guarded by Bhishma, is insufficient, while the Pandava army, guarded by Bhima, is sufficient. He then issues orders to protect Bhishma from every side of the battlefield.

en/1-10-intro-4be2af93.mp3.text: Listen for the exact word Duryodhana uses to describe his own army, a word that reveals his hidden doubt about Bhishma.

en/1-10-intro-b22f549e.mp3.text: Listen for the exact words Duryodhana uses to judge the two armies before the first arrow flies.

en/1-11-body-2bd30fa7.mp3.text: Remain at your stations on every front and protect Bhishma from all sides. Listen to the word eva, only. He does not tell them to protect the army or the king, but to protect only Bhishma, making the grandfather the single pillar holding up every warrior. Sanjaya then tells Dhritarashtra that Bhishma, the grandfather, roars and blows his conch to fill Duryodhana with joy.

en/1-11-intro-a1ab0f75.mp3.text: After sizing up the two armies, Duryodhana gives his first command. Listen for how he places one man at the center of the entire battle plan.

en/1-12-body-d0bac28b.mp3.text: The elder of the Kuru clan, the powerful grandfather Bhishma, roared like a lion and blew his conch loudly, filling Duryodhana with joy. Bhishma does not speak. He roars like a lion and blows his conch loudly, and the sound fills Duryodhana with joy because the old man has read the king's fear and answered it with a signal to fight. Then the whole battlefield erupts as both armies sound their own battle horns at once.

en/1-12-intro-82933c2a.mp3.text: Duryodhana orders his men to protect Bhishma, and the old commander answers with a blast of his conch.

en/1-13-body-7ae41732.mp3.text: Then conches, kettledrums, drums, and trumpets burst forth at once. Their sound became thunderous. The word sahaseva means all at once, and it reveals the sudden, unified roar of the entire army joining their commander. Then Madhava and the Pandava sound their own divine conches from their great chariot.

en/1-13-intro-c560495c.mp3.text: Sanjaya describes the moment the battlefield fills with sound, as every instrument of war answers Bhishma's call.

en/1-14-body-7617e18a.mp3.text: Then, seated on the great chariot yoked with white horses, Madhava and Pandava blew their divine conches. Madhava and Pandava, two names, but they sit together on one chariot. The verse names them side by side, showing they are moving as one. Krishna blows the Panchajanya and Arjuna the Devadatta, answering the enemy noise with their own divine sound.

en/1-14-intro-6d13fa85.mp3.text: The Kaurava war cries have just filled the air. Now, from the other side, two conches answer at once. Listen for who is blowing them.

en/1-15-body-e6680f6a.mp3.text: Hrisikesha Krishna blew the Panchajanya, Dhananjaya Arjuna blew the Devadatta, and Bhima of mighty deeds blew the great conch Paundra. Each conch has its own name, Panchajanya, Devadatta, and Paundra. These are named possessions of the three greatest warriors on the Pandava side. The conches of the remaining Pandava brothers follow, marking the full array of the army.

en/1-15-intro-9f8b4c64.mp3.text: Listen for the names of the conches that sound at the start of the war. Three great warriors are named here.

en/1-16-body-edc67a18.mp3.text: King Yudhishthira, son of Kunti, blew the Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva blew the Sughosha and Manipushpaka. The verse names three brothers in a line, but the order matters. Yudhishthira, the king and eldest, blows first, and the twins Nakula and Sahadeva answer with their own conches right after him. The next verse lists the warriors who follow the Pandava brothers into the fray.

en/1-16-intro-005adf5d.mp3.text: The Pandava conches have already sounded. Now the remaining three brothers join the call. Listen to who blows what.

en/1-17-body-79a6c768.mp3.text: The great archer from Kashi, Shikhandi the great warrior, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata, and invincible Satyaki. The names Shikhandi and Dhrishtadyumna belong to the same family, yet they stand on the Pandava side. This shows that the war has already divided the Panchala kingdom itself. Drupada, Draupadi's sons, and Abhimanyu also blew their conches, so the sound of war spreads further.

en/1-17-intro-10a34846.mp3.text: After the five Pandavas, Sanjaya lists the allies who answer the call to battle. Listen for the next names.

en/1-18-body-d8520a17.mp3.text: Drupada, Draupadi's sons, and mighty Abhimanyu each blew their conches separately, O lord of the earth. Notice the last two words of the verse, separately each. Drupada, the five sons of Draupadi, and Abhimanyu each sound their own conches. That terrible sound split the hearts of Dhritarashtra's side, echoing through sky and earth.

en/1-18-intro-140be69f.mp3.text: Sanjaya has just finished naming the great warriors on the Pandava side, and now he describes the sound they make. Listen to how each one claims his own space.

en/1-19-body-872ed141.mp3.text: That terrible sound split the hearts of Dhritarashtra's side, echoing through sky and earth. The word vyadarayat means to rip open or split. The sound of the Pandava conches rips open the hearts of Dhritarashtra's sons before a single weapon is lifted. Yet Arjuna, the source of this sound, does not stand in joy. He lifts his bow, ready to fight.

en/1-19-body-d50bc074.mp3.text: That terrible sound split the hearts of Dhritarashtra's side, echoing through sky and earth. The word हृदयानि means hearts, and it is split. The sound does not just echo through the sky and earth; it tears into the chests of Dhritarashtra's sons. Arjuna sees the enemy line and raises his bow to begin the fight.

en/1-19-intro-266c5756.mp3.text: The Pandava conches sound, and the noise is so fierce it seems to shake the very ground. Listen for who it strikes.

en/1-19-intro-6a9acd09.mp3.text: The Pandava army sounds its war horns. Listen to how that noise hits the other side.

en/1-2-body-62624a8a.mp3.text: Sanjaya says: Seeing the Pandava army arranged in battle formation, King Duryodhana went to Dronacharya and spoke these words. The verse says Duryodhana approached his teacher, Drona, and spoke. He does not go to his own grandfather, Bhishma, or to King Duryodhana, but to his military preceptor, the first person he trusts to speak to. Duryodhana points to the Pandava army and asks Drona to look at it.

en/1-2-intro-7036719e.mp3.text: Sanjaya answers the king's question by turning to his son Duryodhana. Listen to the very first person Duryodhana approaches.

en/1-20-body-a061621b.mp3.text: Then, seeing the sons of Dhritarashtra standing in battle order while the weapons were about to begin, Arjuna lifted his bow. Notice the word kapidhvajah, meaning he whose banner bears Hanuman. The banner on Arjuna's chariot carries the monkey god, a sign of devotion, right at the edge of a war that will destroy the very world that worships him. Arjuna asks Krishna to stop the chariot between the two armies so he can look at the faces of the men he is about to fight.

en/1-20-body-d549fc7b.mp3.text: Then, seeing the sons of Dhritarashtra standing in battle order while the weapons were about to begin, Arjuna lifted his bow. The verse marks the precise moment before violence begins, प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसंपाते, when the clash of weapons is about to start. Seeing the sons of Dhritarashtra arrayed, Arjuna lifts his bow, but he does not yet loose an arrow. Arjuna now speaks, asking Krishna to place his chariot between the two armies.

en/1-20-intro-b54a1c4b.mp3.text: Notice the exact instant the Gita freezes. Listen for the banner and the bow.

en/1-20-intro-d0aca4cb.mp3.text: Listen for the exact instant before the first blow is struck. Sanjaya places us at the edge of violence and names the warrior who hesitates.

en/1-21-body-0dd53a7c.mp3.text: Arjuna says: O Hrishikesha, place my chariot between the two armies, O Achyuta, until I can look at these men who wish to fight and see with whom I must battle in this war. Arjuna calls out to Achyuta, the unerring one, and asks him to place the chariot between the two armies so he can look at the men he must battle. Arjuna then asks Krishna to stop the chariot so he can see the men standing there, eager for battle.

en/1-21-intro-f4c56ef5.mp3.text: Arjuna has raised his bow, but now he stops. He asks his charioteer to turn the chariot and show him the men on the field.

en/1-22-body-4b568410.mp3.text: Arjuna says: O Achyuta, keep my chariot between the two armies until I can inspect these men standing here, eager for battle, and see with whom I must fight in this great struggle. Arjuna repeats his wish to inspect the enemy, using the word yo'ttukaman, those desirous of fighting, which shows he is still thinking only as a warrior. He then asks to see the warriors who have gathered to fight for the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra.

en/1-22-body-a445999b.mp3.text: Arjuna says: O Achyuta, keep my chariot between the two armies until I can inspect these men standing here, eager for battle, and see with whom I must fight in this great struggle. Notice the word कैः, meaning with whom. Arjuna wants to know exactly with whom he will have to fight in this undertaking. He wants to see those gathered here, eager to fight and ready to please the son of Dhritarashtra.

en/1-22-intro-a8368bfb.mp3.text: Carrying on from the request to hold the chariot, Arjuna repeats his condition and asks one more thing before he looks.

en/1-22-intro-e53a72c3.mp3.text: Continuing the same request, Arjuna asks Krishna to hold the chariot still so he can look closely at the warriors.

en/1-23-body-49994d8b.mp3.text: I want to see those who have gathered here, eager to fight and wishing to please the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra. Arjuna does not call them his enemies. He calls them men who have come to please the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra, Duryodhana. He names their motive before their faces. Sanjaya tells Dhritarashtra that Krishna placed the chariot right in front of Bhishma, Drona, and the kings.

en/1-23-intro-15abc7f1.mp3.text: Arjuna asked Krishna to stop the chariot between the armies. Now he looks at the enemy and names the men on the other side. What does he see?

en/1-24-body-2baa76c8.mp3.text: Sanjaya says: Spoken to thus by Gudakesha, Hrishikesha stationed the finest chariot between the two armies, in front of Bhishma, Drona, and all the kings. The verse names Hrishikesha, the lord of the senses, and Gudakesha, the conqueror of sleep. He places the finest chariot in the middle of both armies, right in front of the elders and the kings. Krishna tells Arjuna to look at the assembled Kurus gathered there.

en/1-24-intro-b50eb1ae.mp3.text: The battlefield is set. Krishna has driven the chariot right into the space between the two armies. Listen to where he stops.

en/1-25-body-98dad172.mp3.text: Standing before Bhishma, Drona, and all the rulers, Krishna said, "O Partha, behold these assembled Kurus." Krishna says, pashya, behold. He does not say fight, or attack, or strike. He says only behold. He wants Arjuna to look, to see the faces, before he acts. Krishna speaks to Arjuna in front of the kings, telling him to behold the assembled Kurus.

en/1-25-intro-c5323c2c.mp3.text: Listen for one word Krishna uses to stop Arjuna's eyes on the front line, before the arrows fly.

en/1-26-body-342572a2.mp3.text: Then Arjuna, son of Pritha, saw fathers, grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, friends, fathers-in-law, and well-wishers standing there. Arjuna, son of Pritha, looks and sees a long string of relations, fathers, grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, and grandsons, all standing there. Seeing all these relatives standing there, Arjuna sinks into grief and speaks in fear.

en/1-26-intro-89f84737.mp3.text: Krishna has pointed the way, and now Arjuna looks. What he sees on the battlefield turns a war into a family tragedy.

en/1-27-body-130c234a.mp3.text: Seeing all his relatives standing there, Arjuna sank into grief and spoke in fear. Arjuna looks across both armies and sees fathers-in-law, friends, and relatives on every side. He does not see enemies, but his own people standing ready for battle. Arjuna turns to Krishna and speaks of the pity and grief that overwhelm him.

en/1-27-intro-472607bc.mp3.text: Sanjaya carries the scene forward by telling us what Arjuna sees when he looks past the ranks.

en/1-28-body-32528800.mp3.text: Arjuna says: Seeing my own people gathered here, eager for battle, I am overcome with pity and grief, O Krishna. Arjuna names the feeling directly to Krishna: I am overcome by supreme pity, and I am grieving. He does not hide it. He tells Krishna, having seen these my own people assembled before me. He then describes the physical collapse that pity causes in his own body.

en/1-28-intro-fa673cb6.mp3.text: Arjuna has already recognized the faces on both sides. Now he names the feeling to Krishna. Listen to how he speaks.

en/1-29-body-c75442b6.mp3.text: My limbs are failing, my mouth is drying up, my body trembles, and my hair stands on end. Listen to the word गात्राणि, limbs. These are the parts of a warrior's body, and here they are failing. His hair stands on end, but first his arms and legs give out. He cannot even hold his bow, and then he tells Krishna his mind is reeling.

en/1-29-body-c857b483.mp3.text: My limbs are failing, my mouth is drying up, my body trembles, and my hair stands on end. Each word here is a part of the body giving out in order. First the limbs, then the mouth, then the whole body shakes, and finally the hair stands on end. The collapse is physical before it is mental. Then he speaks of the bow slipping from his hand and the skin burning, as the collapse becomes total.

en/1-29-intro-4746d12b.mp3.text: Arjuna stands on the battlefield, looking at his own kin. His body begins to break down before his mind can fully catch up.

en/1-29-intro-a6e61f7b.mp3.text: Arjuna looks at the army across from him. His body begins to give out before his mind can catch up.

en/1-3-body-8ed14974.mp3.text: O teacher, look at this great army of the sons of Pandu, arranged in battle formation by your wise disciple, the son of Drupada. Duryodhana calls him Acharya, your teacher, while pointing to the enemy lines. He reminds Drona that the enemy commander is his own wise student, Dhrishtadyumna, turning a report into a personal challenge. Then Duryodhana lists the great warriors standing in the Pandava army, matching strength against strength.

en/1-3-intro-44fe22ee.mp3.text: Duryodhana stands before his commander and points to the enemy lines. He names exactly who leads them.

en/1-30-body-b5e33582.mp3.text: My bow slips from my hand. My skin burns. I cannot stand steady, and my mind reels. Listen for the word Gandiva, his famous bow, and how it slips from his hand. The weapon falls because his mind has already surrendered. He then names the physical signs of his collapse, skin burning and mind spinning.

en/1-30-intro-87507ba5.mp3.text: Arjuna has always been the greatest warrior. Listen for the first sign that his strength is failing.

en/1-31-body-f6afdd69.mp3.text: O Keshava, I see only inauspicious signs, and I see no good in killing my own people in battle. Arjuna says he sees viparitanani, opposite or inauspicious signs. He says he sees no shreyah, no real good, in killing his own people in this battle. Arjuna then tells Krishna he does not want victory, kingdom, or even life itself.

en/1-31-intro-25ad819f.mp3.text: Arjuna has just told Krishna his body is failing him. Now he tells Krishna what he sees around him. Listen for the signs he notices and the reason he gives for not fighting.

en/1-32-body-0aecbaa9.mp3.text: I do not desire victory, Krishna, nor kingdom, nor pleasures. What use is kingdom to us, Govinda? What use are pleasures or even life? Listen to the word Govinda, and the phrase what use is kingdom to us. Arjuna rejects these goals because the people he must defeat to get them are his own. He then turns to the men standing before him, the very ones for whom he once desired this kingdom.

en/1-32-intro-6ecce93b.mp3.text: Carrying on from his refusal to fight, Arjuna now rejects the very goals of the war. Listen to how he dismisses them.

en/1-33-body-70f0ac45.mp3.text: Those for whom we wanted kingdom, pleasures, and comfort stand here in battle, ready to give up life and wealth. The people he wanted the kingdom for are the same ones standing on the battlefield, ready to give up their lives and wealth. That is what breaks him. He now looks closer at the faces of those relatives, teachers, and elders standing in the two armies.

en/1-33-intro-b8af5595.mp3.text: Arjuna looks at the enemy lines and asks who the war is actually for. Listen to the people standing there.

en/1-34-body-2795e2e5.mp3.text: Teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law, and other relatives. He names them one by one, teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, uncles, and in-laws, until the battlefield becomes a family gathering he cannot bear to attack. He says he will not kill them even if they kill him, let alone for a kingdom.

en/1-34-intro-60edddee.mp3.text: Arjuna looks across the battlefield at the faces he knows and lists them one by one.

en/1-35-body-ade038bb.mp3.text: I do not want to kill these people, even if they kill me, O Madhusudana. Not even for the rule of the three worlds, much less for the earth. Listen to one phrase, ghnato'pi, even if they kill me. Arjuna is not just afraid; he is saying his life has no price, and he will not trade it for rule over the three worlds. He then asks Krishna what joy they could possibly find in killing the sons of Dhritarashtra.

en/1-35-intro-abb99053.mp3.text: Arjuna stops his bow at the sight of his kin and asks what good a kingdom would do if it cost them their lives. Listen to how he weighs his life against the whole world.

en/1-36-body-032e380d.mp3.text: O Janardana, what joy would come to us by killing these sons of Dhritarashtra? Killing these aggressors would only bring us sin. Arjuna calls them aggressors, yet he says killing them will bring no joy and only stain the killers with sin. He asks again, how can we be happy after killing our own blood, O Madhava?

en/1-36-intro-44086ef1.mp3.text: Arjuna has just listed his kin and teachers on the battlefield. He names the enemy, but his heart is not in it. Listen for the cost he counts.

en/1-37-body-db21788b.mp3.text: Therefore, we are not fit to kill our own kinsmen, the sons of Dhritarashtra. How could we be happy after killing our relatives, O Madhava? The word here is swajanam, our own people. Arjuna says that if he kills his own people, he cannot be happy. He does not say he might be sad, he says happiness is impossible, and that is why he refuses to fight. Yet even as he refuses, Arjuna sees that his opponents do not see the wrong in destroying a family.

en/1-37-body-ebd47a50.mp3.text: Therefore, we are not fit to kill our own kinsmen, the sons of Dhritarashtra. How could we be happy after killing our relatives, O Madhava? Arjuna refuses to fight by calling the enemy स्वजनं, our own people, and then asks how any happiness could follow their slaughter. He points out that greed has blinded the Kauravas to the wrong of destroying their own family.

en/1-37-intro-72d5018b.mp3.text: Arjuna now draws the final line, refusing to trade the happiness of kin for the grief of war. Listen for the word that seals his refusal.

en/1-37-intro-74376ea1.mp3.text: In the verse before this, Arjuna said that killing would only bring sin. Now he asks what kind of joy could ever come from it.

en/1-38-body-aa1e57c9.mp3.text: Though greed has blinded them, they do not see the fault in destroying a family or the wrong in betraying friends. Listen to one phrase, lohopahata chetasa, blinded by greed. It is not that the Kauravas cannot see with their eyes; it is that greed has clouded their minds so they cannot see the fault in destroying a family or the sin in betraying friends. He asks why his own side should turn away from this sin, since they do see the fault in destroying the family.

en/1-38-intro-c3348f9d.mp3.text: Arjuna has just said he would not kill his own kin. Here he explains why the other side does not see the harm they are causing. Listen for the reason they are blind.

en/1-39-body-8cdb75a5.mp3.text: Why should we not turn away from this sin, when we clearly see the fault in destroying the family, O Janardana? He does not wait for the other side to agree. He says that while they are blinded by greed, he and his side can clearly see the fault of destroying the family, and that alone is reason enough to turn away from this sin. He warns that once a family falls apart, its ancient duties are lost.

en/1-39-intro-19babb5e.mp3.text: Arjuna sets aside his warrior's eagerness for victory. He sees that killing relatives will destroy the family, and he asks Krishna why they should step back.

en/1-4-body-16f27b9a.mp3.text: Here in the Pandava army are mighty warriors, great archers, equal to Bhima and Arjuna in battle: Satyaki, Virata, and the great chariot-warrior Drupada. He names Satyaki, Virata, and Drupada, calling them equal to Bhima and Arjuna. Sanjaya then continues with the names of Drupada's sons and the kings from Kashi and other lands.

en/1-4-intro-efa45ca7.mp3.text: Duryodhana stands before Drona and lists the strongest fighters in the enemy camp.

en/1-40-body-702ef19f.mp3.text: When a family falls apart, its ancient duties disappear. When duty is lost, wrongdoing overtakes the whole family. The verse speaks of the entire family, kulam kritsnam. With the elders dead, nothing is left to hold the house together, and the whole line is left exposed to ruin. Arjuna says that this lawlessness then corrupts the women of the family, and from that corruption, social disorder is born.

en/1-40-intro-ee63cdbb.mp3.text: Arjuna now traces what happens after the killing ends. Listen for the word that names the total ruin of the Kuru line.

en/1-41-body-629e4fc8.mp3.text: When lawlessness grows, the women of the family are corrupted. When women are corrupted, mixed social disorder is born. Arjuna names Krishna as his witness and calls him Vrishni, a descendant of his own family. By speaking to Krishna this way, he shows that he is laying out his deepest fear before the one person he trusts most. Arjuna then moves from the corruption of women to the ruin of lineage and the fall of ancestors.

en/1-41-intro-b71116a6.mp3.text: Arjuna has just argued that a family in ruins loses its ancient duties. Now he looks ahead to the next generation. Listen to what he says will happen when lawlessness grows.

en/1-42-body-cce61579.mp3.text: Mixed lineage leads the destroyers of family to ruin, and their ancestors fall because offerings of food and water stop. The word pitroh, ancestors, is followed by patanti, fall, meaning the dead themselves collapse from their place because the rites that feed them have stopped. Arjuna continues, stating that this mixed social disorder destroys the eternal duties of the family and community.

en/1-42-intro-f75d1808.mp3.text: Arjuna now looks past the living to the dead, warning that civil war destroys the very rites that sustain the ancestors.

en/1-43-body-c9c96b54.mp3.text: Because of these faults that create mixed social order, the eternal duties of family and community are destroyed. Arjuna calls his own side kulaghnanam, family-destroyers, and says that these faults destroy the eternal duties of family and community. He now says that those whose duties are destroyed dwell in a lower realm.

en/1-43-intro-b903a6f0.mp3.text: Arjuna is building a chain of consequences for war. Listen for the final item on his list.

en/1-44-body-5d33ec76.mp3.text: O Janardana, we have always heard that those whose family duties are destroyed dwell long in a lower realm. The word anushushruma means we have heard. Arjuna is not stating his own opinion here; he is leaning on a tradition he learned from his elders to justify his refusal to fight. He immediately follows by naming the grave wrong he has resolved to commit against his own kin.

en/1-44-intro-4b328837.mp3.text: Arjuna pauses his argument to cite an ancient teaching. Listen for the authority he relies on.

en/1-45-body-878dd823.mp3.text: Alas, we have resolved to commit a grave wrong, driven by greed for kingdom and pleasure, we are ready to kill our own kin. Listen to one word, vayum, we. The verse says we are ready to kill our own kin, and he includes himself in that we. He is no longer just judging the other side. He now asks what good a kingdom will be if it is won by killing his own people.

en/1-45-body-f8d837bb.mp3.text: Alas, we have resolved to commit a grave wrong, driven by greed for kingdom and pleasure, we are ready to kill our own kin. The word is स्वजनम्, kin, and it comes right before हन्तुं, to kill. With these two words, Arjuna admits his own side is ready to kill its own people. Arjuna now says that if the enemy kills him unresisting, it would be better than fighting them. Listen to his next thought.

en/1-45-intro-7de7d980.mp3.text: Arjuna sees the two armies and the word that stops him is kin. Listen for how he names the wrong he is about to do.

en/1-45-intro-93bef645.mp3.text: Arjuna is no longer looking at the enemy. He is looking at his own side. Listen for the word that makes him own the guilt.

en/1-46-body-0303b0cc.mp3.text: If the armed sons of Dhritarashtra were to kill me in battle while I stood unresisting and without weapons, that would be far better for me. Arjuna says it would be better to be killed unresisting and unarmed than to fight back against Dhritarashtra's sons, revealing his absolute refusal to defend himself. Sanjaya then reports that Arjuna sat down on the chariot, dropped his weapons, and gave way to grief.

en/1-46-intro-8e2f9fee.mp3.text: Arjuna looks at the armed Kaurava army and asks if it would be better to die unresisting than to raise his own weapon against his kin.

en/1-47-body-5ec067ab.mp3.text: Sanjaya says: Saying this, Arjuna sat down on the chariot seat in the midst of the battlefield, casting aside his bow and arrows, his mind overwhelmed by grief. Arjuna casts aside his bow and arrows, his hands letting go of the very instruments of his duty, and he sits down in the middle of the battlefield. Sanjaya now turns to the moment when Krishna speaks to Arjuna, whose eyes are full of tears and clouded with grief.

en/1-47-intro-49275e30.mp3.text: Arjuna has just spoken his despair. Sanjaya watches him drop his weapons and sink down. Listen to the weight of what he casts aside.

en/1-5-body-66eac553.mp3.text: Dhृष्टकेतु, Chekitana, and the valiant king of Kashi; Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Shaibya, the best among men. The roll call keeps growing: Dhrishtaketu, Chekitana, the king of Kashi, Purujit, Kuntibhoja and Shaibya. Sanjaya then lists even more warriors, bringing the total number to seven.

en/1-5-body-7fadbb42.mp3.text: Dhृष्टकेतु, Chekitana, and the valiant king of Kashi; Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Shaibya, the best among men. पुरुजित् and कुन्तिभोज appear as two names in the same breath, and the valiant king of Kashi is named right beside them. Sanjaya then names Yudhamanyu, Uttamaujas, Abhimanyu and the sons of Draupadi, all great warriors.

en/1-5-intro-b4e5fe14.mp3.text: Sanjaya lists the warriors in the Pandava army. Listen for the names that stand together.

en/1-5-intro-f9bcb2c6.mp3.text: Duryodhana is naming the Pandava commanders one by one. Listen for the two brothers who are also his own uncle's family.

en/1-6-body-aabb3d07.mp3.text: Yudhamanyu, brave and powerful, Uttamaujas, brave and powerful, Subhadra's son, and the sons of Draupadi, all of them are great warriors. Listen to one word, sauhadrashcha, Subhadra's son. The Pandavas are not fighting alone; Subhadra's son and Draupadi's sons stand beside them, so the enemy line reads like a full family under arms. Duryodhana then turns from the enemy to name the great warriors on his own side.

en/1-6-intro-f30a746f.mp3.text: Duryodhana keeps naming the enemy's best fighters. Listen to how he names the sons of Subhadra and Draupadi.

en/1-7-body-8725ffd6.mp3.text: O best of the twice-born, note also our own chief warriors. I name them to remind you of our army. He calls Drona dvijottama, best of the twice-born, and then says he names these chiefs just to remind him of them. The word reminds him of the army he leads. Duryodhana lists Bhishma, Karna, and Kripa as the pillars of his army.

en/1-7-body-bcd7ccb4.mp3.text: O best of the twice-born, note also our own chief warriors. I name them to remind you of our army. Having praised the enemy at length, Duryodhana now turns to count his own commanders for Drona. He names Bhishma, Karna, and Kripa, the towering figures of the Kaurava army.

en/1-7-intro-a506006c.mp3.text: Sanjaya has just listed the Pandava heroes, and Duryodhana does not wait to reply. He turns to his own teacher and begins to name his commanders.

en/1-7-intro-ef8d8b0e.mp3.text: Duryodhana finishes naming the enemy and now turns to his own side. Listen to how he presents his commanders to Drona.

en/1-8-body-c2ea2353.mp3.text: Bhishma, Karna, Kripa, Ashvatthama, Vikarna, and the son of Somadatta are also there. Duryodhana lists Bhishma, Karna, Kripa, Ashvatthama, Vikarna, and Somadatta's son, as if the names alone could hold his fear. He now moves from naming his commanders to listing the heroes who have already died for him.

en/1-8-intro-486efe07.mp3.text: Duryodhana is trying to steady himself by naming the great warriors on his side. Listen for who he calls out.

en/1-9-body-d52de2bd.mp3.text: Besides these, many heroes have given up their lives for my sake. They wield many kinds of weapons and are all skilled in warfare. Listen to the phrase tyaktajivitah, having given up life, and madarthe, for my sake. These men have already paid the highest price for his cause, and he names their sacrifice as his own strength. Duryodhana then compares the two sides, claiming his force is smaller but still sufficient.

en/1-9-intro-8cbc56ce.mp3.text: Duryodhana continues his boast to Drona. He names more of his own side's fighters, and then counts one thing as his real strength.

en/10-1-body-17c8fa46.mp3.text: The Blessed Lord says: Listen again, O mighty-armed one, to my supreme word, which I will speak for your welfare because you are deeply dear to me. Krishna opens chapter ten by telling Arjuna he speaks again because Arjuna is dear to him. Krishna now says even the great sages do not know his origin, and he is the source of them all.

en/10-1-intro-4ac61987.mp3.text: Krishna turns to what comes next, asking Arjuna to listen once more.

en/10-10-body-302b61e3.mp3.text: To those who are always devoted and worship Me with love, I give the discernment that leads them to Me. Notice that the gift here is not a weapon or a sign, but buddhi-yoga, the discernment that leads to him. Krishna gives the mind that can find him to those who keep worshipping with steady love. This gift of discernment is not limited to the battlefield; it is a light that destroys ignorance within the devotee's own self.

en/10-10-intro-af92c4fa.mp3.text: Krishna turns the talk from devotion to wisdom, promising a gift to those who love him steadily. Listen for what he gives and to whom.

en/10-11-body-da42e252.mp3.text: To show them compassion, I destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge, dwelling in their own being. Notice the word anukampartham, for compassion. Krishna does not destroy ignorance because it is wrong to be ignorant, but because he pities the one who is lost in it. Arjuna now speaks, and he lists the many names he gives to Krishna in his awe.

en/10-11-intro-22d03718.mp3.text: Krishna continues explaining how he helps his devotees. Listen closely to the two images he uses.

en/10-12-body-a009f484.mp3.text: Arjuna says: You are the supreme reality, the highest refuge, the purest one, the eternal divine person, the first being, unborn, and all-pervading. Arjuna names Krishna the supreme reality and the highest refuge, the pure one, the eternal divine person, the first being, unborn, and all-pervading. He then adds that all the sages, including Narada and Vyasa, speak of Krishna this way.

en/10-12-intro-433842ba.mp3.text: Arjuna has just seen Krishna as the source of all creation. Now he answers with a string of names. Listen to what each title means.

en/10-13-body-f37af98b.mp3.text: All the sages speak of you this way: the divine sage Narada, Asita, Devala, and Vyasa. You yourself also say this to me. The verse names sages like Narada, Asita, Devala, and Vyasa, and then adds Krishna himself to their number. Arjuna then accepts all of this as true, saying that even the gods do not know your full form.

en/10-13-intro-8895d539.mp3.text: Arjuna lists the great sages who speak of Krishna this way, and then adds Krishna himself to their number.

en/10-14-body-2d45df3d.mp3.text: I accept as true all that you have said, O Keshava. O Bhagavan, neither the devas nor the asuras know your manifested form. Arjuna calls Krishna Keshava, and he says he accepts every word as true, yet he admits that neither the devas nor the asuras know your manifested form. He now says that only the Supreme Person can know himself, setting up the next verse.

en/10-14-body-bb0352ea.mp3.text: I accept as true all that you have said, O Keshava. O Bhagavan, neither the devas nor the asuras know your manifested form. The Sanskrit phrase विदुर्देवा न दानवाः means that devas and asuras do not know your manifested form. Arjuna admits that neither the radiant gods nor the demons can grasp it. Arjuna then says that only you know yourself, O Supreme Person, O source of all beings, O lord of all beings, O divine of the divine, O ruler of the world.

en/10-14-intro-62aa8465.mp3.text: Arjuna has just heard Krishna describe his divine nature. Listen now for the exact words Arjuna uses to accept this truth.

en/10-14-intro-c1621415.mp3.text: Arjuna is listening to Krishna describe his divine nature, and he tells Krishna to listen for the one thing that makes this truth so staggering.

en/10-15-body-5ea42d5c.mp3.text: O Supreme Person, you alone know yourself by yourself, O source of all beings, lord of all beings, divine of the divine, ruler of the world. Arjuna says that you alone know your own self by your own self. This shows that Krishna is not dependent on anyone else to know who he is, and he is the source of all beings. Arjuna asks Krishna to fully describe his divine manifestations, by which he pervades and sustains all the worlds.

en/10-15-intro-746f343c.mp3.text: Arjuna has just accepted Krishna as the divine source behind all existence. Now he acknowledges a truth about Krishna's nature and speaks it aloud.

en/10-16-body-1e7c708a.mp3.text: Only you can fully describe your own divine manifestations, by which you pervade and sustain all these worlds. The word tvam, you, shows Krishna filling and sustaining all these worlds through these divine manifestations. Arjuna then asks how to fix his mind on these forms through constant contemplation.

en/10-16-intro-a60a2b9d.mp3.text: Arjuna has just called Krishna the source of all beings, and now he asks for the details of that source.

en/10-17-body-5a6f7802.mp3.text: O Yogi, how shall I know You by constant contemplation? In what forms should You be contemplated, O Blessed One? Arjuna asks how to know Krishna by constant contemplation, and wants to know in which forms he should be contemplated. He wants a concrete anchor for his mind. He asks for a clear way to keep Krishna in his thoughts at all times.

en/10-17-intro-a0387c35.mp3.text: Arjuna has moved from fear to deep reverence, and now he asks for a practical path. Listen for the exact forms he wants to hold in his mind.

en/10-18-body-f6968e20.mp3.text: O Janardana, tell me again in detail of Your yogic power and Your manifestations, for I am not satisfied hearing Your nectar-like words. Arjuna calls Krishna's words nectar and says he is not satisfied hearing them. He is turning devotion into a hunger to know the divine more fully. Krishna agrees to speak, saying there is no end to His divine expansions.

en/10-18-intro-9cf95b42.mp3.text: Arjuna has stopped asking about war and now asks about Krishna himself. He says he cannot hear enough.

en/10-19-body-6f5ec6bd.mp3.text: Krishna says: I will tell you briefly of my divine manifestations, chief of them, Arjuna, for there is no end to their विस्तार. Krishna uses the word विस्तार, meaning spread or extent. He says there is no end to his विस्तार, so he can only name the chief ones, and that too briefly. He begins that brief list by telling Arjuna he is the Self seated in every heart.

en/10-19-body-724e8a39.mp3.text: Krishna says: I will tell you briefly of my divine manifestations, chief of them, Arjuna, for there is no end to their विस्तार. Listen for anantah, endless. Krishna says there is no end to his manifestations, so he can only name the main ones, because a full list is impossible. He then says he is the Self seated in every heart, the beginning, middle and end of all beings.

en/10-19-intro-432e82ff.mp3.text: Krishna starts to answer. Listen for one word that tells you why he can only give a partial list.

en/10-19-intro-7f6a0061.mp3.text: Krishna has agreed to show his divine side. Now he sets a limit on how much he will reveal. Listen for the word that tells us why the list must be brief.

en/10-2-body-bcbf22b7.mp3.text: The hosts of devas do not know my origin, nor do the great sages, for I am the beginning of the devas and the great sages in every way. The hosts of devas and great sages do not know my origin. Krishna states that even these exalted beings cannot trace his source, because he is the very beginning of all of them. Krishna then says that whoever knows him as unborn and without beginning is freed from all wrong deeds.

en/10-2-intro-bfd1e6e0.mp3.text: If the great sages and the hosts of gods do not know Krishna's source, what exactly is this origin he speaks of? Listen for the answer.

en/10-20-body-93fb355b.mp3.text: I am the Self, O Gudakesha, seated in the heart of all beings. I am the beginning, the middle, and the end of all beings. Listen to the word ahama, I am, repeated at the start and again before the end of beings. It shows the same speaker, the same Self, is present at the very start and the very finish of every life. Krishna then names a new pair of opposites, the sun and the moon, among the sons of Aditi.

en/10-20-intro-1c03c129.mp3.text: Arjuna asked to know Krishna’s divine forms, and Krishna replies that he is closest of all: he is the Self inside every heart. Listen to how he names the three stages of existence.

en/10-21-body-5c0bab8f.mp3.text: Among the sons of Aditi, I am Vishnu; among radiant things, I am the sun with rays. I am the brilliance in the Maruts, and among stars, I am the moon. The verse tells us that Vishnu is among the sons of Aditi, and that the sun is among radiant things. By choosing the brightest of each group, Krishna shows that the great powers of the world are simply different forms of his presence. Krishna moves from cosmic lights to the gods, saying he is the Sama Veda among the Vedas and Indra among the radiant beings.

en/10-21-intro-67c2e275.mp3.text: Krishna continues naming the bright powers of the world. Listen for how he places himself among the lights.

en/10-22-body-79275163.mp3.text: Among the Vedas, I am the Sama Veda; among the radiant beings, I am Indra. Among the senses, I am the mind; among living beings, I am consciousness. The word asmi, I am, repeats four times, binding each object to the speaker. The verse places the mind above the senses and names it as the ruling presence among them. He now names the Rudras and Kubera, moving from the inner world of the mind to the outer world of the gods.

en/10-22-intro-4322dfae.mp3.text: Krishna answers a question with four names. Listen for the single thread that binds them all.

en/10-23-body-d37dcf3c.mp3.text: Among the Rudras, I am Shankara; among the Yakshas and Rakshasas, I am Kubera. Among the Vasus, I am fire, and among mountain peaks, I am Mount Meru. Shankara is the greatest among the fierce Rudras, Kubera is the lord of wealth among the Yakshas and Rakshasas, and Meru is the highest of all mountain peaks, showing Krishna is the greatest of each group. Krishna moves on to the greatest of priests, commanders, and waters, to show his presence in leadership and depth.

en/10-23-intro-05f5bd07.mp3.text: The battlefield falls silent as Krishna describes the greatest of each group he represents.

en/10-24-body-01dcbbcf.mp3.text: Among priests, know Me as Brihaspati; among commanders, I am Skanda; among waters, I am the ocean. Skanda, the name Krishna uses for himself among commanders, is the name of the god of war, pointing to supreme martial strength. Next, Krishna turns from human and divine power to the vastness of the ocean and the syllable Om.

en/10-24-intro-473f7507.mp3.text: Listen for one name among commanders. Krishna is naming the greatest powers of the world, and one name here stands out as the peak of military strength.

en/10-25-body-274878e8.mp3.text: Among great sages I am Bhrigu; among words I am the one imperishable syllable. Among sacrifices I am the sacrifice of silent repetition; among the steadfast I am the Himalayas. Krishna names Bhrigu the greatest of sages and the Himalayas the most steadfast of mountains. He also picks the one imperishable syllable and the sacrifice of silent repetition, showing his presence in the quietest and most enduring things. He continues the list with the sacred fig tree, Narada, Chitraratha, and Kapila. The roll call goes on.

en/10-25-intro-5de45eda.mp3.text: Krishna continues his list of divine presences, naming the most revered forms across the world. Listen to the specific names he chooses.

en/10-26-body-675e87d0.mp3.text: Among all trees I am the sacred fig tree. Among divine sages I am Narada; among celestial musicians, Chitraratha; among perfected sages, the sage Kapila. Krishna pairs the greatest among trees with the greatest among divine sages, and the best among musicians with the best among perfected sages, showing a pattern of the highest in every category. He now turns to horses, elephants, and kings, naming the lord of horses born from nectar.

en/10-26-intro-16da33c7.mp3.text: Krishna continues his list of the finest forms. Listen for how he pairs the greatest among trees and sages with the best among musicians and perfected beings.

en/10-27-body-bd7bd23b.mp3.text: Among horses, know me as Ucchaihshravas, born from nectar. Among royal elephants, I am Airavata, and among humans, I am the king. Ucchaihshravas the horse was born from the churning of the ocean, and Airavata the elephant emerged from the same waters, yet both are only one among many, while the king stands above the rest of humanity. Krishna now names the greatest weapons and the king of serpents, the thunderbolt and Vasuki.

en/10-27-intro-4f6311da.mp3.text: A question hangs over the chapter: how can the infinite be seen in the world around us? Krishna answers by naming the greatest of every kind.

en/10-28-body-c558ce2f.mp3.text: Among weapons, I am the thunderbolt; among cows, I am the wish-fulfilling cow. I am the cause of procreation, and among serpents, I am Vasuki. Notice how Krishna includes the wish-fulfilling cow and the force of procreation in his list, placing desire itself among his divine forms. Krishna continues naming the highest beings in creation, moving from Vasuki to Varuna, the lord of the waters.

en/10-28-intro-5c213579.mp3.text: The battlefield of Kurukshetra is a stage for the divine. Listen to how Krishna names his presence in the very forces of creation.

en/10-29-body-0aabec08.mp3.text: Among serpents I am Ananta; among water beings I am Varuna. Among ancestors I am Aryaman; among those who govern, I am Yama. The word is asmi, I am. Krishna says he is these beings. The one presence fills the serpent, the water, the ancestors, and the judge of the dead. Krishna then names Prahlada and the lion, moving from a devotee to a wild beast.

en/10-29-intro-f99f939e.mp3.text: Krishna is naming his own presence inside every part of the world. Listen for the word that repeats after each being he names.

en/10-3-body-29e661be.mp3.text: One who knows Me as unborn, beginningless, and the great lord of all worlds is undeluded among mortals and is freed from every wrong deed. The word asammudhah means undeluded, and the verse says that person is freed from all wrong deeds. Knowing Krishna as the beginningless lord of all worlds removes confusion and frees a person from wrongdoing. Krishna next lists the qualities that arise from him alone, starting with understanding and wisdom.

en/10-3-intro-c5a45af3.mp3.text: Krishna has just said that even the gods and sages do not know his origin. Now he tells the listener what happens when they do know him.

en/10-30-body-123764e1.mp3.text: Among the daityas I am Prahlada; among calculators I am Time. Among beasts I am the lion, and among birds I am Garuda. Listen to the first name Krishna gives here, Prahlada. He is the daitya prince whose devotion outshone his demon father, and Krishna says he is that very devotion among the demons. Krishna then names Time, the lion, and Garuda, showing that absolute power and speed are also his.

en/10-30-intro-31d57f00.mp3.text: Krishna has been naming his presence in the world, and now he moves from the cosmic to the personal. Hear how he claims to be Prahlada.

en/10-31-body-e5c9deec.mp3.text: Among purifiers, I am the wind. Among wielders of weapons, I am Rama. Among aquatic beings, I am the crocodile. Among flowing rivers, I am the Ganga. Listen to the crocodile. It is the fiercest creature of the water, and Krishna places it among the aquatic beings, showing his presence in the most fearsome form of the wild. Krishna now claims the beginning, the middle, and the end of all creation, and the knowledge of the true self. Listen to how he names his own limits.

en/10-31-intro-f6a73ac0.mp3.text: Krishna carries on by naming the supreme of each class. Listen to the four figures he claims as his own.

en/10-32-body-0498a67b.mp3.text: I am the beginning, the middle, and the end of all creation, Arjuna. Among all forms of knowledge, I am the knowledge of the true self; among speakers, I am the reasoned debate that seeks truth. Krishna says he is the knowledge of the true self among all sciences, and the reasoned debate among speakers. He places the inner truth and the spoken argument on equal ground. He now moves from knowledge to the very letters and time that build it.

en/10-32-intro-a57a95ef.mp3.text: Krishna has just listed many visible forms of his power. Now he names the invisible forces that hold knowledge and argument together. Listen for how he places them.

en/10-33-body-c2826f63.mp3.text: Among letters I am the letter A. Among compounds I am the dual compound. I am endless time itself, and I am the all-facing sustainer. The word ahameva, I indeed, stands alone. It is the first syllable of the word akshara, the imperishable. Here, the speaker claims to be the very first letter of the alphabet and the endless time that follows. Krishna moves from the grammar of language to the grammar of life, naming the women who shape human destiny.

en/10-33-intro-1f49c824.mp3.text: Krishna shifts from forms of knowledge to the grammar of the universe. Listen for the first letter and the first compound.

en/10-34-body-503d5634.mp3.text: I am death that takes everything, and the source of all future beings. Among women, I am fame, fortune, speech, memory, intelligence, steadfastness, and forgiveness. The word mrityuh, death, is paired with sarvaharah, all-taking. Together they describe the force that ends every life, and the word udbhava, origin, names the force that starts all future beings. Krishna now moves to the qualities that make human life dignified, naming seven virtues among women.

en/10-34-intro-1589ec91.mp3.text: Krishna has named cosmic powers, letters, and time. Now he names the forces that shape human life itself. Listen for the two words that mark the end and the start of all beings.

en/10-35-body-5678e3c9.mp3.text: Among hymns I am the Brihat-Sama; among meters I am Gayatri. Among months I am Margashirsha; among seasons I am spring. Krishna sits inside the calendar itself. He is the Gayatri among meters, the month of Margashirsha among months, and spring among seasons. Nothing is outside him. Krishna then names his presence in the midst of those who deceive, showing he is found even in human cunning.

en/10-35-intro-ffbfa063.mp3.text: Krishna continues to show Arjuna where he is found, moving from human qualities to the very order of time itself. Listen for the sacred sounds and the turning of the seasons.

en/10-36-body-0801f6ff.mp3.text: Among deceivers I am gambling, among the vigorous I am splendor. I am victory, I am resolve, and I am the goodness of the good. The word dutyam, gambling, belongs to the deceivers, yet Krishna claims it as his own form. Victory, resolve, and noble character are all his expressions. He then names Vasudeva among the Vrishnis and Dhananjaya among the Pandavas.

en/10-36-intro-e999eea5.mp3.text: Krishna keeps naming where divine power appears, even in the ordinary. Listen for the surprising place he places himself.

en/10-37-body-bc4e50ce.mp3.text: Among the Vrishnis I am Vasudeva; among the Pandavas I am Dhananjaya. Among sages I am Vyasa, and among poets I am Ushana, the poet. Krishna names himself as the greatest among the Vrishnis, the Pandavas, the sages, and the poets. He places his own divine presence at the heart of human excellence, from the mightiest warrior to the wisest sage. Krishna continues naming his presence among enforcers, seekers, and secrets.

en/10-37-intro-5b52f157.mp3.text: Krishna lists the greatest among the Vrishnis, the Pandavas, the sages, and the poets. Listen to how he places his presence at the heart of human excellence.

en/10-38-body-26955499.mp3.text: Among enforcers, I am punishment; among those seeking victory, I am policy. Among secrets, I am silence; among the wise, I am knowledge. Krishna claims four forms of his presence: corrective force, strategic conduct, silence, and the knowledge of the wise. He then moves from governing to creation, declaring he is the seed of all beings.

en/10-38-intro-9e8368a4.mp3.text: Krishna lists the quiet tools of governing and the force behind them. Listen to how he places silence and knowledge alongside punishment and policy.

en/10-39-body-153dee6b.mp3.text: Arjuna, I am the seed of all beings. Without me, nothing moving or unmoving could exist. Krishna says he is the bija, the seed, of all beings. Without this seed, nothing that moves or stands still could exist. It is the foundation of all that is. He then says his forms are endless and what he has shared is only a small part of his divine presence.

en/10-39-intro-99bfd7c4.mp3.text: Krishna has just named his many forms and powers. Now he points to the single source behind all of them. Listen for the word he uses for that origin.

en/10-4-body-19d58bad.mp3.text: Understanding, wisdom, freedom from confusion, forgiveness, truth, self-restraint, calmness, pleasure, pain, coming into being, ceasing to be, fear, fearlessness, nonviolence, evenness, contentment, austerity, charity, fame, and disgrace arise from me alone. Krishna puts bhayam, fear, and abhayameva, fearlessness, in the same breath. He does not say that fearlessness is the end of fear; he says both are his. Next, Krishna says that nonviolence, honor, and dishonor all arise from him alone.

en/10-4-intro-45dbbfd7.mp3.text: In this verse, Krishna lists the conditions of human life. Listen for the two words that sit together at the end, bhayam and abhayameva.

en/10-40-body-6817e206.mp3.text: O scorcher of foes, my divine manifestations have no end. What I have described to you is only a brief summary of my vast manifestations. Krishna admits that his divine manifestations have no end, and the examples he just gave are only a brief summary. He now tells Arjuna to know that every splendid thing arises from a spark of his own radiance.

en/10-40-intro-17a6aa9a.mp3.text: Krishna has just finished listing many of his divine forms, and now he speaks directly to Arjuna about the limits of that list.

en/10-41-body-bca79c07.mp3.text: Whatever being or thing is endowed with splendour, beauty, or power, know that to have arisen from a spark of my radiance. Krishna tells Arjuna that every grand, strong, or glorious thing is only a portion of his radiance. He then steps back from the list and asks if Arjuna really needs to know every detail.

en/10-41-intro-59c0c2f2.mp3.text: Krishna has just said his manifestations are endless, yet now he pulls the point tight. Listen for the single source he names.

en/10-42-body-f46e14fb.mp3.text: Or, Arjuna, what is the need for all this detailed knowledge? I sustain this entire universe with a single fragment of myself. The word to notice is ekamsena, a single part. Krishna says that even one fragment of his presence is enough to sustain the whole universe. Arjuna accepts this truth and asks to see the universal form.

en/10-42-intro-96522ac2.mp3.text: Krishna has just shown Arjuna endless divine forms. Now he asks what use there is in knowing all of them. Listen to his answer.

en/10-5-body-8999f60a.mp3.text: Nonviolence, equanimity, contentment, austerity, charity, honor, and dishonor, all these different states of beings arise from Me alone. Krishna lists honor and dishonor side by side. Both are states of beings that arise from him alone. Krishna then says that even the great sages and Manus were born from his mind.

en/10-5-intro-7938f564.mp3.text: Krishna tells Arjuna that nonviolence, balance, contentment, discipline, generosity, honor, and dishonor all arise from him alone. Listen to how he frames these qualities.

en/10-6-body-8327504b.mp3.text: The seven great sages, the four ancient sages, and the fourteen Manus were born from my mind. The people of these worlds descend from them. The sages and Manus did not arrive as bodies from outside; they were born from his mind, and every person in the world descends through that single line of thought. Krishna then tells Arjuna that knowing this truth makes one stand firm in yoga without any doubt.

en/10-6-intro-b6ad2ecb.mp3.text: Krishna widens Arjuna’s sight from the battlefield to the source of all life. Listen for the origin he names here.

en/10-7-body-e5a14185.mp3.text: One who truly knows this glory and this yoga of mine becomes steadfast in yoga without doubt. Listen for the word tattvatah, knowing in truth. It is not mere learning, but a deep realization that makes the mind unshaken and removes all doubt. Krishna then adds that he is the source of all and that everything moves from him.

en/10-7-intro-0dae8965.mp3.text: Krishna has just listed the signs of his presence. Now he tells Arjuna what happens to someone who truly understands them.

en/10-8-body-40a01d08.mp3.text: I am the source of all; everything moves from me. Knowing this, the wise worship me with wholehearted devotion. Notice the word matatah, from me. Everything that exists, Krishna says, moves and proceeds from him. The wise, knowing this, worship me with wholehearted devotion.

en/10-8-intro-756a0c32.mp3.text: Krishna has shown his many forms. Now he says where they all come from. Listen to who moves and what the wise do.

en/10-9-body-7f7875aa.mp3.text: With minds fixed on Me and lives offered to Me, My devotees speak of Me to one another, and find continual joy in that shared devotion. The word is परस्परम्, meaning one another. Krishna says the devotees instruct and speak of him to one another, and it is that shared talk that gives them continual joy. Krishna then promises that to these devoted speakers, he gives the very discernment that leads them back to him.

en/10-9-body-93d36def.mp3.text: With minds fixed on Me and lives offered to Me, My devotees speak of Me to one another, and find continual joy in that shared devotion. Listen to paratahparam, meaning one another. The devotees speak of Krishna to each other, and that shared conversation is what makes them find continual joy. Krishna then offers the gift of discernment to those who are always devoted and worship him with love.

en/10-9-intro-63295752.mp3.text: Listen for one word that tells us exactly how these devotees keep their joy alive.

en/10-9-intro-cdd69309.mp3.text: Krishna points to one word that shows how his followers find their joy together, through shared talk. Listen for it.

en/11-1-body-0a4004f0.mp3.text: Arjuna says: By the gracious words you spoke for my benefit alone, my delusion has been dispelled. Arjuna says his delusion is gone because of the words Krishna spoke. The secret teaching was given for Arjuna alone, and with that, the confusion is simply gone. He asks to see the cosmic form of the Lord, having heard about the birth and death of all beings.

en/11-1-intro-90e55383.mp3.text: Arjuna is not asking a new question now, but answering the one Krishna just asked. Listen for the one thing he says has already cleared his mind.

en/11-10-body-cac8adf3.mp3.text: With many mouths and eyes, with countless wondrous forms, adorned with many divine ornaments and many uplifted divine weapons. Sanjaya begins a list, repeating the word many, or anek. The form is not a single body but a vast scene filled with countless faces, eyes, ornaments, and raised weapons. The vision continues with the form facing everywhere, wearing garlands and divine garments.

en/11-10-intro-98437b5e.mp3.text: Arjuna has just received divine sight. Listen to how Sanjaya begins to describe what he sees.

en/11-11-body-c0de1b5b.mp3.text: Wearing divine garlands and garments, anointed with divine fragrances, wondrous in every way, endless, and facing everywhere. The word is divya. It means divine, and it appears again and again: divine garlands, divine clothes, divine fragrance, divine ornaments, divine weapons. The vision is not merely grand; it is repeatedly set apart as otherworldly. Arjuna feels that even a thousand suns could not equal the light of this being.

en/11-11-intro-2593dadb.mp3.text: Listen for one word that repeats like a drumbeat in this verse, marking everything you see as coming from a source beyond this world.

en/11-12-body-8baf468e.mp3.text: If a thousand suns rose together in the sky, their light would still barely match that great being's radiance. Arjuna is not describing a man, but a radiance that dwarfs the sky. He says that even a thousand suns rising at once would barely equal the light of that one great being. He now looks inside that body and sees the whole universe gathered in one place.

en/11-12-body-dfdaf876.mp3.text: If a thousand suns rose together in the sky, their light would still barely match that great being's radiance. Listen to the word भवेत्, would be. Arjuna does not say the thousand suns are enough. He says they would barely be equal, and even that is a stretch for a form that is beyond all measure. In the very next verse, Arjuna sees the whole universe gathered inside that single body.

en/11-12-intro-26097716.mp3.text: Arjuna stares at the form that has swallowed the battlefield, and tries to name its light. Listen to how he measures the form against the sky itself.

en/11-12-intro-43e0dbc2.mp3.text: Arjuna is staring at a form that is too vast for the eye. Listen for the impossible comparison he uses to measure it.

en/11-13-body-6b4ac98b.mp3.text: There Arjuna saw the entire universe gathered in one place, divided in countless ways within the body of the Lord of the gods. The word ekastham means gathered in one place. In the body of the god of gods, Arjuna sees the entire universe, all of it, held together in a single spot. Overwhelmed by this, Arjuna bows his head to the divine and speaks with folded hands.

en/11-13-intro-58220c60.mp3.text: Carrying on from the blinding light, the vision now opens up, showing the whole world inside a single form.

en/11-14-body-f0247e5a.mp3.text: Then, overwhelmed with wonder, Arjuna’s hair stood on end. He bowed his head to the divine and spoke with folded hands. The verse says Arjuna was vismaya-avishtah, filled with wonder. His body reacts with hrishtha-roma, hair standing on end. He bows his head and speaks with folded hands. The body moves first, and only then does he find words. Arjuna now begins to speak, naming the gods he sees inside the Lord's cosmic form.

en/11-14-intro-e9882692.mp3.text: Arjuna has just seen the divine form. Now his body reacts before his mind finds words. Listen to what his body does.

en/11-15-body-0adcd80b.mp3.text: Arjuna says: O divine one, I see all the gods in your body, and all kinds of distinct beings, Brahma seated on the lotus, Shiva, all the sages, and all the radiant serpents. Arjuna sees the whole divine order inside Krishna's body: gods, beings of every kind, Brahma, Shiva, sages, and radiant serpents. He is looking at the structure of the cosmos. He then sees You with many arms, bellies, mouths, and eyes, everywhere without end. He sees no beginning, middle, or end of You, O Lord of all, O cosmic form.

en/11-15-intro-2aa6a986.mp3.text: Arjuna has just seen Krishna's cosmic form. Now he looks again and names exactly what is inside it.

en/11-16-body-b04a9d3e.mp3.text: I see You with many arms, bellies, mouths, and eyes, everywhere without end. I see no beginning, middle, or end of You, O Lord of all, O cosmic form. Notice the word ananta-rupam, endless-formed. Arjuna sees countless arms and faces, but the one thing that truly stops him is that this form has no beginning, middle, or end to be seen anywhere. Arjuna now asks how he can find a place to enter this endless, blazing form.

en/11-16-intro-b5a9cf2b.mp3.text: Listen for the word that marks a boundary breaking. This is the moment Arjuna realizes the form before him has no edges.

en/11-17-body-4c76ff16.mp3.text: I see you wearing a crown, holding a mace and discus, blazing everywhere, hard to behold, and immeasurable, like fire and the sun in brilliance. The word tejorashim means a mass of radiance. Arjuna does not just see a man; he sees a burning, armed, crowned being whose light is too much for the eyes to hold. Arjuna now names the very form he has just seen, calling Krishna the imperishable supreme reality.

en/11-17-intro-e39d1bbd.mp3.text: Arjuna has just seen the formless infinite, and now he sees the details of that same form. He sees weapons, a crown, and a light he cannot stare at.

en/11-18-body-75df2492.mp3.text: You are the imperishable supreme reality, the highest support of this world, the guardian of eternal dharma, and the eternal person. Arjuna calls him the guardian of eternal dharma. By placing this name on the terrifying form, Arjuna names what he sees as the source of all order. He goes on to name the form as the endless person with infinite arms and blazing mouths.

en/11-18-intro-921c6867.mp3.text: Carrying on from the blinding light, Arjuna now tries to name what he is seeing.

en/11-19-body-af5c94e1.mp3.text: I see you as beginningless, middleless, and endless; of infinite power, with infinite arms, with eyes like the moon and the sun, with mouths blazing like fire, and scorching this world with your own radiance. Listen to the word shasi-sury-netram, eyes of the moon and sun. He sees the same pair that mark day and night, now fixed in one face, showing the whole world contained in a single glance. Arjuna sees countless mouths blazing like fire, and the world burns in the light of his radiance. He speaks again.

en/11-19-intro-d1cae91d.mp3.text: Arjuna is staring at a form that breaks his ordinary sight. Listen for the first words that name what he sees.

en/11-2-body-f96b2cef.mp3.text: O lotus-eyed one, I have heard from You in detail about the arising and passing away of all beings, and also about Your imperishable majesty. Arjuna calls him Kamalapatraksha, lotus-eyed. This name points to the eyes. Arjuna has heard about the imperishable majesty, and is ready to see it. He asks to see the divine form, saying everything Krishna has said is true.

en/11-2-intro-a81f4db0.mp3.text: Arjuna stops arguing and tells Krishna what he has learned. Listen to the one name he uses for him.

en/11-20-body-c3fdd9ec.mp3.text: The space between heaven and earth and all directions are filled by You alone. Seeing Your wondrous and fierce form, the three worlds tremble, O great one. The word lokatrayam, the three worlds, literally means heaven, earth, and the space between. It shows the form is total, filling every place that exists. Arjuna now watches the beings inside that form react, some with fear and some with praise.

en/11-20-intro-456adf10.mp3.text: Arjuna keeps staring at the cosmic form. Listen for the word that shows this vision reaches every corner of existence.

en/11-21-body-47e1b58e.mp3.text: The hosts of the radiant beings enter into you. Some, frightened, join their palms and sing your names and qualities. Great seers and perfected beings praise you with abundant hymns, saying, “May all be well.” Some gods, called surasanghah, enter into Krishna's form. Others are frightened, fold their palms, and praise him, while great seers and perfected beings sing hymns saying, 'May all be well.' Arjuna now names the Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, and Maruts, all gazing in wonder at the cosmic form.

en/11-21-intro-6179e25f.mp3.text: Arjuna is looking at Krishna's cosmic form, and now he points to the gods themselves. Listen for how they react.

en/11-22-body-572e2644.mp3.text: The eleven Rudras, the twelve Adityas, the eight Vasus, the twelve Sadhyas, the Visvedevas, the two Ashvins, the forty-nine Maruts, the ancestors, and the hosts of Gandharvas, Yakshas, Asuras, and Siddhas all gaze at you in wonder. The word vispmitah means astonished. Even the highest beings, from Rudras to Asuras, are left staring in wonder at Krishna, unable to look away. Arjuna then admits that he himself is shaken by the many mouths and terrible fangs he sees in the vision.

en/11-22-intro-4e217d20.mp3.text: Arjuna is still staring at the cosmic form. Listen to every class of being he names, and notice who is looking and who is not.

en/11-23-body-b65d0342.mp3.text: O mighty-armed one, seeing your great form with many mouths and eyes, many arms, thighs, and feet, many bellies, and terrible fangs, all beings are shaken, and so am I. Arjuna does not hide his trembling. He says that all beings are shaken by the sight, and so is he. He names the many mouths, eyes, and terrible fangs to show why. Arjuna continues, saying he cannot find steadiness or peace, and asks to see Krishna's gentle form again.

en/11-23-intro-ac42d1b2.mp3.text: The sight is so vast it shakes everyone, including the warrior himself. Listen to how he admits his own fear.

en/11-24-body-7b69bd5c.mp3.text: O Vishnu, seeing you touching the sky, blazing with many colors, with mouths spread wide and bright, vast eyes, my inner being is shaken. I cannot find steadiness or peace. Arjuna calls out to Vishnu, the preserver of the cosmos. Yet the sky-touching blaze he sees does not bring him comfort. Instead, it takes away his steadiness and peace. He admits he cannot find peace, and then he asks for grace to steady himself again.

en/11-24-intro-9eee6be5.mp3.text: Arjuna asked to see the universe, but the sight has shaken his inner being. Listen for the word that names the power he thought would save him.

en/11-25-body-b0beb4fb.mp3.text: Seeing your flaming, terrible mouths with their fangs, I can no longer find directions or peace. Be gracious, Lord of the divine beings, dwelling place of the world. Arjuna names two things he has lost, direction and peace, before he asks for grace. He then names the warriors rushing into the mouths, crushed between the teeth.

en/11-25-intro-93a9da14.mp3.text: Arjuna stares into the cosmic form and loses his bearings. Listen to what he sees and what he asks for.

en/11-26-body-a89b372f.mp3.text: Bhishma, Drona, Karna, and all the sons of Dhritarashtra, along with the hosts of kings and our own chief warriors, are rushing into your fearful mouths. Some are seen caught between your teeth, with crushed heads. Notice one name, sutaputrah, the charioteer's son. It is Karna, and Arjuna places him among those already rushing into the mouths of the cosmic form. Arjuna sees the sons of Dhritarashtra and our own chief warriors all rushing into your mouths.

en/11-26-intro-b2d0ad91.mp3.text: Listen to one name that cuts through the ranks of heroes. See how Arjuna names the greatest fighters and places them inside a cosmic mouth.

en/11-27-body-60e9f827.mp3.text: Your blazing, terrible mouths swallow them in haste. Some are seen caught between your teeth, with crushed heads. Here Arjuna sees the great warriors getting caught between teeth. The heads are crushed. The war ends not with swords, but with bodies being swallowed. The next verse says these warriors rush into the mouths like rivers flowing to the sea.

en/11-27-intro-d0dd0ea8.mp3.text: Arjuna has been staring at the cosmic form, and now he sees the warriors he knows rushing toward certain destruction. Listen for the physical detail of how they enter.

en/11-28-body-f2c5d1ec.mp3.text: As many streams of water rush naturally toward the sea, so these great warriors of the world enter your blazing mouths. Rivers run to the sea without choosing, and Arjuna sees the great warriors entering Krishna's mouths the same way. As moths rush into a flame, so the people rush into your blazing mouths to their own destruction.

en/11-28-intro-f3edbae5.mp3.text: Listen to the image Arjuna uses to show the warriors' fate.

en/11-29-body-41c3127a.mp3.text: As moths rush with great speed into a blazing fire to their destruction, so these people rush with great speed into your mouths to their destruction. Notice the word patangah, moths, and the word jvalanam, fire. Like moths that rush to a flame and die, these people rush into your mouths for their own destruction. Krishna's mouths are devouring these warriors while also licking up all the worlds with fierce radiance.

en/11-29-intro-1c2015a3.mp3.text: Arjuna sees a terrifying sight: entire armies rushing into Krishna's cosmic mouths. Listen for the single image that captures their doom.

en/11-3-body-2ac15f96.mp3.text: O Supreme Person, everything you have said about yourself is true. Yet I wish to see your divine form. Arjuna believes every word Krishna said about himself, and still asks to see the divine form with his eyes. Arjuna asks Krishna to show that imperishable self if he thinks Arjuna can bear to see it.

en/11-3-intro-63e98981.mp3.text: Arjuna has heard Krishna's words, and now he asks for something beyond hearing. Listen for the shift from belief to sight.

en/11-30-body-886cb774.mp3.text: You lick up all the worlds from every side with your blazing mouths. Your fierce radiance fills the whole universe and burns it, O Vishnu. Arjuna calls the blazing mouths that devour everything from every side. The word he uses is lelihyase, you lick up, so the universe is not just being destroyed, it is being eaten like a meal. He asks who this fierce form is and begs to know the purpose of this vision.

en/11-30-intro-a907b6b7.mp3.text: Arjuna stands before the cosmic form, and his voice breaks as he describes what he sees. Listen to the word that makes the universe sound like food.

en/11-31-body-29441856.mp3.text: Tell me who You are in this fierce form. Salutations to You, best of the radiant beings; be gracious. I wish to know You, the primal one, for I do not understand Your purpose. Arjuna asks to know the primal source of this vision. He says he does not know your purpose, and in that admission he surrenders his last demand for control. Krishna answers by naming himself Time, the destroyer of worlds, and tells Arjuna that the enemy warriors will not survive.

en/11-31-intro-61a50046.mp3.text: Arjuna stops resisting. He bows to the cosmic terror and asks two plain questions: who are you in this form, and why? Listen for the second one.

en/11-32-body-b424e5c3.mp3.text: The Blessed Lord says: I am Time, the great destroyer of worlds, here to end all beings. Even without you, the warriors standing in the opposing ranks will not survive. Krishna names himself as Time, the great destroyer. He tells Arjuna that the warriors in the opposing ranks are already doomed, and will die even without Arjuna lifting a single weapon. Krishna commands Arjuna to rise, telling him the enemy is already slain and he is merely the instrument.

en/11-32-intro-5520709b.mp3.text: Arjuna has just trembled before the cosmic form and demanded to know who this fierce being is. Now Krishna answers from within that vision.

en/11-33-body-456df6d8.mp3.text: Therefore, rise and win fame. Conquer your enemies and enjoy a prosperous kingdom. They have already been slain by me; become only the instrument, Arjuna. Listen to the word nimittam, instrument. Krishna tells Arjuna that the enemies are already slain by him, so Arjuna must become merely the instrument, with no claim over the act or the result. Krishna lists the great warriors already slain by him, urging Arjuna to stand firm and fight.

en/11-33-intro-4e8c9d15.mp3.text: Krishna has shown Arjuna the cosmic form, and now he turns the vision into action. Listen to how he redefines the battle as a mere formality.

en/11-34-body-8b29b21d.mp3.text: Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, Karna, and the other great warriors have already been slain by Me. Do not falter; fight, and you will surely conquer your enemies in battle. Krishna names four of Arjuna's greatest teachers and rivals, Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, and Karna, and says they have already been slain by Him. He then commands Arjuna to stop trembling and simply be the instrument to finish them. Sanjaya hears Arjuna's choked voice as he folds his hands and bows to Krishna, terrified by what he has just seen.

en/11-34-intro-71227f9b.mp3.text: Arjuna has just seen the whole universe in one form. Now Krishna names the very warriors he fears, and tells him what to do.

en/11-35-body-024764fc.mp3.text: Sanjaya says: Hearing Krishna's words, Arjuna trembled, folded his hands, bowed again and again, and spoke to Krishna in a choked voice, filled with fear. The crowned warrior, Arjuna, who should be fighting, is reduced to trembling, folding his hands, and bowing again and again, unable to stand before the cosmic form. Arjuna now speaks, and his words begin by praising the very chanting that terrifies him.

en/11-35-intro-7703254f.mp3.text: Arjuna, the great warrior, has just seen the cosmic form. Listen to how he folds his hands and trembles before Krishna.

en/11-36-body-8cb420e0.mp3.text: Arjuna says: O Hrishikesha, by chanting Your names and glories, the whole world rejoices and becomes devoted. By that chanting, frightened beings flee in all directions, and all the perfected ones bow to You. This is only fitting. Listen to the word sthane, which means fittingly. Arjuna is not surprised that the perfected ones bow; he says it is only right and proper that they do so. Arjuna now asks why the perfected beings would not bow to Krishna, the greatest teacher.

en/11-36-intro-a4f1919f.mp3.text: Arjuna has stopped arguing and is overwhelmed. Listen to the single word he uses to describe why Krishna's glory makes the perfected ones bow.

en/11-37-body-5deb9c72.mp3.text: O great one, why would the perfected beings not bow to you, the greatest teacher, the first maker even of Brahma? Endless Lord of radiant beings, abode of the world, you are the imperishable, the real and the unreal, and beyond both. Arjuna asks why perfected beings would not bow to the first maker even of Brahma, and then names you as the imperishable, the real and the unreal, and what lies beyond both. He then calls you the knower and the knowable, the supreme refuge of the entire world.

en/11-37-intro-6920aa72.mp3.text: After seeing the cosmic form, Arjuna's fear turns to awe. He asks why perfected beings would not bow to the one who created even Brahma.

en/11-38-body-f7038074.mp3.text: You are the first divine presence, the ancient person, the supreme refuge of this universe. You are the knower, the knowable, and the highest abode. O infinite one, the whole world is pervaded by you. Arjuna calls him the ancient person, the supreme person, the knower, and the knowable, saying the whole world is pervaded by him. He sees Krishna as both the one who knows and the one who is known. He then names Krishna as the wind, fire, the moon, and the great ancestors, bowing again and again.

en/11-38-intro-f4d4e6a3.mp3.text: Carrying on from his praise of Krishna as the first maker, Arjuna now names the ancient person who is the highest refuge.

en/11-39-body-47f68cbc.mp3.text: You are air, Yama, fire, Varuna, the moon, Prajapati, and the great ancestor. I bow to you a thousand times, and again and again. The word pratapamahatvam in the next verse points to boundless power, but here Arjuna fixes his gaze on the great ancestor, the source of Brahma, showing that the creator and the destroyer are one. Arjuna bows to this boundless power from every direction, acknowledging that it is all around him.

en/11-39-intro-04fea327.mp3.text: After seeing the cosmic form, Arjuna names the forces of nature and bows again and again. Listen to how he addresses the Lord.

en/11-4-body-955b4546.mp3.text: If you think I can see that form, Lord, then show me your imperishable self, Master of yoga. Arjuna does not demand the vision; he says, if you think I can see it, then show me. He leaves the power to grant the vision entirely to Krishna, the master of yoga. Krishna answers by opening his vision to thousands of forms, divine and many-colored, visible to Arjuna alone.

en/11-4-intro-ae8cb410.mp3.text: Arjuna has asked to see the divine form, but now he faces a doubt. Listen to how he hands the choice over to the Master of yoga.

en/11-40-body-21c7f3e9.mp3.text: Salutations to you from the front, from behind, and from every side. You are endless power and immeasurable might; you pervade all and therefore are all.
