The word purastat means from the front, and prishthatah means from behind. By naming front and behind, Arjuna shows that no direction exists where Krishna is not. Arjuna now admits he has treated Krishna like an equal friend, and he asks forgiveness for his disrespect.

en/11-40-intro-afee4ce2.mp3.text: Arjuna has just seen the cosmic form, and his body bows to every side. Listen to how he names the directions.

en/11-41-body-24446742.mp3.text: Thinking of you as a friend, I addressed you carelessly: “O Krishna, O Yadava, O friend.” Not knowing your greatness, I spoke in negligence or affection. I ask forgiveness from your immeasurable form for every disrespect I showed in laughter, play, walking, sleeping, sitting, eating, alone or before companions and relatives. "O Krishna, O Yadava, O friend": Arjuna remembers calling him these names casually and now asks forgiveness. He now asks for forgiveness for every careless and disrespectful word he has ever spoken to you.

en/11-41-intro-78b18db7.mp3.text: Arjuna is overwhelmed, and he names the exact words he used to call his friend. Listen for how he asks for forgiveness.

en/11-42-body-842b8047.mp3.text: Whatever disrespect I showed you in jest, while walking, resting, sitting, eating, alone or before others, I ask your immeasurable forgiveness. Listen to the word ekah, alone. Arjuna asks for forgiveness for both private errors and public ones, showing he holds nothing back before the divine form. Arjuna now calls Krishna the supreme object of reverence, the greatest teacher, and the father of all beings.

en/11-42-intro-08ed210a.mp3.text: Arjuna has just seen the universal form and now confesses all his casual slights. Listen to how he names his own carelessness.

en/11-43-body-e9bf1d6b.mp3.text: You are the father of all moving and unmoving beings, the highest object of reverence, and the greatest teacher. In the three worlds, no one equals you, much less surpasses you. Arjuna names Krishna as the father, the greatest teacher, and the unmatched power. He states that in the three worlds, no one equals him, much less surpasses him. Arjuna bows, seeking to please the Lord of praise, and asks for forgiveness as a father forgives a son.

en/11-43-intro-ccdc8942.mp3.text: Arjuna apologizes for his familiar ways, then names the supreme source behind all existence. Listen to how he defines the Lord.

en/11-44-body-86557fd3.mp3.text: Therefore, bowing down my body, I seek to please You, the worthy Lord of praise. Like a father bearing a son’s fault, a friend bearing a friend’s, or a lover bearing a beloved’s, You should forgive what I have done. The word sakhya means of a friend, and Arjuna places his body down to plead. He asks Krishna to forgive him as a friend forgives a friend, as a father forgives a son, and as a lover forgives a beloved, revealing the deep personal bond Arjuna fears he has broken. Arjuna admits his mind is filled with fear, and he asks to see Krishna's gentle form once more.

en/11-44-intro-a19d3c92.mp3.text: Arjuna has just seen the universe inside Krishna's body and now begs for mercy. Listen for the three relationships he uses to ask for forgiveness.

en/11-45-body-7fbafcd5.mp3.text: I have never seen this form before. Seeing it, I am filled with joy, yet my mind is troubled by fear. Show me again your gentle divine form; be pleased, O Lord of lords, O dwelling of the world. Listen to how Arjuna names his two feelings. He is hrsito, delighted, yet his manah, mind, is pravyathita, disturbed. He does not choose between joy and fear; they arrive together. Arjuna asks to see Krishna's crowned form again, with mace and discus in his hands.

en/11-45-intro-e7010410.mp3.text: Arjuna stands before the cosmic form and asks Krishna to show him the gentle one again. Listen for the two feelings that rise in him.

en/11-46-body-912ef595.mp3.text: I want to see you again in your crowned form, with mace and discus in your hands. O Thousand-Armed One, O Universal Form, return to that four-armed shape. Listen to the pairing of sahastrabaho, the thousand-armed one, and chaturbhuja, the four-armed one. Arjuna is asking the infinite to shrink back into the shape he can hold in his mind and love. Krishna confirms that no one but Arjuna has ever seen this form, and he then begins to explain it.

en/11-46-intro-d2678556.mp3.text: Arjuna asks to see a shape he recognizes again. Listen to the contrast between the infinite and the familiar.

en/11-47-body-3a7f5033.mp3.text: Krishna says: O Arjuna, I have shown you this supreme, radiant, endless, original form through my grace. No one except you has seen it before. Krishna says he has shown this form to Arjuna through his own power and grace, and that no one else has ever seen it before. Krishna says this form cannot be seen by any ritual act in the human world, except by Arjuna.

en/11-47-intro-de508dd5.mp3.text: Arjuna has just asked to see Krishna’s familiar form again after the overwhelming cosmic vision. Krishna answers that the vision itself came by his grace and power, and that Arjuna has been given a sight no one else has received.

en/11-48-body-e306eff1.mp3.text: I cannot be seen in this form in the human world by study of the Vedas, sacrifice, charity, severe austerity, or ritual acts, except by you, Arjuna. Krishna lists study of the Vedas, sacrifice, charity, severe austerity, and ritual acts, then says this form is not seen by any of them except by you, Arjuna. Krishna then asks Arjuna to set aside his fear and look once more at his familiar form.

en/11-48-intro-c048a5c8.mp3.text: Krishna continues, naming every path to the divine and saying they fall short of this vision. Listen to the one exception.

en/11-49-body-2f3e983c.mp3.text: Do not be distressed or confused by this fierce form of mine. Free from fear and calm-minded, look again upon this very form of mine. Krishna tells Arjuna to drop distress and confusion, and to look again with a calm, pleased mind. Sanjaya describes Krishna returning to his gentle form, reassuring the frightened Arjuna.

en/11-49-intro-7110fea2.mp3.text: After the cosmic vision, Arjuna is shaken. Krishna now asks him to let go of fear and confusion.

en/11-5-body-8b69de1c.mp3.text: The Blessed Lord says: See, Partha, my forms in hundreds and thousands, diverse, divine, and of many colors and shapes. Krishna addresses him as Partha, son of Pritha, and tells him to see hundreds of thousands of divine forms. The word rupani, forms, shows this is not one body but a universe of shapes and colors. He then lists the Adityas, Vasus, and Rudras, showing Arjuna the gods themselves gathered in one vision.

en/11-5-intro-cd82c944.mp3.text: Krishna stands ready to reveal more than Arjuna ever asked for. Listen to what he asks him to look at.

en/11-50-body-735c1dd4.mp3.text: Sanjaya says: After speaking thus to Arjuna, Vasudeva revealed his own form again. The great one then reassured the frightened Arjuna, taking once more a gentle form. Krishna, the great one, returns to a gentle form, saumya-vapuh, and reassures the frightened Arjuna. The terror ends not with a command, but with mercy. Arjuna tells Krishna that seeing this gentle form has restored his calm and his natural state.

en/11-50-intro-f6ce8a9b.mp3.text: Arjuna has just seen the terrifying cosmic form and trembles. Listen to how Krishna answers his fear.

en/11-51-body-65b2c9c7.mp3.text: Arjuna says: Seeing your gentle human form, Janardana, I am calm again and restored to my natural state. Listen to the word samyavrittah, restored. After the cosmic terror, Arjuna says he is restored and returned to his natural state. Krishna says the gentle form is easy, but the cosmic one is hard to behold, and even the radiant beings long for it.

en/11-51-intro-11221f84.mp3.text: After the cosmic terror, Krishna returns to his gentle human form. Listen for the word that shows Arjuna is back to himself.

en/11-52-body-543694a4.mp3.text: Krishna says: The form you have seen is very hard to behold. Even the radiant beings long forever to see it. The most telling thing is that even the radiant beings always long to see this form. The vision Arjuna has just been given is rarer than anything even the divine beings can behold. Krishna then says that this form cannot be seen through the Vedas, austerity, charity, or sacrifice.

en/11-52-intro-40fdb64b.mp3.text: Arjuna has just been steadied by Krishna's human form after being overwhelmed by the cosmic vision. Now Krishna explains what Arjuna has just been allowed to see.

en/11-53-body-f4e484c9.mp3.text: I cannot be seen in this form through the Vedas, austerity, charity, or sacrifice, as you have seen me. Krishna lists four standard ways to the divine, Vedas, austerity, charity, and sacrifice, and says none of them can produce the sight Arjuna has just had. He then tells Arjuna that only undivided devotion can truly reveal him.

en/11-53-intro-455f104b.mp3.text: Krishna now turns to what cannot be done. Listen for the four paths he sets aside.

en/11-54-body-e5b33d61.mp3.text: But only through undivided devotion can I be truly known, seen, and entered, Arjuna. Krishna says that knowing, seeing, and entering him is possible, shakya, but only through ananyaya, undivided devotion. Ordinary effort and ritual cannot do this. Krishna now lists the qualities of the devotee who comes to him, free from attachment and enmity.

en/11-54-intro-d5b15c93.mp3.text: After showing his cosmic form, Krishna now names the one path that can reach him. Listen for the exact word he uses.

en/11-55-body-9990a5cd.mp3.text: O Pandava, the devotee who works for Me alone, takes Me as the highest goal, is devoted to Me, is free from attachment, and bears no enmity toward any being, comes to Me. The word sarvabhuteshu means toward all beings, and it closes the door on any hostility. The devotee must bear no enmity toward any being, and that is the price of reaching Me. Arjuna now asks a practical question about which of these two paths is better for most people.

en/11-55-intro-69bd66a1.mp3.text: Krishna finishes the description of the true devotee by naming four qualities that must be present together. Listen to how they fit.

en/11-6-body-39a781f4.mp3.text: See the twelve Adityas, the eight Vasus, the eleven Rudras, the two Ashvins, and the forty-nine Maruts. See many wonders never seen before, O Bharata. Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, Ashvins and Maruts appear inside Krishna, wonders Arjuna has never seen before. Krishna now tells Arjuna to look at the whole universe gathered in one place in his body.

en/11-6-intro-0b272d83.mp3.text: Listen for the names of the deities Krishna points to inside his own form. Notice the exact list he gives.

en/11-7-body-58b04254.mp3.text: Behold the entire universe, with all that moves and does not move, gathered here in one place in My body. See whatever else you wish to see as well. Krishna addresses Arjuna as Gudakesha, the conqueror of sleep. He commands him to see the entire moving and unmoving world placed in one spot inside His body, as if the universe were a single object. Krishna tells Arjuna he cannot see this with ordinary eyes and must be given divine sight instead.

en/11-7-intro-53fa687b.mp3.text: Krishna has just shown Arjuna the twelve Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, and Maruts. Now He tells Arjuna to look closer at His body.

en/11-8-body-f135573d.mp3.text: You cannot see me with these ordinary eyes. I give you divine sight, so you may behold my supreme power. Krishna tells Arjuna that he cannot see him with these only, own eyes, and because of that, he gives him divine sight to see his supreme power. Sanjaya now tells Dhritarashtra that Krishna revealed the supreme divine form to Arjuna.

en/11-8-intro-cb2c11ea.mp3.text: Arjuna asked to see the cosmic form, and Krishna showed him the universe gathered in his body. But ordinary sight is not enough.

en/11-9-body-f002d4d4.mp3.text: Sanjaya says: Having spoken thus, O King, the great lord of yoga, Hari, revealed to Arjuna the supreme divine form. Sanjaya tells Dhritarashtra that the great lord of yoga, Hari, reveals to Partha the supreme divine form, the very cosmic reality Arjuna asked to see. Sanjaya then describes the many mouths, eyes, and divine weapons on this form.

en/11-9-intro-537344af.mp3.text: After Krishna grants Arjuna divine sight to see beyond the physical, what does Arjuna witness? Listen to Sanjaya's account of the revelation.

en/12-1-body-33a723d9.mp3.text: Arjuna says: Those devotees who worship You with constant devotion, and those who worship the imperishable, unmanifest reality, who among them are the most accomplished in yoga? Arjuna asks who are the best yogis: those who worship Krishna personally, or those who worship the unmanifest, formless absolute. Krishna answers that those who worship him with unwavering devotion and supreme trust are the highest yogis.

en/12-1-intro-38d40581.mp3.text: Krishna has just shown Arjuna his universal form. Now, before the war resumes, Arjuna asks a sharp question about the two paths of worship.

en/12-10-body-d50d9446.mp3.text: If you are unable even to practice, then be devoted to working for Me. By doing actions for My sake, you will attain perfection. Listen for madartham, for My sake. Krishna does not ask Arjuna to stop working or to meditate perfectly. He asks him to keep doing actions, but to do them for Krishna's sake. The work itself becomes the offering, and the offering itself becomes the path to perfection. If even this is too much, Krishna says, then simply renounce the fruits of your actions.

en/12-10-intro-a4b6810b.mp3.text: Listen for one word that changes the nature of any action. Krishna lowers the bar for Arjuna again.

en/12-11-body-dd94b778.mp3.text: If you still cannot do even this while taking refuge in my yoga, then, self-controlled, renounce all fruits of action. The word yata-atman means a controlled self, and Krishna tells Arjuna to do exactly that: keep the mind steady and renounce the fruit of action. Krishna then says that knowledge is better than practice, leading to the next verse.

en/12-11-intro-aab3088f.mp3.text: Krishna has already offered the path of devotion and steady practice. Now he offers one last, simpler way. Listen to the final step down.

en/12-12-body-a146d8b4.mp3.text: Knowledge is better than practice; meditation is better than knowledge. Renouncing the fruits of action is better than meditation, and peace follows at once from renunciation. The verse moves from meditation to a higher step, karma-phala-tyaga, renouncing the fruits of action. This letting go of personal reward is the exact moment peace arrives. Krishna now describes the person who has reached this state, one free from ego and equal in pleasure and pain.

en/12-12-intro-cfbd7619.mp3.text: Krishna continues by ranking the steps of the path, showing where the real release begins.

en/12-13-body-c7ab32d9.mp3.text: One who hates no being, is friendly and compassionate, free from possessiveness and ego, equal in pleasure and pain, and forgiving. Krishna pairs two absences: without possessiveness and without ego. The devotee does not cling to possessions and does not claim the self, which leaves no room for inner conflict. Krishna then adds that this devotee remains equal in pain and pleasure, steady through all conditions.

en/12-13-intro-9c017bbd.mp3.text: Krishna outlines the traits of a devotee who is dear to him. Listen for how he describes the absence of inner conflict.

en/12-14-body-7d5f599d.mp3.text: The devoted yogi is always content, self-controlled, and steady in resolve. One whose mind and discerning mind are offered to Me is dear to Me. The verse ends with a direct statement: the devotee whose mind and intellect are offered to Me is dear to Me. The reward for all this self-control and resolve is simply being dear to Him. Krishna then adds another trait, that of one who is free from envy and fear.

en/12-14-intro-409522de.mp3.text: Krishna describes the one who is dear to Him by listing his inner qualities. Listen for the one who is steady.

en/12-15-body-27c90806.mp3.text: The one who disturbs no one and is disturbed by no one, and who is free from delight, envy, fear, and agitation, is dear to me. The word udvijate means to agitate. Krishna says a devotee is free from both giving agitation and receiving it, and is also free from delight, resentment, envy, and fear. Krishna then adds that a devotee has no expectation, is pure, and has given up all undertakings.

en/12-15-intro-23f6e366.mp3.text: Krishna names four inner enemies a devotee must drop. Listen for the word that means to agitate or unsettle.

en/12-16-body-59986b90.mp3.text: One who has no expectation, is pure, skilled, detached, free from anxiety, and has given up all undertakings is dear to me, my devotee. The first word here is anapeksha, without expectation. It heads a list of a person who is pure, skilled, detached, and free from distress, and it reveals that the beloved devotee has no restless urge to launch new undertakings. Krishna then adds that the beloved one is free from attachment to both good and bad actions.

en/12-16-intro-b364c46d.mp3.text: Krishna continues his description of the devotee who is close to him. Listen for the quality that removes the urge to start anything new.

en/12-17-body-e393e4f7.mp3.text: One who neither rejoices, hates, grieves, nor craves, and who has given up attachment to both good and bad actions, is dear to me. The word bhakti, devotion, is named here as the mark of the person who has let go of both good and bad actions. Krishna now lists more pairs the devotee faces without reaction, starting with enemy and friend.

en/12-17-intro-18f30dd6.mp3.text: Krishna continues to describe the devotee who has given up clinging to both good and bad actions. Listen for the exact list of what this person no longer does.

en/12-18-body-b1be88ea.mp3.text: One who is equal to enemy and friend, honor and dishonor, heat and cold, pleasure and pain, and is free from attachment is dear to Me. The Sanskrit word samah, equal, appears twice in this verse. It marks the steady state Krishna asks of a devotee, someone who does not tilt toward friend or enemy, or toward comfort or pain. Krishna now names the outer signs of that steadiness in the next verse.

en/12-18-intro-4b8cc639.mp3.text: What does it take to remain steady when the world pushes and pulls on every side? Krishna names the pairs that usually throw a person off balance.

en/12-19-body-9015a84c.mp3.text: Equal in praise and blame, silent, content with whatever comes, homeless, steady-minded, the devoted person is dear to me. Krishna adds praise and blame to the list, and then silence, and then having no fixed home, aniketah. The devotee is steady-minded because he has stopped clinging to a place, a body, or to opinions. Krishna then turns to the devotees who trust him and live this nectar-like teaching.

en/12-19-intro-eef5d2d6.mp3.text: Krishna describes the inner life of a steady devotee. Listen for the details he adds to this portrait.

en/12-2-body-4fa7f52c.mp3.text: Those who focus their mind on me, worship me with unwavering devotion, and are filled with supreme trust are, in my view, the highest yogis. Krishna calls those who fix their mind on Him with supreme trust the highest yogis, and He uses the word nityayuktah, always united, to show that steady focus is the mark of the best. Krishna then names those who worship the unmanifest, the eternal, and the imperishable, restraining the senses to reach Him alone.

en/12-2-intro-b851ca00.mp3.text: Krishna answers by naming the highest yogis, and He defines them by their steady focus and complete trust.

en/12-20-body-de5d23dd.mp3.text: Those devotees who trust, take refuge in Me, and faithfully live this nectar-like teaching are exceedingly dear to Me. The word is paryupasate, to diligently practice. It is not enough to trust or to hold Krishna as the highest aim; the devotee must actively live this nectar-like teaching, and that practice is what makes them exceedingly dear to him. Arjuna now asks to understand the teaching itself, beginning with the nature of the field and the knower of the field.

en/12-20-intro-0e15267c.mp3.text: Krishna is closing chapter 12 by naming the exact action that makes a devotee dear to him. Listen for the word that means to practice.

en/12-3-body-7217a69a.mp3.text: Those who worship the unchanging, the indefinable, the unmanifest, the all-pervading, the unthinkable, the unmoving, the eternal, the imperishable, restraining the senses, reach Me alone. Notice the word acintyam, unthinkable. The divine is not an object the mind can picture, and yet those who worship this unthinkable reality with controlled senses reach Krishna. Krishna then says that those who restrain the senses and remain even-minded and delight in the welfare of all beings reach him alone.

en/12-3-intro-812ff77a.mp3.text: This verse answers the question of who is the best devotee. Listen for the qualities Krishna gives to those who worship the formless.

en/12-4-body-ff8e26ab.mp3.text: Those who restrain the senses, remain even-minded everywhere, and delight in the welfare of all beings reach me alone. The key phrase here is sarvabhutahite ratah, delighting in the welfare of all beings. This means devotion is an active wish for the good of every living thing. Sanjaya says that for those who worship the unmanifest, the path is even harder and full of struggle.

en/12-4-intro-94d84180.mp3.text: Right before this verse, Krishna described the highest kind of worshipper. Now he turns to the shape of that worship.

en/12-5-body-d3577ab0.mp3.text: For those whose minds cling to the unmanifest, the struggle is greater. The unmanifest path is hard to reach for embodied beings. Krishna warns that minds set on the unmanifest face more struggle, since embodied people find that path hard. Krishna now turns to the easier path of single-pointed devotion to a personal form.

en/12-5-intro-5115688a.mp3.text: Listen closely to the word that tells us why the unmanifest path is so difficult, and why embodied beings find it hard.

en/12-6-body-1ca4d031.mp3.text: But those who surrender all actions to Me, take Me as their highest aim, and worship Me with single-pointed devotion, meditating on Me alone. After saying the unmanifest is hard, Krishna names a path where a devotee places every single action at his feet and holds him as the highest aim. Krishna then says he quickly lifts those who follow this path out of the ocean of mortal existence, O Partha.

en/12-6-intro-240b761c.mp3.text: Krishna has just said the unmanifest path is hard for those in a body. Now he names a different way, open to anyone.

en/12-7-body-3d5d7398.mp3.text: I quickly become the one who lifts those whose minds are fixed on me from the ocean of mortal existence, O Partha. The word nacirata means not after long. Krishna does not promise rescue after many lifetimes, but very soon for those who fix their minds on him. Krishna then tells Arjuna to fix his mind on him alone and live in him beyond doubt.

en/12-7-intro-2921d94c.mp3.text: Krishna answers the devotee's deepest fear of being trapped in endless mortality with a promise to rescue them. Listen for the speed of his rescue.

en/12-8-body-118e6e9c.mp3.text: Fix your mind on me alone. Place your discerning mind in me, and you will live in me beyond doubt. The word buddhi means the discerning mind, and Krishna asks Arjuna to fix both his ordinary mind and his discerning mind on him. Krishna offers a backup plan: if the mind cannot rest on him, Arjuna should seek him through the practice of yoga.

en/12-8-intro-b6ac2e30.mp3.text: Krishna has just promised to lift his devotees from the ocean of birth and death. Now he tells Arjuna the exact method to receive that rescue.

en/12-9-body-23cb82b9.mp3.text: If you cannot steadily fix your mind on me, then, Dhananjaya, seek me through practice yoga. Practice yoga, repeated practice, is Krishna's fallback if you cannot hold your mind on him. If even practice feels too hard, Krishna offers a final, gentler path to reach him.

en/12-9-intro-5254b9aa.mp3.text: Arjuna is still frozen, so Krishna offers a gentler rung if steady devotion feels too hard.

en/13-1-body-63428de5.mp3.text: Arjuna says: O Keshava, I wish to understand nature, the field, the knower of the field, wisdom, and what is to be known. The verse pairs the field and the knower of the field, and adds wisdom and what is to be known to Arjuna's list. Arjuna asks what is to be known. Krishna answers by calling the body the field and the knower of that field the field-knower.

en/13-1-intro-62c55459.mp3.text: Arjuna asks Krishna to explain nature, the field, the knower of the field, wisdom, and what is to be known.

en/13-10-body-562b82e8.mp3.text: Freedom from attachment to sons, wife, home, and the like; and constant evenness of mind in desired and undesired events. The word anabhisvanga, no clinging, is the key. It points not to hatred of family, but to the refusal to let sons, wife, or home hold the mind captive. Next, Krishna continues.

en/13-10-intro-750786f7.mp3.text: Krishna is still describing the field of knowledge. Listen for how he names the ordinary bonds that tie a person to the world.

en/13-11-body-ffa8aefe.mp3.text: Undivided devotion to me, a love that does not waver, delight in solitude, and no attraction to crowds. Unwavering devotion to Krishna, a taste for solitude, and no appetite for crowds go on his list of knowledge. Krishna then tells us that seeing this supreme reality is the mark of true understanding, and anything else is ignorance.

en/13-11-intro-30cf8440.mp3.text: Krishna continues his list of what it means to know the field and the knower of the field.

en/13-12-body-99c549da.mp3.text: Constant awareness of the inner reality, and seeing the supreme reality as the meaning of true understanding, this is called knowledge; whatever is contrary to this is ignorance. Krishna ends the list by saying knowledge is steady awareness of the inner reality and seeing the supreme reality everywhere; anything else is ignorance. Krishna now begins to tell what is to be known: the beginningless supreme reality beyond existence and nonexistence.

en/13-12-intro-6e04e4f8.mp3.text: Krishna has just listed the qualities of a true student. What exactly is the goal of all this discipline? Listen for the final definition.

en/13-13-body-531968e8.mp3.text: I will now tell you what is to be known. Knowing it, one attains freedom. It is beginningless supreme reality, beyond existence and nonexistence. The verse denies both terms, calling the supreme reality neither sat, existent, nor asat, nonexistent. It is the truth that stands beyond these two opposites. Krishna then describes how this reality pervades the world, having hands and feet everywhere.

en/13-13-intro-6efa32eb.mp3.text: Krishna now moves from the student to the knowledge itself, pointing to the beginningless reality that frees the knower.

en/13-14-body-dd477aee.mp3.text: The supreme reality has hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads, and faces everywhere, and ears everywhere. It pervades all things and stands within all things. Notice the word Sarvatah, everywhere. It appears three times, telling you that there is no place, no direction, and no being outside of this reality. Krishna then tells you that this same reality has no senses, yet it lights up every sense object.

en/13-14-intro-24a3e242.mp3.text: Listen closely to the body Krishna gives to the supreme reality: it has hands, feet, eyes, and ears everywhere.

en/13-15-body-13a7b208.mp3.text: The supreme reality has no senses, yet illumines every sense-object. It is detached, supports all beings, beyond the three qualities, and yet experiences the qualities. Notice how Krishna speaks of a reality that is devoid of all senses, yet shines through every object the senses touch, and is without qualities, yet the enjoyer of all qualities. Krishna then explains that this subtle reality is both near and far, inside and outside all beings.

en/13-15-intro-deec3102.mp3.text: Krishna has just described Brahman as having hands, feet, and eyes everywhere. Now He turns to a deeper mystery, speaking to Arjuna about a reality that is both here and beyond.

en/13-16-body-b4de4b1c.mp3.text: The supreme reality is inside and outside all beings, moving and unmoving. Because it is subtle, it cannot be known; it is far away and near at hand. Listen to the word bahi, outside, and antah, inside. It fills everything, yet because it is so subtle, it cannot be known, and it is far away and near at the same time. Krishna now says this undivided reality appears divided among all beings, and that it creates and devours them.

en/13-16-intro-5a1fe287.mp3.text: Krishna just said the supreme reality is beyond the senses, yet Krishna now says it is inside and outside all beings.

en/13-17-body-59989d64.mp3.text: Undivided among beings, it appears divided. Know it as the one who bears, devours, and creates all beings. The verse opens with a paradox: the reality is undivided, yet it appears divided among beings. It is one reality playing the roles of creator, sustainer, and destroyer of all. Krishna now tells us that this reality is the light of all lights, beyond all darkness.

en/13-17-intro-b94e55da.mp3.text: If the supreme reality is everywhere, how does it appear as many? This verse answers that exact question.

en/13-18-body-6a160fa2.mp3.text: It is the light of all lights, beyond darkness. It is knowledge, the knowable, reached through knowledge, and abiding in every heart. The word jnanagamyam means reached through knowledge, and here it is knowledge itself. The knower and the known are one and the same. Krishna then briefly summarizes the field, knowledge, and the knowable before telling his devotee about attaining his state.

en/13-18-intro-c16ef3ea.mp3.text: Krishna sets the scene by describing the ultimate reality as the source of all light.

en/13-19-body-8ce69f08.mp3.text: Thus, field, knowledge, and the knowable have been explained briefly. My devotee, understanding this, attains my state. The word is madbhavaya, to my state. Krishna says that a devotee who understands these three truths reaches his own state, the goal of the entire teaching. Krishna now asks to know Prakriti and Purusha as beginningless, and to see qualities arise from Prakriti.

en/13-19-intro-0ea449de.mp3.text: Krishna now gathers the three terms he has taught, field, knowledge, and the knowable. Listen for the one word that names the reward.

en/13-2-body-026b413e.mp3.text: The body is called the field, O Arjuna. Those who know it call the knower of the field the field-knower. Krishna names the body as the kshetra, the field. The one who knows this field is the kshetrajna, the knower of the field. Krishna now identifies Himself as the knower of the field in every body, Arjuna.

en/13-2-intro-8fbbd468.mp3.text: Krishna begins to answer Arjuna's question with a pair of terms. Listen to how he names the body and the one who knows it.

en/13-20-body-4936247b.mp3.text: Know both Prakriti and Purusha to be beginningless, and know the modifications and qualities to arise from Prakriti. Krishna names two beginningless realities, Prakriti and Purusha, and says that every modification and quality comes only from Prakriti, leaving the Purusha untouched. He now assigns Prakriti as the cause of the body and action, and the Purusha as the cause of feeling pleasure and pain.

en/13-20-intro-07d65212.mp3.text: Krishna has just finished describing the field and the knower. Now he tells Arjuna how to separate the silent witness from the changing world.

en/13-21-body-a734cd14.mp3.text: Nature is said to be the cause of the body, the senses, and action. The inner being is said to be the cause of experiencing pleasure and pain. Prakriti causes the body, senses and action, Krishna says, while Purusha is the cause of experiencing pleasure and pain. Krishna then explains that the inner being, situated in nature, experiences the qualities born of nature.

en/13-21-intro-58af778f.mp3.text: Krishna continues his explanation of the field and the knower of the field by separating the doer from the experiencer.

en/13-22-body-827aa944.mp3.text: The inner being, situated in nature, experiences the qualities born of nature. Attachment to those qualities causes birth in good and bad wombs. The inner being, Purusha, sits inside nature and tastes its qualities. That same attachment to these qualities becomes the cause of being born into good or bad bodies. Krishna then describes how this inner self relates to the body as the witness, the giver of consent, and the great lord.

en/13-22-intro-20f6c8c2.mp3.text: If nature creates the body, who is the one that actually experiences it? This verse answers that.

en/13-23-body-d0b64350.mp3.text: The inner self becomes the witness, consent-giver, supporter, enjoyer, and great lord through its relation with the body. Yet in its true nature, it is called the supreme self and remains beyond the body. The self seems to become five things, upadrashta, anumanta, bharta, bhokta, and maheshvara, yet in its true nature it is called the supreme self and remains beyond. Knowing this distinction between the self and the body frees one from rebirth.

en/13-23-intro-717eec9e.mp3.text: Krishna now lists the roles the inner self seems to play. Listen for the chain of identities it takes on.

en/13-24-body-8cd7c65a.mp3.text: Whoever thus knows the purusha and prakriti together with the qualities is not born again, even while living and acting in every way. The crucial word is veitti, knows. It is a clear knowing of the self, nature, and qualities. That knowing alone is what stops the cycle of rebirth. Krishna next names the three paths that lead a person to this knowing.

en/13-24-intro-f6a51308.mp3.text: Krishna points to the moment of seeing itself. Listen for the single word that tells you how a person can act fully in the world and still break the cycle of birth.

en/13-25-body-96deebec.mp3.text: Some realize the true self within through meditation on the self. Others through clear discernment and yoga, and still others through the yoga of action. Krishna names three kinds of people: some, others, and yet others. He shows that the self is not reached by a single path alone. He then adds that even those who do not know these paths can cross beyond death if they listen to the teaching.

en/13-25-intro-3deba08b.mp3.text: Krishna has just described how a person who truly knows the self and the body is freed from birth. Now he explains how that knowing happens.

en/13-26-body-86d11882.mp3.text: Others do not know these paths, but they worship by hearing from others. Even they cross beyond death if they listen with devotion. Krishna says even those who do not know the paths cross beyond death, because they listen with devotion to others who do. He now asks Arjuna to know the source of every moving and unmoving thing.

en/13-26-intro-6e5b2e7d.mp3.text: Not everyone can follow the hard paths of yoga directly, so Krishna speaks of a simpler way.

en/13-27-body-927b0f00.mp3.text: O best among the Bharatas, know that whatever comes into being, moving or unmoving, arises from the union of the field and the knower of the field. Listen again to one word, mamakah, my own. The Pandavas are his brother's sons, raised in his own house, and with that one word he splits the family into mine and theirs. Sanjaya answers with the king's own son, Duryodhana, looking across at the Pandava army.

en/13-27-intro-857e05ae.mp3.text: The Gita opens far from the fighting, in a palace, where a blind king waits for news. Listen to how he names the two armies.

en/13-28-body-34669880.mp3.text: One who sees the supreme being equally present in all beings, imperishable amid the perishing, truly sees. The word avinashyantam means imperishable, and Krishna sets it against vinashyatsu, the perishing. He says the supreme being is unperishing among the perishing, and the one who sees this truly sees. Seeing the divine equally everywhere, a person does not wound the true self by the true self, and reaches the highest state.

en/13-28-intro-ddefe5f0.mp3.text: Krishna shifts the lesson from the battlefield to the nature of reality, and asks Arjuna to look past the dying bodies to the one presence within them.

en/13-29-body-8ca944a4.mp3.text: Seeing the divine equally everywhere, a person does not wound the true self by the true self, and reaches the highest state. The key word is hinasati, hurts, which literally means to strike or wound. A person who sees the divine equally everywhere stops striking the true self by the true self, and therefore goes to the highest state. Krishna then explains that the true self is the non-doer, while all actions are performed by nature alone.

en/13-29-intro-b5d1186e.mp3.text: Listen for the word that makes the self stop wounding itself. Notice how Krishna connects seeing the divine with a person's final destination.

en/13-3-body-127067e9.mp3.text: Know Me as the knower in all fields, Arjuna. In my view, true knowledge is knowing the field and the knower of the field. He declares that true knowledge is not one thing but a pair, knowing the field and the knower of the field, and he places himself as the knower in every field. Now hear the field itself, its nature, its changes, and the knower of the field, in brief.

en/13-3-intro-7e51890c.mp3.text: Krishna shifts from the body as a field to the knower inside it. Listen to how he names the one who knows.

en/13-30-body-575fde75.mp3.text: One who sees all actions as being done only by nature, and sees the true self as the non-doer, sees rightly. The verse repeats the word pashyati, sees, to show that true vision is seeing two things at once: the body-mind acts through prakrti, while the atma remains akartaram, a non-doer. Next Krishna describes how this true vision grows into seeing all beings rooted in one source.

en/13-30-intro-5d67f542.mp3.text: Krishna is teaching Arjuna about the difference between the field and the knower of the field, and here he explains who really performs all actions.

en/13-31-body-f3eba202.mp3.text: When one sees all beings as rooted in one nature and all expansion arising from that source, one attains the supreme reality. The verse pairs two acts of seeing. First, you see the separate states of beings resting in one place, and then you see their expansion. Seeing both together is what carries you to the supreme reality. Krishna now names the supreme self, calling it beginningless, beyond the gunas, and beyond action.

en/13-31-intro-fa2e9526.mp3.text: Krishna carries on by showing how to see the whole picture instead of just the parts. Listen to the two acts of seeing in this verse.

en/13-32-body-ee75506a.mp3.text: O son of Kunti, this supreme self is beginningless, beyond the gunas, and imperishable. Though abiding in the body, it does not act and is not stained. The verse tells you this self is beginningless and beyond the gunas, and even while it lives in a body, it does not act and is not stained. Krishna explains that just as space is untouched by what happens within it, the self remains pure in every body.

en/13-32-intro-9de1a7af.mp3.text: Krishna has just described the source of all expansion. Now he asks you to look at the self that lives inside the body. What is its nature?

en/13-33-body-b76b81db.mp3.text: As all-pervading space is not tainted because of its subtlety, so the self, present in every body, is not tainted. Space is everywhere and stays untouched because it is subtle, and the self in every body is the same. The next verse brings in the sun, showing how the knower of the field lights up the whole field.

en/13-33-intro-4819e75a.mp3.text: Krishna explains the true self inside the body using the image of space. Listen to how he shows the self remains untouched.

en/13-34-body-702e4352.mp3.text: As one sun illuminates this whole world, so the knower of the field illuminates the whole field, O Bharata. Notice the verb prakashayati, illuminates. The knower of the field is not a passive witness; it actively illuminates the whole field, just as the sun lights the world. Krishna now turns to the eye of wisdom that allows us to distinguish between the field and the knower of the field.

en/13-34-intro-a3f237d0.mp3.text: Listen for the word that reveals who is doing the illuminating here.

en/13-35-body-a1059d6e.mp3.text: In this way, those who know the distinction between the field and the knower of the field with the eye of wisdom, and who know release from the source of nature, attain the supreme. Krishna pairs the eye of knowledge with release from nature. He says the supreme is reached by those who know the difference between the field and the knower and also know how to free themselves from material nature. Krishna says he will speak again of this highest knowledge, which sages have used to reach the supreme perfection.

en/13-35-intro-731c21ee.mp3.text: Krishna is teaching the final truth, that the knower and the known must be seen as different. Listen for the two things a person must know to reach the supreme.

en/13-4-body-8cd78d75.mp3.text: Listen to the field, its nature, its changes, its source, and the knower of the field, along with that knower's powers, in brief. Krishna lists four things about the field: its nature, its changes, its source, and the powers of the knower, showing that the field is a changing object. Sages and Vedic hymns have already explained this distinction between the field and the knower.

en/13-4-intro-c7632d28.mp3.text: Listen for the word kshetra, the field, as Krishna begins to describe it and the knower who stands within it.

en/13-5-body-84f9315b.mp3.text: This truth about the field and the knower has been sung in many ways by sages, in varied Vedic hymns, and in the reasoned, conclusive verses of the Brahma Sutras. The word gitam means sung, and Krishna says sages, hymns and Brahma Sutras have already sung this truth about the field. Krishna moves on to list the parts of the field, starting with the five great elements.

en/13-5-intro-fb9fc036.mp3.text: Krishna has just told Arjuna to listen to the field and the knower. Now he names the teachers who came before.

en/13-6-body-826e114c.mp3.text: The five great elements, ego, intellect, the unmanifest, the ten senses, the one mind, and the five sense-objects: this is the field in brief. Krishna lists the twenty-four elements, including the five great elements, the ego, the intellect, and the unmanifest, that constitute the field. Krishna then describes how desire, pain, and consciousness move through this field, bringing its changes to life.

en/13-6-intro-79684e55.mp3.text: Krishna continues listing the parts of the field, moving from the knower to the known. Listen to the twenty-four elements.

en/13-7-body-4e2b6756.mp3.text: Desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the body, consciousness, and steadiness: this field, together with its changes, is briefly described. Krishna lists desire and aversion right alongside pleasure and pain, showing the field is the body and the impulses that drive it. Next, Krishna continues.

en/13-7-intro-c9dd2d9f.mp3.text: Krishna has been listing the parts of the body and the mind. But what exactly counts as the field itself, and what does it include?

en/13-8-body-15f689cb.mp3.text: Absence of pride, absence of pretence, nonviolence, forgiveness, simplicity, service to the teacher, purity, steadiness, and self-control. The list opens with amanitvam, the absence of pride, and adamantvam, the absence of pretence. Knowledge begins not with seeing, but with emptying the self of arrogance and show. Krishna now turns to the inner eye, describing dispassion toward sense objects and the constant seeing of the fault in birth and death.

en/13-8-intro-4b1e80a5.mp3.text: Krishna finishes his list of what shapes the wise. The qualities are not about grand visions, but about daily conduct.

en/13-9-body-919a2c4d.mp3.text: Dispassion toward sense objects, absence of ego, and constant seeing of the fault in birth, death, old age, and disease. Notice how the word ahankara, ego, appears right beside the list of birth, death, old age, and disease, and how Krishna names the seeing of these faults as a repeated act. Krishna now moves to the next step, asking the listener to let go of attachment to people and places.

en/13-9-intro-7fe66c2e.mp3.text: Krishna names one inner obstacle to clear sight, and then asks the listener to notice how he describes the endless cycle of bodily decline.

en/14-1-body-f0f6c3a6.mp3.text: The Blessed Lord says: I will speak again of the highest knowledge, the best of all knowledge. Knowing this, all sages have reached the supreme perfection from here. Krishna calls this the paramah jnanam, the highest knowledge. He is not offering a new subject, but the final knowledge that ends all seeking, the very same knowledge that carried all the sages to perfection. He explains that those who take refuge in this knowledge attain his likeness, never to be born again at the next creation.

en/14-1-intro-218be689.mp3.text: Krishna has just described the field and the knower of the field, and now he promises a deeper truth. What is the one knowledge that frees everyone? Listen to how he introduces it.

en/14-10-body-43b9afba.mp3.text: Arjuna, when rajas and tamas are subdued, sattva rises. When sattva and tamas are subdued, rajas rises. When sattva and rajas are subdued, tamas rises. The gunas compete: one rises by pressing down the other two, so inner states keep changing. Krishna now shows how sattva makes itself known when it grows strong in the body.

en/14-10-intro-f718f820.mp3.text: Last we saw how each guna binds. Now listen to how they battle one another to take the lead.

en/14-11-body-9d8206b4.mp3.text: When light, clarity, and understanding arise in all the gates of this body, know that sattva has grown strong. Krishna does not point to an outside sign. He points to the body itself, to the gates, the senses and the mind, saying that when light arises inside them, you can know sattva is growing. Krishna then turns to the opposite sign, showing how rajas, activity, and desire arise when that same inner light is missing.

en/14-11-intro-53d1d7c2.mp3.text: Krishna has been describing the three qualities that bind us. Now he gives a clear sign. Listen for the moment when light arises inside the body's gates.

en/14-12-body-d022342d.mp3.text: O best of the Bharatas, when rajas grows, greed, activity, the beginning of actions, restlessness, and desire arise. Krishna lists the marks of rising rajas: greed, busy activity, fresh undertakings, restlessness and desire. Krishna then turns to tamas, the opposite darkness that brings delusion and inertia.

en/14-12-intro-453d04fb.mp3.text: Krishna turns from the calm of sattva to the restless force of rajas. Listen for the five signs of this growing energy.

en/14-13-body-ca321c7e.mp3.text: O descendant of Kuru, when tamas grows strong, darkness, inertia, negligence, and delusion arise. Krishna lists four things born from tamas: darkness, inertia, negligence, and delusion. They arrive in sequence as the quality of tamas increases and takes over. Sanjaya now describes what happens when sattva predominates at the time of death.

en/14-13-intro-7ca3473b.mp3.text: Krishna asks you to listen for the exact chain of events that follows when tamas grows.

en/14-14-body-a5d1af55.mp3.text: When sattva is predominant at death, the embodied being reaches the pure worlds of the wise. Listen for the word amalan, pure or stainless. The embodied one reaches the pure worlds where the wise dwell. Krishna then turns to rajas, the force of action, and shows how it shapes the next birth.

en/14-14-intro-de3f6270.mp3.text: Krishna explains the path that opens when clarity, sattva, is strongest at the moment of death. Listen for how he names the destination.

en/14-15-body-ed83bb5f.mp3.text: A being who dies in rajas is born among those attached to action. A being who dies in tamas is born among deluded forms. One word reveals the fate of restless desire, rajas. A being who dies in rajas is born among those attached to action, caught again in the very cycle of work that binds them. Krishna now explains that the result of rajasic action is suffering, while the result of tamasic action is ignorance and delusion.

en/14-15-intro-4f55aced.mp3.text: Krishna finishes the picture of the gunas by looking at the two lower paths. Listen to how the state of mind at death shapes the next birth.

en/14-16-body-4bb7a910.mp3.text: The result of wholesome action is pure and clear; the result of rajasic action is suffering; the result of tamasic action is ignorance and delusion. The word phalam, fruit, appears three times in this verse. Krishna uses it to show that every action, whether good, restless, or dark, yields a specific fruit that matches its nature. Krishna now lists the fruits that arise directly from each of the three gunas.

en/14-16-intro-31c47546.mp3.text: Why do some actions leave us clear and others leave us in pain? Listen to how Krishna judges the result of every action.

en/14-17-body-e1b50916.mp3.text: From sattva comes knowledge; from rajas, greed; from tamas, negligence, delusion, and ignorance. Each of the three gunas produces a specific inner result. Sattva gives birth to knowledge, while rajas gives birth to greed. Krishna then explains the direction of movement for those established in each of these three gunas.

en/14-17-intro-356fe5f3.mp3.text: Krishna continues his teaching on the three gunas. Listen for the inner result that each one produces.

en/14-18-body-f30a78cc.mp3.text: Those established in sattva go upward; those in rajas remain in the middle; those in the lowest movement of tamas go downward. Krishna maps the three gunas onto directions. Sattva, sattvastha, means those established in sattva, and they move upward. Rajas, rajasa, means those in rajas, and they remain in the middle. Tamas, tamasa, means those in tamas, and they go downward. Krishna then says that the seer who knows the one beyond the gunas reaches his own being.

en/14-18-intro-59eb8e05.mp3.text: Krishna offers a map of movement. Listen to how he pairs each guna with a direction.

en/14-19-body-a27bd624.mp3.text: When the seer understands that no doer exists apart from the three qualities, and knows the divine nature beyond them, that seer reaches my being. The verse names the seer who looks and sees clearly that there is no doer apart from the three qualities themselves. When that sight also reaches beyond the qualities into Krishna's own nature, the seer arrives at him. Krishna now goes on to say that the one who rises beyond these three qualities is freed from birth, death, and sorrow.

en/14-19-intro-d04a4fad.mp3.text: Krishna has just described how the three qualities pull the embodied soul up or down, and now he turns to the one who sees through them. Listen to what that clear sight reveals.

en/14-2-body-2eda1a5c.mp3.text: Having taken refuge in this knowledge, they attain my likeness. They are not born at creation, and they are not troubled at dissolution. The word upashritya means taking refuge, and it shows a deliberate choice to align with the divine. Those who make this choice share Krishna's likeness and are untouched by creation and dissolution. He calls his primal nature a womb, and says he places the seed in it, so that all beings are born.

en/14-2-intro-0412b52a.mp3.text: Krishna speaks of a knowledge that changes a person's relationship to time itself. Listen to how he describes the one who takes refuge in it.

en/14-20-body-626e3ada.mp3.text: The embodied one who rises beyond these three qualities, which arise from the body, is freed from birth, death, old age, and sorrow, and attains immortality. Here the word dehi, the embodied one, is the one who crosses beyond the qualities, and the reward is amritam, immortality, the freedom from birth, death, old age, and sorrow. Arjuna now asks, by what signs is a person known who has gone beyond these three qualities?

en/14-20-intro-138e8ff9.mp3.text: The embodied one who rises beyond these three qualities, which arise from the body, is freed from birth, death, old age, and sorrow, and attains immortality.

en/14-21-body-30074c49.mp3.text: Arjuna says: O Lord, by what signs is a person known who has gone beyond these three qualities? How does such a person behave, and how does one cross beyond the three qualities? Arjuna asks three things in one breath: how to recognise the one beyond the gunas, how they act, and how to cross beyond them. He wants a sign he can see and a path he can walk. Krishna answers with the signs of a person who does not hate or long for the gunas.

en/14-21-intro-a0abaee7.mp3.text: If the wise can escape the three gunas, how do we know them, and how do we do the same? Listen to Arjuna’s three practical questions.

en/14-22-body-b4cdef6c.mp3.text: Krishna says: O Arjuna, the one who has gone beyond the three gunas does not hate light, activity, or confusion when they appear, and does not long for them when they disappear. The word mohameva, delusion itself. Krishna places delusion on the same level as light and activity, showing that a steady mind meets confusion with the same calm as clarity. Krishna then describes the one who stands firm, knowing the gunas are only acting among themselves.

en/14-22-intro-eb59fe59.mp3.text: Arjuna asks for signs of a person beyond the gunas. Krishna answers with a test of even-mindedness, naming three states of mind.

en/14-23-body-5f1a20f2.mp3.text: One who remains like an indifferent witness, unmoved by the three qualities, stands firm and does not stir, knowing only that the qualities are acting among themselves. The word to catch is asina, seated. He does not say the wise man is active or fighting the gunas; he says the man sits, still and uninvolved, while the gunas move around him. Next, Krishna shows how this steady one treats gold and a clod of earth as exactly the same.

en/14-23-intro-b6a0fffc.mp3.text: Krishna points to a single posture to listen for in this verse, a way of sitting that shows the highest steadiness.

en/14-24-body-a5f1ca2f.mp3.text: The steady one remains equal in pleasure and pain, in a clod of earth, a stone, and gold; equal toward the liked and the disliked, toward praise and blame. The steady one, the dhirah, sees a clod of earth, a stone, and gold as identical. The same equal mind covers praise and blame, because gold is just another object to be treated with indifference. Sanjaya answers with the king's own son, Duryodhana, looking across at the Pandava army.

en/14-24-intro-028201c2.mp3.text: Krishna is showing Arjuna what a person who has gone beyond the three qualities looks like in everyday life. Listen for what they treat as exactly the same.

en/14-25-body-c62cf904.mp3.text: The steady one is equal in honor and dishonor, equal toward friend and foe, and has abandoned all undertakings. Such a person is called beyond the three gunas. The word sarvarambhaparityagi, one who has abandoned all beginnings of action, shows that the person beyond the gunas no longer starts deeds from personal craving, but lets go of the very root of action. Next, Krishna continues.

en/14-25-intro-96c580ce.mp3.text: Krishna carries on by naming the final pair of opposites that the steady one meets with the same evenness.

en/14-26-body-461fb2ae.mp3.text: Whoever serves Me with unwavering devotion transcends these qualities and becomes fit for union with the supreme reality. The word sevate simply means serves. It is a steady action of serving the supreme, and this serving directly causes one to cross over the qualities. Krishna then reveals that he himself is the very foundation of this highest reality and the eternal bliss it holds.

en/14-26-intro-74732c0c.mp3.text: What is the exact way to rise above the forces that bind human behavior? Listen closely to how devotion is described.

en/14-27-body-83e796fb.mp3.text: For I am the foundation of Brahman, of immortality, of the imperishable, of eternal dharma, and of unending bliss. The verse rests on one word, pratishtha, meaning foundation or support. Krishna is not merely a part of the world; he is the base upon which Brahman, immortality, and ultimate bliss all stand. Krishna now turns to the cosmic tree, with its roots above and its branches below. Listen to how he describes its shape.

en/14-27-intro-e48d821b.mp3.text: Krishna closes this chapter by naming the ground beneath everything. Listen for the word that holds up all of existence.

en/14-3-body-9109787a.mp3.text: O Bharata, my primal nature is the womb; I place the seed in it. From that, all beings are born. Yoni means womb, and it names the source from which every being comes. Krishna places the seed in that origin, and from there all life is born. He then names himself as the seed-giving father of every living form.

en/14-3-intro-0212f35b.mp3.text: Krishna points to the source of all beings. Listen to the word that names this origin.

en/14-4-body-4b7dd731.mp3.text: O son of Kunti, in all forms of birth, the material nature is the womb, and I am the seed-giving father. Listen to the pairing of father and mother, seed-giving father and womb. Krishna says that whatever body is born, he is the one who plants the seed. Krishna then explains how the three qualities of nature bind the inner self to the body.

en/14-4-intro-f5610df2.mp3.text: Krishna has just called material nature the womb. Now he tells Arjuna that he is the father who places the seed.

en/14-5-body-66ca1bc7.mp3.text: Arjuna, the three qualities of nature, sattva, rajas, and tamas, bind the imperishable inner being to the body. The word nibadhnanti means bind. The three qualities do not merely color life, they tie the deathless self to the body, so even sattva is a chain. Krishna now turns to sattva alone, showing that even purity and light keep the self tied to the body.

en/14-5-intro-478ef653.mp3.text: The previous verse spoke of the seed and the womb. Now Krishna names the forces born from that union.

en/14-6-body-76e5813a.mp3.text: Among those qualities, sattva, because it is pure and luminous and free from affliction, binds the embodied being through attachment to happiness and to knowledge, O sinless one. Even sattva, which is free from affliction, binds the embodied being through attachment to happiness and to knowledge, O sinless one. Krishna now turns to rajas, born of craving, and names the chain of action.

en/14-6-intro-bb0ceded.mp3.text: Krishna has named sattva as pure and bright. But why does he warn that this quality still binds? Listen to the two chains he names.

en/14-7-body-094dbfa7.mp3.text: Know rajas as passion-born, born of craving and attachment. It binds the embodied being through attachment to action, O son of Kunti. Krishna names rajas as born from craving and attachment, and he says that force binds the embodied being through attachment to action. Krishna goes on to name the third force, tamas, born of ignorance and sleep.

en/14-7-intro-623810c8.mp3.text: Krishna continues his lesson on the three forces. He now names the restless force that keeps a person tied to action.

en/14-8-body-f94c4146.mp3.text: Arjuna, know tamas to be born of ignorance and deluding all embodied beings. It binds them through heedlessness, laziness, and sleep. Listen to mohanam, deluding. It is not a physical weapon but a veil that clouds the mind of every embodied being, making the truth invisible to them. Krishna now names the three things that tamas uses to keep beings bound in darkness.

en/14-8-intro-4f60d008.mp3.text: Krishna points to the final quality, tamas, and asks you to hear the one word that describes its grip on every living being.

en/14-9-body-7edb18ed.mp3.text: Sattva binds through pleasure, rajas through action, and tamas, covering knowledge, binds through negligence. The Sanskrit word Sanajayati means binds, and it binds all three: Sattva through pleasure, Rajas through action, and Tamas through negligence. Krishna then explains how the three forces take turns rising when the other two are subdued.

en/14-9-intro-227a2d0c.mp3.text: Krishna is finishing his list of the three forces that shape the world. Listen to the one word that unites them.

en/15-1-body-7f8670f1.mp3.text: The Blessed Lord says: They speak of the imperishable banyan-like tree of the world, with roots above and branches below. The Vedas are its leaves. One who knows this tree knows the Vedas. The word ashvattha points to the world-tree, which has roots above and branches below. The Vedas are its leaves, meaning the deepest knowledge is not in the branches of worldly action but in the roots above. Krishna goes on to explain how this tree grows from the three qualities, tying every living being to the cycle of action and result.

en/15-1-intro-167eb815.mp3.text: Krishna shifts the battlefield into a cosmic vision, asking Arjuna to see the world as an upside-down tree. Hear how the Vedas are described as its leaves.

en/15-10-body-871f21f1.mp3.text: The deluded do not see the inner being departing, staying, or enjoying the world through the qualities. Those with the eye of understanding do see. Notice who is doing the looking and who is being looked at: the deluded look, but they do not see the self, while those with the eye of knowledge see it. Krishna now turns to the yogis who, with steady practice, are able to see this supreme reality abiding within themselves.

en/15-10-intro-d3a83dcb.mp3.text: Krishna now asks you to listen for two kinds of sight. One is ordinary sight, and the other is the eye of wisdom. Notice which one sees the truth.

en/15-11-body-654648ea.mp3.text: The striving yogis see this supreme reality abiding in themselves. The unrefined and thoughtless, even while striving, do not see it. Listen to the word yatinah, striving, repeated twice. The striving yogis see the supreme reality within, but the thoughtless and unrefined do not, even when they try. Krishna then speaks of the radiance in the sun, moon, and fire that belongs to Him alone.

en/15-11-intro-49e57c45.mp3.text: Krishna distinguishes between two kinds of people who try, showing that effort without inner refinement is not enough.

en/15-12-body-462268ac.mp3.text: The radiance in the sun, the moon, and the fire is Mine alone. Notice the word tejah, radiance, appearing three times. The light that shines in the sun, the moon, and fire is his alone. He then turns from the sky to the earth, sustaining all beings with his power.

en/15-12-intro-ed183fd9.mp3.text: Krishna moves from the unseen reality to the light that everyone can see.

en/15-13-body-87f0a2c9.mp3.text: Entering the earth, I sustain all beings with my power. Becoming the moon of life-giving essence, I nourish all plants. He enters the earth itself to support all living beings with his power, and he becomes the moon of life-giving essence to nourish all plants. He now turns from the moon and earth to the fire inside every living being.

en/15-13-intro-42918d7e.mp3.text: Krishna has just said the sun, moon, and fire are his alone. Now he explains how he actively sustains the earth and feeds every plant.

en/15-14-body-b60fbe09.mp3.text: I become the digestive fire within living beings, joined with the outgoing and incoming breaths, and digest the four kinds of food. The word prana-apana means the inward and outward breaths. Krishna says this fire that digests food is joined with the breath that keeps the body alive. He then says that memory and knowledge also come from him, moving from the body to the mind.

en/15-14-intro-f0831850.mp3.text: Krishna moves from nature to the body. He is the fire that digests food inside every living being, working through the breath.

en/15-15-body-41433671.mp3.text: I dwell in the hearts of all beings. Memory, knowledge, and removal of doubt come from Me. I am the one known through all the Vedas, the maker of Vedanta, and the knower of the Vedas. Krishna places himself in every heart, as the source of memory, knowledge and the clearing of doubt. Krishna now names the two kinds of beings that exist in this world.

en/15-15-intro-b27dc946.mp3.text: Listen closely for one specific power that Krishna says he gives to every being from inside their heart.

en/15-16-body-4d4842e0.mp3.text: In this world, there are two kinds of beings: the perishable and the imperishable. All embodied beings are perishable; the steadfast one is called imperishable. Krishna names two kinds of beings, ksharah and aksharah. Every body is ksharah, but the steady reality within it is aksharah, the imperishable. Krishna then speaks of the Supreme Self, who is beyond both these two.

en/15-16-intro-55539680.mp3.text: Krishna moves from the battlefield to the nature of all existence. Listen for the two kinds of beings He names.

en/15-17-body-df8b074c.mp3.text: The Supreme Self is beyond both the perishable and the imperishable. The imperishable ruler enters the three worlds and sustains them all. Sanjaya listens as Krishna names the Supreme Self, the imperishable ruler who enters and sustains all three worlds. Krishna now declares that He is beyond both the perishable and the imperishable, and is known as Purushottama.

en/15-17-intro-23752d7d.mp3.text: The previous verse spoke of the perishable and the imperishable. Now Krishna points to what stands beyond both.

en/15-18-body-dbe69813.mp3.text: I am beyond the perishable and even beyond the imperishable. Therefore, I am known in the world and in the Vedas as Purushottama, the Supreme Self. Listen to the word Purushottama. It means the highest among all persons, and he gives this name to himself because he is above both the changing world and the unchanging principle. This supreme knowledge is not for everyone; it is for the one who worships with a whole being.

en/15-18-intro-6aa508a0.mp3.text: After describing the perishable and the imperishable, Krishna now answers the deepest question by naming himself. Listen for the title he claims.

en/15-19-body-3cfaa6c3.mp3.text: Arjuna, the one who is free from confusion and knows Me as the Supreme Self, worships Me with all his being. Whoever knows Krishna as Purushottama, free of confusion, worships him with their whole being. Krishna then closes this section by declaring that knowing this secret teaching makes a person wise and completes all their duties.

en/15-19-intro-99b77ba5.mp3.text: Krishna has just finished describing the Supreme Self beyond all change. Now he tells Arjuna what happens when a person truly sees him.

en/15-2-body-6fdde5c6.mp3.text: Its branches spread below, above, and across. They are nourished by the three qualities, with sense-pleasures as their shoots. In the human world, action-bound roots extend everywhere, tying beings to results. The branches of this tree grow below and above, fed by the three qualities. Sense-pleasures act as shoots, while action-bound roots spread everywhere in the human world. Krishna now says that this tree has no true beginning, no end, and no fixed base.

en/15-2-intro-1aa53d64.mp3.text: Krishna now shows how this upside-down tree grows and feeds itself. Listen for the three qualities.

en/15-20-body-5febfbed.mp3.text: O sinless Arjuna, thus this most secret teaching has been spoken by Me. Knowing this, a person becomes wise and has accomplished all that must be done, O descendant of Bharata. The word guhyatamam, the most secret, marks the end of this chapter. It means this is not ordinary advice, but the final key Krishna places in Arjuna's hands. Krishna now begins to describe the qualities of the divine and the demonic natures.

en/15-20-intro-5df3d494.mp3.text: Krishna calls this the most secret teaching. Listen to how he says it changes a human life.

en/15-3-body-ef2bec46.mp3.text: Its form is not perceived here as it truly is: it has no beginning, no end, and no fixed base. Cut down this deeply rooted ashvattha tree with the strong sword of detachment. Krishna says the form of this world-tree is not perceived as it truly is, and it has no beginning or end. The tree is deeply rooted and must be cut with a strong sword of detachment. Krishna then says to seek that supreme state where one never returns to this cycle.

en/15-3-intro-59e0a570.mp3.text: How do you fight a world that has no beginning, no end, and no solid ground? Krishna answers this by naming the weapon and the enemy.

en/15-4-body-9131261b.mp3.text: Therefore one should seek that supreme state, reaching which one does not return again. I take refuge in that original Person from whom this ancient creation has spread forth. The verse names a state, padam, that once reached, stops all return. Krishna then grounds that promise in the original Person, declaring his own refuge in the source from which all of creation spreads. Krishna then lists the qualities of those who reach this imperishable state.

en/15-4-intro-600f817b.mp3.text: Krishna has just described the endless tree of change. Now he points beyond it.

en/15-5-body-ec793462.mp3.text: Free from pride and delusion, victorious over attachment, ever rooted in the true self, desireless, and beyond the opposites of pleasure and pain, the undeluded reach that imperishable state. Listen to dyvandvaih, from the pairs of opposites. Krishna names the two things that rule ordinary life, pleasure and pain, and says that reaching the highest state means stepping out of their grip. Krishna then says that the sun, moon, and fire do not illumine that place.

en/15-5-intro-b078bf8d.mp3.text: Listen for the pairs of opposites Krishna sets aside. One word names the very things that pull us back and forth.

en/15-6-body-c6a3d501.mp3.text: The sun, moon, and fire do not illumine that place. Having reached it, one does not return. That supreme abode is Mine. Three words stand out: sun, moon, and fire. These are the three sources of light in the world, and Krishna says they do not illumine that supreme abode. He then says that anyone who reaches that place does not return to the cycle of birth and death.

en/15-6-intro-25555aa2.mp3.text: Krishna has just described the highest reality beyond decay and return. Now he names that goal directly, telling Arjuna about a supreme abode beyond all ordinary light.

en/15-7-body-57a821d8.mp3.text: The embodied being in this world is my eternal part, yet it draws the mind and the five senses, which rest in nature. Krishna calls each living being his eternal part, yet the same being draws along the mind and five senses that belong to changing nature. Krishna then shows how this same being carries those senses into a new body, like wind carrying a scent.

en/15-7-intro-dee0cbf4.mp3.text: Krishna has just shown the supreme abode, a place of no return. Now he turns back to the living being still caught in the world, carrying the mind and senses.

en/15-8-body-fa507ec5.mp3.text: Just as the wind carries fragrance from its source, the embodied being carries the mind and senses into a new body. Krishna names one word that moves with the self: the mind. The embodied being leaves one body and enters another, carrying the mind and senses onward, just as wind carries scent from a source. Krishna then shows the inner being using the ears, eyes, skin, tongue, and nose to experience the world.

en/15-8-intro-2006253c.mp3.text: The Gita asks how a person moves from one life to the next. Listen for the exact image that explains what travels.

en/15-9-body-f1f70363.mp3.text: Taking hold of the mind, the inner being experiences objects through the ears, eyes, skin, tongue, and nose. The verse names five senses, yet it is the mind that takes hold. The senses are only the instruments, and the mind is the hand that reaches out to experience the world. Krishna now explains who is deluded about this process and who truly sees it.

en/15-9-intro-8411ea70.mp3.text: Krishna explains how the self moves through the world. Listen for the tool it uses to reach out to objects.

en/16-1-body-51a257a9.mp3.text: Fearlessness, purity of mind, steadfastness in the yoga of knowledge, generosity, self-control, sacrifice, study of the sacred texts, austerity, and straightforwardness. Notice how the list begins with abhayanam, fearlessness. After the despair of the battlefield, Krishna names this as the very foundation of a divine life. These divine gifts are followed by qualities like nonviolence, truthfulness, and freedom from anger.

en/16-1-intro-befcee9b.mp3.text: Krishna continues listing the divine qualities, the first of which is the strength to face the world without dread. Listen to how the list begins.

en/16-10-body-fa82fc12.mp3.text: Taking refuge in desires that can never be filled, filled with hypocrisy, pride, and intoxication, they wander under delusion, holding onto impure vows and false beliefs. Notice the word asat-grahan, false graspings, and asuchivrata, impure vows. A person living under delusion does not merely hold wrong views; they live by them as their daily conduct. Krishna then shows how these people believe that this world is all there is, with nothing beyond it.

en/16-10-intro-26ae8087.mp3.text: Krishna turns from false views to the habits that trap a person in delusion. Listen for how he names the inner state.

en/16-11-body-57a5da6f.mp3.text: They take refuge in endless worries that last until death, live only for acquiring and enjoying things, and decide that this is all there is. Here the word pralayantam, lasting until death, shows that their worry is not a passing mood but a permanent shelter. They decide that desire-enjoyment is the highest goal, and that this is all there is. Next Krishna shows how they bind themselves with hundreds of cords of hope to gather wealth unjustly.

en/16-11-intro-cbe0a2fa.mp3.text: Carrying on from the previous verse, Krishna now describes the restless inner state of those who live only for desire.

en/16-12-body-1c20357e.mp3.text: Bound by hundreds of cords of hope, driven by desire and anger, they strive to gather wealth unjustly for the enjoyment of desires. The verse names two forces that trap and drive them. Listen for the word baddha, bound, and for the pair kama and krodha, desire and anger, which push them to gather wealth unjustly. Krishna adds that they believe this is everything, and they will fight to keep what they have gained.

en/16-12-intro-12fcde8b.mp3.text: Why do people chase wealth so blindly? Krishna points to the trap that binds them, and the engine that pushes them forward.

en/16-13-body-1ddadbbd.mp3.text: This much I have gained today; I will get this desire fulfilled. This wealth is mine now, and more will be mine again. The speaker uses the word idam, this, three times, and the word me, of me, twice, claiming ownership over every object and every future gain. That same deluded mind then declares, I am the lord, I enjoy, and I am happy.

en/16-13-intro-0b8e248a.mp3.text: Here, Krishna shows the inner speech of a mind trapped in endless acquisition. Listen for the voice that claims ownership over the past, present, and future.

en/16-14-body-74196e01.mp3.text: That enemy has been slain by me, and I will slay the others too. I am the lord, I enjoy, I am accomplished, powerful, and happy. The word is aham, I. It repeats seven times in this single verse, each time a new claim of ownership: I am the lord, I enjoy, I am accomplished, I am the master of strength, I am happy. The text shows how this same delusion of I and mine leads to endless sacrifice and giving.

en/16-14-intro-99722af7.mp3.text: Listen closely to one word that keeps returning in this verse. It is the root of every claim made by the arrogant mind.

en/16-15-body-9461d636.mp3.text: We are rich, surrounded by many people. Who is equal to us? We will sacrifice, give, and enjoy. Deluded by ignorance, they think this way. The deluded mind is full of 'I'. It says, 'I am rich, I will sacrifice, I will give, I will rejoice.' It turns even charity and worship into proof of its own greatness. Krishna then says that such people, trapped by desires and confusion, fall into misery.

en/16-15-intro-0f215d53.mp3.text: Krishna has just described the mind of an enemy who claims to have already won. Now he shows how that same pride speaks, and what it plans to do with its wealth.

en/16-16-body-c6463f01.mp3.text: Deluded by many desires, trapped in the net of confusion, and deeply attached to pleasures, people fall into a lower realm of misery. Mohajaala, the net of delusion, is the trap itself. A mind caught in this net is not merely confused by many desires, but is also attached to those very pleasures, ensuring the fall into misery. Krishna then shows what happens when pride and wealth make people pretend to perform sacrifice.

en/16-16-intro-a61e706e.mp3.text: Krishna continues describing those who are not free. Listen for the trap that catches them.

en/16-17-body-aaad8cb8.mp3.text: Self-important, stubborn, drunk on wealth and praise, they perform ritual in name only, with pretence and without proper method. Listen to dambhena, pretence. They perform rituals in name only, without proper method, and with arrogance. The outer action remains, while the inner sincerity is missing. Those who act from ego and anger hate Me, who dwell in their bodies and in the bodies of others, and they find fault with My qualities.

en/16-17-intro-1dd5271d.mp3.text: If you see someone performing elaborate rituals, how do you know if the act is pure? Krishna names the warning signs hidden inside the act itself. Listen for the mask.

en/16-18-body-d3332274.mp3.text: Those who take refuge in ego, force, arrogance, desire, and anger hate Me, who dwell in their own bodies and in the bodies of others, and they find fault with My qualities. Krishna lists five inner habits, ego, force, arrogance, desire, and anger, and says those who take refuge in them hate Me, who dwell in their own bodies and in the bodies of others. He then warns that He casts these hateful people into demonic births again and again.

en/16-18-intro-770dd5f9.mp3.text: Krishna names the inner habits that make a person hostile to the divine presence within themselves and in others. Listen to how he connects them.

en/16-19-body-96797e54.mp3.text: I cast those hateful, cruel, and vile people again and again into demonic births. Krishna names himself as the one who casts the hateful and cruel down. He does not let them drift; he sends them again and again into demonic births as the consequence of their own actions. Those deluded beings born into shadowed births sink into a lower state and never reach the divine.

en/16-19-intro-9d031134.mp3.text: Krishna draws a line between a life of cruelty and a life of peace. Listen for the word that tells us what happens to those who choose cruelty.

en/16-2-body-78d2c25b.mp3.text: Nonviolence, truthfulness, freedom from anger, renunciation, inner calm, absence of slander, compassion for all beings, freedom from greed, gentleness, modesty, and absence of restlessness. Krishna lists ten virtues, and among them is apaisunam, the absence of slander. This quality protects others not through action but through the restraint of speech. Krishna continues with the qualities of splendor, forgiveness, and steadiness that mark a divine nature.

en/16-2-intro-518bfa05.mp3.text: Krishna has just named the qualities of a fearless soul. Now he lists the inner habits that make that courage possible. Listen for one quality that protects others from harm.
