en/7-16-body-1ebd312e.mp3.text: Four kinds of virtuous people worship Me, Arjuna: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise one, O best of the Bharatas. Krishna names four kinds, and the last one, the wise, is the highest. The distressed come for relief, the curious for answers, the wealthy for gain, and the wise for union. Krishna now crowns the wise devotee as the best, saying they are dear to him above all others.

en/7-16-body-6899fb4e.mp3.text: Four kinds of virtuous people worship Me, Arjuna: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise one, O best of the Bharatas. Krishna names four kinds of people, सुकृतिनः, those who have done good deeds. They come to him in pain, curiosity, desire, or wisdom, and all four are counted among the virtuous. Krishna then says that among these four, the wise one is the greatest.

en/7-16-intro-1d78512e.mp3.text: Krishna continues by naming four kinds of people who do not fall into that delusion. Listen to how they come to him.

en/7-16-intro-f35a5bf1.mp3.text: Krishna continues, naming the four kinds of virtuous people who still turn to him. Listen to the four reasons that bring them to his feet.

en/7-17-body-3ef8e1cd.mp3.text: Among those four, the wise devotee who is ever united and one-pointed is श्रेष्ठ. For I am exceedingly dear to the wise one, and the wise one is dear to me. Krishna singles out the wise devotee who is nityayukta, ever united and devoted to only him. He says this kind of love is mutual. Krishna goes further, saying this wise devotee is not only dear to him, but is his very self.

en/7-17-intro-ebcd6bf3.mp3.text: Krishna has just named four kinds of devotees. Now he answers which one he values most. Listen for the one he calls distinguished.

en/7-18-body-ae9c3dcf.mp3.text: All these are noble indeed, but the wise devotee is My very self. Established in yoga, that person is steadfast in Me as the unsurpassed goal. Krishna calls all four noble, then says the wise devotee is his very self, fixed on him alone as the highest goal. He adds that such a wise one is very rare, having come only after many births of seeking.

en/7-18-intro-7f90a283.mp3.text: Krishna has just praised four kinds of people who turn to him. Now he raises the highest one and reveals the secret of union.

en/7-19-body-0c0d2a8b.mp3.text: After many births, the wise one surrenders to Me, knowing that Vasudeva is everything. Such a great soul is very rare. Vasudeva is the name of the divine, and it means the one who dwells everywhere. The wise one who sees that Vasudeva is everything and surrenders is what Krishna calls rare. Krishna then explains that those whose understanding is clouded by desire turn to other radiant beings instead.

en/7-19-intro-43e45a4d.mp3.text: Krishna now says that the wise one who sees the divine everywhere and surrenders is very rare. Listen for that word.

en/7-2-body-0d693a8c.mp3.text: I will reveal to you knowledge together with direct realization in full. Knowing that, nothing more remains to be known here. Krishna pairs jnana with vijnana, knowledge joined to direct realization, and says he will speak it completely, so that after knowing it, nothing else remains to be known. He then says that among thousands, one may strive, and among them, one may know Him in truth.

en/7-2-intro-2e52901d.mp3.text: Krishna has asked Arjuna to fix his mind on Him. Now, He answers what that knowing actually is. Listen for the promise that ends all inquiry.

en/7-20-body-90e35052.mp3.text: Driven by desire, people whose understanding has been taken away turn to other radiant beings. They follow the rules of each, shaped by their own nature. Krishna names the root cause of the error: hrit-jnanah, those whose understanding is taken away by desire. It is not a lack of knowledge, but a theft of the mind. He then says that whatever form a devotee chooses, he makes that faith firm and lasting.

en/7-20-intro-2757422e.mp3.text: After describing the rare soul who surrenders to the supreme reality, Krishna now explains the opposite path. Listen to who takes refuge instead.

en/7-21-body-a4aeabb6.mp3.text: Whatever form a devotee wants to worship with faith, I make that faith firm in that very form. Notice the word विदधामि, I make firm. Krishna is not just watching the worship; he is the one who makes the devotee's faith in that chosen form unshaken. When that faith is set, the worshipper gets what they ask for, given by Krishna alone.

en/7-21-body-ea66c3cf.mp3.text: Whatever form a devotee wants to worship with faith, I make that faith firm in that very form. Whatever form a devotee worships with faith, Krishna says he himself makes that faith steady. That steady faith then leads the devotee to receive their desires, given by Krishna alone.

en/7-21-intro-0d70bfba.mp3.text: Krishna answers why people turn to different gods: he is the one who steadies the faith behind each form. Listen for the word that means making faith firm.

en/7-21-intro-b3508d40.mp3.text: Krishna carries on from the last verse by explaining that he personally strengthens the faith behind every form of worship.

en/7-22-body-27805cb1.mp3.text: Endowed with that faith, that person seeks that worship, and receives those desires, granted by Me alone. The word mayeva, by Me alone, means the deity is only the postman. The devotee asks the god for a boon, yet Krishna admits in this verse that he alone ordains every single one of those wishes. Krishna then draws a sharp line between the temporary rewards of these worshippers and the eternal reward of his own devotees.

en/7-22-intro-ddc4fb8a.mp3.text: A person worships a chosen god and gets a wish granted. Listen for who really hands over the reward.

en/7-23-body-55962a7b.mp3.text: But the reward gained by those of limited understanding is finite. Those who worship the radiant beings go to the radiant beings; my devotees come to me. Notice the word फलम्, fruit or result. Krishna says that for those of little wisdom, that fruit is finite, meaning their reward has a fixed limit. He then turns to those who worship the gods, explaining where they go and contrasting it with his own devotees.

en/7-23-body-a3904916.mp3.text: But the reward gained by those of limited understanding is finite. Those who worship the radiant beings go to the radiant beings; my devotees come to me. Krishna says those with limited understanding get limited rewards. Worshippers of the gods reach the gods. His devotees reach him. The unwise think I have taken a visible form from the unseen. They do not know my imperishable, supreme nature.

en/7-23-intro-688d2639.mp3.text: Krishna is drawing a clear line here. Listen to how he sorts the results of worship.

en/7-23-intro-bbb869fd.mp3.text: Krishna draws a line between limited worship and true devotion. Listen to how he measures the reward.

en/7-24-body-7d573bea.mp3.text: The unwise think I have taken a visible form from the unseen. They do not know my imperishable, supreme nature. The unwise think I have taken a visible form from the unseen. They do not know that avyakta, the unmanifest, is the source from which this visible form came. Krishna then explains that he is hidden from the deluded by yoga-maya, his divine illusion.

en/7-24-intro-92b067e4.mp3.text: Krishna asks you to listen for one word that describes the true source of his human form.

en/7-25-body-fb622c69.mp3.text: Veiled by yoga-maya, I am not visible to everyone. Deluded people do not recognize me as unborn and imperishable. The word yogamaya, yoga-maya, is the veil. It covers him so that the deluded, the confused, look and fail to see the immortal, unborn self. He then says he knows every being in all three times, past, present, and future. No one knows him.

en/7-25-intro-b5a5c2a8.mp3.text: Krishna explains why he is hidden from ordinary eyes even while standing right before everyone. Listen for the reason he gives.

en/7-26-body-25f8a309.mp3.text: Arjuna, I know all beings of the past, the present, and the future. No one knows me. Listen to the word vedah, I know. It is the first verb in the verse, and it carries the entire weight of the verse: Krishna knows every being, but no one knows him. O descendant of Bharata, all beings fall into delusion at birth, from the confusion born of desire and aversion, O scorcher of foes.

en/7-26-intro-194b40a3.mp3.text: Krishna has just said he is hidden from ordinary sight. Now he tells Arjuna what that hiding means.

en/7-27-body-00e92195.mp3.text: O descendant of Bharata, all beings fall into delusion at birth, from the confusion born of desire and aversion, O scorcher of foes. The verse names the exact source of delusion, ichchha-dvesha, desire and aversion. These two opposing pulls create duhkha, and from that confusion, all beings are thrown into repeated birth and death. Krishna now tells Arjuna what happens when that confusion is finally cleared away.

en/7-27-intro-d074f127.mp3.text: Krishna now explains exactly what keeps a soul trapped in the cycle of birth and death. Listen for the pair of forces behind it.

en/7-28-body-b89091f6.mp3.text: But those whose wrongdoing has been cleared away, and whose good deeds have matured, are freed from confusion and worship me with firm resolve. Listen to dvandvamohanirmuktah, freed from the confusion of opposites. In this verse, people who have cleared away their wrongdoing and ripened their good deeds are no longer pulled between pleasure and pain. Krishna then explains that these people, seeking release from old age and death, come to know Brahman and all action.

en/7-28-intro-f2cdadb2.mp3.text: Krishna speaks of the people who have moved past the confusion of opposites. Listen for the state they reach.

en/7-29-body-24fc984a.mp3.text: Those who, seeking release from old age and death, take refuge in me, come to know Brahman, the whole field of the inner life, and all action. Those who take refuge in Krishna to escape old age and death come to know Brahman, self, and action. Krishna then tells how those who know him at the moment of death see the whole world differently.

en/7-29-intro-519794f0.mp3.text: Krishna names the deepest human fear to show the path beyond it. Listen for the one who takes refuge in him.

en/7-3-body-c749db0e.mp3.text: Among thousands of people, one may strive for perfection; among those striving, one may know Me in truth. The word kashchit, some one, appears twice in this verse. It shows that one in thousands strives, and among those strivers, one knows Me in truth. He then moves from the rarity of knowing him to the very elements that make up his lower nature.

en/7-3-intro-16a2b038.mp3.text: Krishna does not promise that many will find him; he says the path is hard and the goal is rare.

en/7-30-body-88ac3f71.mp3.text: Those who know me together with the physical realm, the radiant powers, and the inner sacrifice know me even at the time of death. Listen to the end of the verse. Those with a disciplined mind know me even at the time of death. The verse shows that knowing Krishna in matter, in the gods, and in sacrifice leads to knowing him at death. The next chapter begins with Arjuna asking Krishna to define the terms he has just used.

en/7-30-intro-ecf998e3.mp3.text: Krishna has just explained the full structure of reality, and now he gives Arjuna a final key. Listen to how knowing him in three layers leads to reaching him at death.

en/7-4-body-3abea56d.mp3.text: Earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intellect, and ego: this is My eightfold lower nature. The word manas, mind, sits right between the five elements and the intellect. By placing mind among matter, Krishna shows that even our inner world belongs to the lower nature. Krishna then names the higher nature that sustains the world, beyond these eight parts.

en/7-4-intro-f8bebfbc.mp3.text: Krishna lists eight parts of creation. Listen for the word 'mind' and notice where it is placed in that list.

en/7-5-body-e836e30c.mp3.text: Know My higher nature, which is different from this lower nature, O mighty-armed one. By that living nature, this world is sustained. Krishna asks Arjuna to know his higher nature, jivabhutam, become living. The lower nature is matter and mind, but the higher nature is a living power that sustains the world. Krishna now declares that all beings spring from these two natures, and he is their source and end.

en/7-5-intro-66195971.mp3.text: Krishna has just listed the material world. Now he points past it. Listen for the living force that keeps everything together.

en/7-6-body-c35dbeec.mp3.text: Know that all beings are born from these two natures. I am the source and the dissolution of the entire universe. Krishna uses the word prabhavah, source, and pralayastatha, dissolution also. In one breath, he holds the beginning and the end of the universe as his own. Krishna now makes his claim absolute, saying nothing is higher than him in all the world.

en/7-6-intro-4aa69132.mp3.text: Krishna continues by explaining how every living thing is born, and then states his own position in all of it.

en/7-7-body-c3beff60.mp3.text: O Dhananjaya, nothing exists higher than Me. All this world is strung on Me like pearls on a thread. Notice the word protam, meaning strung. The entire world is not just near him, it is woven through him like beads on a thread, held in place only by that single line. Krishna then lists his form in the elements, the syllables, and the qualities of human beings.

en/7-7-intro-7743adb6.mp3.text: After explaining the two natures, Krishna now asks Arjuna to see the whole world in one image. Listen for the single word that holds the universe together.

en/7-8-body-f536dff8.mp3.text: O son of Kunti, I am the taste in water, the light in the moon and sun, the syllable Om in all the Vedas, the sound in space, and the valor in human beings. The first word, rasah, means taste in water, and Krishna claims it as his own. He is the flavor that makes water life-giving, right there in the water Arjuna drinks. Krishna then names the light in the moon and sun, the sound in space, and the strength in human beings.

en/7-8-intro-0f47b7ed.mp3.text: Krishna now speaks to Arjuna, showing how he is the very life in ordinary things. Listen for the first thing he names.

en/7-9-body-bf11e07a.mp3.text: I am the pure fragrance in the earth, the radiance in fire, the life in all beings, and the austerity in ascetics. Listen for tapah, austerity. It means the heat of discipline, the burning energy of those who fast, meditate, and restrain the body. Krishna says he is this heat in the very people who practice it. He then tells Arjuna to know him as the eternal seed of all beings.

en/7-9-intro-187597e1.mp3.text: Listen for one word that names a quality found in people who deny themselves. Notice how Krishna claims it as his own.

en/8-1-body-285e452b.mp3.text: Arjuna says: O Supreme Person, what is Brahman? What is the self? What is action? What is called the field of changing things, and what is called the divine principle? What is the sacred offering here in this body, and how are you known at the time of death by those with disciplined minds? Arjuna calls Krishna Purushottama, the Supreme Person, and fires off a string of five what questions. The Sanskrit repeats kim, what, five times, turning the verse into a single, urgent demand for definitions. Arjuna asks who the sacrifice is inside the body and how Krishna is known at the moment of death. This verse answers what Brahman and the other terms are.

en/8-1-intro-1de5eeef.mp3.text: Arjuna now asks Krishna to define the deepest terms behind life, death, and the imperishable reality. Listen to the five questions he fires off.

en/8-10-body-2acba7ff.mp3.text: At the time of departure, one who leaves the body with an unmoving mind, devotion, and the power of yoga, placing the life-force between the eyebrows, reaches the divine supreme person. Listen to the exact place, bhruvor madhye, between the eyebrows. This is where the life-force is drawn up, and from here the soul departs. He now names the imperishable state that the knowers of the Vedas call deathless.

en/8-10-intro-8bdf8b41.mp3.text: Krishna carries on from the supreme person's light, and now he asks what inner state carries a person to that same light at departure.

en/8-11-body-a31b514c.mp3.text: I will briefly tell you that imperishable state, which the knowers of the Vedas call imperishable, which the detached ascetics enter, and which seekers follow through celibate discipline. The verse repeats one word, aksharam, the imperishable. It is the same object that Vedic scholars name, detached ascetics enter, and celibate seekers pursue, binding all three paths to a single goal. Krishna then closes the senses and fixes the mind, giving the exact method to reach that imperishable state.

en/8-11-intro-a3851646.mp3.text: What is the imperishable state that sages seek and describe? Krishna promises to answer this question in one verse.

en/8-12-body-9df19323.mp3.text: Closing all the doors of the senses, holding the mind in the heart, and placing the life-force in the head, one remains fixed in yoga-discipline. Listen to the word murdhni, the head. Krishna directs the life-force to be placed there, making the head the seat of his final yoga-discipline. He adds that uttering Om and remembering Him is the final step that seals this departure.

en/8-12-intro-e137522a.mp3.text: Krishna shifts from the goal to the method of departure. He gives a precise sequence of three acts to master the body at death.

en/8-13-body-77315223.mp3.text: Uttering Om, the one-syllable Brahman, and remembering Me, one who departs while leaving the body attains the supreme state. The single syllable Om is called Brahman, the one-syllable absolute. It is not a mere sound, but the ultimate reality, and it is to be spoken while Krishna is remembered. Krishna then tells Arjuna that for one who constantly remembers him, he is easy to reach.

en/8-13-intro-2669a712.mp3.text: Listen for the sound that Krishna says is the one-syllable form of the absolute, and how it is joined to his own name at the final moment.

en/8-14-body-468e306b.mp3.text: Arjuna, for the one whose mind is wholly on me and who remembers me constantly, I am easy to reach. Krishna says he is easy to reach, sudhalam, for the yogi who is nitya-yuktasya, ever-joined, and whose mind is ananya-cetah, one-pointed, so that his remembrance is constant. He then says that great souls who reach him do not return to this cycle of birth.

en/8-14-intro-e1c6c177.mp3.text: After telling Arjuna how to leave the body, Krishna steps back to describe the living path of devotion. Listen for the condition that makes him easy to reach.

en/8-15-body-5fdb7715.mp3.text: Great souls who reach me do not return to this painful, temporary cycle of birth. The word dhuhalayama, abode of suffering, describes this world of rebirth, and the verse tells us that those who reach Krishna do not return to it. Krishna then speaks of all worlds returning to this same cycle, except for the one who reaches him.

en/8-15-intro-6abe0384.mp3.text: Krishna continues by naming the destination that lies beyond the cycle of birth, a place where suffering ends.

en/8-16-body-17afa6d0.mp3.text: All worlds up to Brahma's realm return again, Arjuna. But having reached me, O son of Kunti, there is no rebirth. The word punaravartinah means returning again. Krishna uses it to name the endless cycle of birth and death, and then he offers one permanent way out. He now explains the true length of Brahma's day and night to show why even cosmic time is temporary.

en/8-16-intro-d39b9e3d.mp3.text: Krishna names the highest heaven and says even that one sends beings back, yet there is one permanent way out.

en/8-17-body-4b45d672.mp3.text: Those who know that Brahma’s day lasts a thousand yugas, and his night lasts a thousand yugas, know day and night truly. The phrase ahah ratrividah literally means knowers of day and night. In this verse, the phrase ahah ratrividah refers to the people who know the true length of Brahma's day and night, which is defined by the term yugas. At the start of Brahma's day, all beings arise from the unmanifest, and at the start of Brahma's night, they dissolve back into that same unmanifest.

en/8-17-intro-4d08db56.mp3.text: Krishna describes the vast duration of Brahma's day and night. Listen for the word that measures this cosmic time.

en/8-18-body-54cf9785.mp3.text: At the start of Brahma's day, all beings arise from the unmanifest; at the start of Brahma's night, they dissolve back into that same unmanifest. The word is avyakta, the unmanifest. Beings arise from it and dissolve back into it, showing that this is the source of their appearance and disappearance. Krishna then says that this entire group of beings is born again and again, helplessly, at the coming of day.

en/8-18-intro-bc8d970b.mp3.text: Krishna describes a cycle of birth and dissolution. Listen for the word that names the source from which beings arise and into which they dissolve.

en/8-19-body-968ea8dd.mp3.text: O Arjuna, this entire group of beings is born again and again, and is dissolved at the coming of night; at the coming of day, it rises again, helplessly. The word avashah means helplessly, under compulsion. Every being is forced to arise and dissolve again and again. They have no choice in this cycle. Next, Krishna continues.

en/8-19-intro-ab143595.mp3.text: Krishna has just described the unmanifest and its cosmic rhythm. Now listen to what happens to all living beings caught inside that rhythm.

en/8-2-body-5850f847.mp3.text: Arjuna says: O Madhusudana, who is the sacrifice here, and how does he dwell in this body? And at the time of death, how are you known by those with disciplined minds? Arjuna asks about adhiyajna, the lord of sacrifice, and where that presence lives: inside the body. He wants to know how the self, the body, and the sacrifice fit together. Krishna answers that the imperishable is the supreme reality and one's own nature is the inner self.

en/8-2-intro-5893760d.mp3.text: Arjuna asks Krishna to name the inner ruler of sacrifice, and to explain how a disciplined mind knows him at the moment of death.

en/8-20-body-b3374839.mp3.text: Beyond that unmanifest is another, eternal unmanifest. Even when all beings perish, it does not perish. The verse holds two unmanifest states, and the word parastasmattu, beyond that, marks the shift from the temporary to the eternal. The unmanifest that dissolves gives way to the one that cannot be destroyed, even when all beings perish. Krishna calls this eternal unmanifest the highest goal and his supreme abode, from which there is no return.

en/8-20-intro-a2a68823.mp3.text: Krishna has traced the path of every living form from birth to dissolution, and now he points to what remains when all forms vanish. Listen to how he names the imperishable.

en/8-21-body-54891a3c.mp3.text: That is called the unmanifest and the imperishable. It is the highest goal. Having reached it, one does not return. It is my supreme abode. The word अक्षर means imperishable. Krishna names this imperishable state as his own supreme abode, the highest goal where souls do not return after reaching it. Krishna then tells Arjuna that this supreme person is reached through undivided devotion.

en/8-21-body-70daccbb.mp3.text: That is called the unmanifest and the imperishable. It is the highest goal. Having reached it, one does not return. It is my supreme abode. The verse calls the destination paramam dhama, the supreme abode. It is the highest goal, and reaching it means one does not return. Krishna now explains how Arjuna can reach this supreme person through undivided devotion.

en/8-21-intro-0b24dff8.mp3.text: Where does the cycle of return end? Krishna names the destination as the imperishable and unmanifest. Listen for the word that marks the final departure.

en/8-21-intro-5a0fd1ff.mp3.text: After describing a reality beyond the changing world, Krishna turns to Arjuna. He now names the destination itself. Listen for the word that marks the end of every cycle of return.

en/8-22-body-b8dd4ba6.mp3.text: O Arjuna, the supreme person is reached through undivided devotion. All beings dwell within that being, and this entire world is pervaded by that being. Krishna names the supreme person as the one in whom all beings dwell, and who pervades this entire world, and then he names undivided devotion as the way to reach that very being. He now speaks of the time when yogis leave this world and the time when they return to it.

en/8-22-intro-4f56ff63.mp3.text: Krishna now describes the supreme person and the path to reach him. Listen to how he links the way to him with what he already is.

en/8-23-body-2a225b97.mp3.text: I will tell you of the time when yogis do not return, and the time when they do, O best of the Bharatas. Notice the pair, anavrttim and avrttim. One is non-return, the other is return. Krishna promises to name the exact times that send a departed yogi down one road or the other. He begins that explanation by naming the fire, the daylight, and the bright half of the month as paths of return.

en/8-23-intro-dc48b10f.mp3.text: Krishna now shifts from the nature of the supreme being to the moment of leaving the body. Listen for the two words that mark the two paths after death.

en/8-24-body-e288399d.mp3.text: Fire, daylight, the bright fortnight, and the six months of the northward course: those who depart then, knowing the supreme reality, go to the supreme reality. Listen to the list of light, agni, jyoti, daylight, the bright fortnight, and uttarayan, the northern course. These are not random times; they trace the bright path of the sun, the route through which the knower of Brahman departs. Krishna then names the opposite path of smoke and night, the route that leads the departing soul back to earth.

en/8-24-intro-2d373ab7.mp3.text: Krishna has just spoken of the times when a yogi departs and returns, and now he names the very path that leads away from return.

en/8-25-body-0a2dd004.mp3.text: In the path ruled by smoke, night, the dark fortnight, and the six months of the southern course, the yogi who departs there returns after reaching the moon's light. The verse lists four images: smoke, night, the dark fortnight, and the southern half-year. The yogi who departs there reaches lunar light and returns. The next verse states that these two paths are the eternal ways of the world, one leading to no-return, the other to return.

en/8-25-body-ec854f1e.mp3.text: In the path ruled by smoke, night, the dark fortnight, and the six months of the southern course, the yogi who departs there returns after reaching the moon's light. The crucial word here is निवर्तते, returns. The yogi reaches the lunar light, but that light is only a stopover, and he must come back. Krishna now states plainly that these two paths, bright and dark, govern all mortal departure forever.

en/8-25-intro-4d2ba3b8.mp3.text: Krishna has just described the bright path that leads beyond return; now he turns to the opposite. Listen for the word that seals the fate of the traveler.

en/8-25-intro-c5ba4293.mp3.text: Krishna now names the opposite path, the one that leads back to birth. Listen to the sequence of images that mark it.

en/8-26-body-1b5c5b4b.mp3.text: The bright and the dark are the two eternal paths of the world. One leads to non-return; the other brings return again. Listen again to the word अनावृत्तिम्, non-return. The bright path does not end in another birth; it ends birth altogether, while the dark path merely sends the soul back. Krishna then says that knowing these two paths protects a yogi from confusion and delusion.

en/8-26-body-498ba93b.mp3.text: The bright and the dark are the two eternal paths of the world. One leads to non-return; the other brings return again. The two paths are called shuklakrisne, the bright and the dark. One leads to non-return, the other brings the traveler back again, and this is true for the entire world. Krishna says the yogi who knows these two paths is never deluded, so remain steadfast in yoga at all times.

en/8-26-intro-c8c28734.mp3.text: Krishna has just described the dark path of smoke and night, where the yogi returns after reaching the moon. Now he names the larger rule that governs both routes.

en/8-26-intro-d7a87fd4.mp3.text: Krishna has just described the path of smoke and night. Now he answers what lies beyond. Listen for the two eternal roads that every soul travels.

en/8-27-body-a37e43ad.mp3.text: O Arjuna, the yogi who knows these two paths is never deluded. Therefore, remain steadfast in yoga at all times. The word yogi is joined in yoga. The word deluded means confused, and the word knowing means understanding. The yogi who understands these two paths is never confused, so Krishna tells Arjuna to be joined in yoga at all times. Knowing these two paths, the yogi goes beyond the merits of the Vedas and reaches the supreme abode.

en/8-27-intro-20de0145.mp3.text: Krishna has just shown the two routes the soul takes after death. Arjuna stands frozen between them. Listen to the simple command Krishna gives.

en/8-28-body-45bfef08.mp3.text: Knowing the two paths, the yogi goes beyond all the merits declared in the Vedas, sacrifices, austerities, and gifts, and reaches the primal supreme abode. The word is atyeti, meaning goes beyond. The yogi does not merely collect the fruits of sacrifice and austerity; knowing the two paths, he passes beyond them all. Krishna now promises to reveal a secret knowledge that frees you from all that is harmful.

en/8-28-body-aab96643.mp3.text: Knowing the two paths, the yogi goes beyond all the merits declared in the Vedas, sacrifices, austerities, and gifts, and reaches the primal supreme abode. Notice the single word अत्येति, which means goes beyond. The yogi does not merely gain merit, he goes beyond all of it, leaving behind the rewards of sacrifice, austerity, and gift. Krishna now promises to share an even deeper secret, one that will free Arjuna from all harmful things.

en/8-28-intro-31f3de0d.mp3.text: Listen for one action that the yogi performs, an action that moves him past the highest rewards of ritual.

en/8-28-intro-3e8a73f0.mp3.text: Krishna points to a single word that marks the limit of all religious action: listen for the verb that means to go beyond.

en/8-3-body-a712e5f3.mp3.text: The imperishable is the supreme reality. One's own nature is called the inner self. The offering that brings beings into existence is called action. Krishna names three things in one breath. First, the imperishable, aksharam, is the supreme reality, Brahman. Then he says your own nature, svabhavah, is the inner self, adhyatma. Finally, the offering that brings beings into existence is called action. Krishna now turns to the body and the cosmic person, showing how the perishable and the radiant meet. He says I am the inner witness in this body, Arjuna.

en/8-3-intro-8cf9117c.mp3.text: Krishna begins to answer by naming three things. Listen for how he defines the imperishable reality, the inner self, and the act that creates life.

en/8-4-body-845ba5b5.mp3.text: The perishable world is the lower realm; the cosmic person is the radiant being. I am the inner witness of sacrifice in this body, Arjuna. Krishna calls himself the inner witness of sacrifice inside the body, adhhiyajna, and says this is true for every embodied being, var. He then says that whoever remembers him at the end and leaves the body attains his state.

en/8-4-intro-77792388.mp3.text: Krishna now answers Arjuna's question about the terms needed for dying with awareness. Listen for the three things he names.

en/8-5-body-3dfb20b3.mp3.text: Whoever remembers Me at the end and leaves the body attains My state; there is no doubt. Whoever remembers Krishna at the end and leaves the body reaches his state, he says, without doubt. Krishna now explains why the state a person remembers is exactly the state they reach.

en/8-5-intro-7184e49f.mp3.text: Krishna has just described the sacred act and the cosmic person. Now he gives the final promise.

en/8-6-body-e1486bc7.mp3.text: Whatever state a person remembers at the end, that state is reached, because the mind has been shaped by it. Krishna does not say the final thought is a sudden accident. He says the mind is always formed by that state, meaning the final thought is simply the deepest habit of a lifetime. Krishna then tells Arjuna to make that habit of remembering Him his daily practice.

en/8-6-intro-337b3128.mp3.text: If you remember Me at death, you reach Me, Krishna said in the last verse. But what if you remember something else? Here is the answer.

en/8-7-body-9a648787.mp3.text: Therefore, remember Me at all times and fight. With mind and intellect offered to Me, you will surely come to Me. Notice the pairing in this verse. Krishna commands Arjuna to remember Me at all times and to fight. Remembrance and action are not separate. Krishna then explains that the final thought at the moment of death determines the final destination.

en/8-7-intro-848a33a0.mp3.text: Krishna has taught that the final thought shapes the final destination. Now he gives Arjuna two commands together.

en/8-8-body-3ad7fc08.mp3.text: One who departs while remembering the divine person with a mind trained by practice and fixed on nothing else reaches that supreme divine being, O Partha. Listen for nanyagamina, meaning not going elsewhere. A mind trained by steady practice and fixed on nothing else reaches the supreme person at the moment of death. Krishna turns to the nature of the supreme person, who is beyond thought and radiant like the sun.

en/8-8-intro-00c0b5c5.mp3.text: Listen closely for one word, and you will hear how Krishna describes the exact state of mind that reaches the supreme divine at the moment of death.

en/8-9-body-55594a93.mp3.text: Whoever remembers the wise, ancient, ruler, subtler than the subtle, supporter of all, beyond thought, radiant like the sun, and beyond darkness... This verse names the divine as anushastaram, the ruler. This is not a king of a land, but the ruler of the self, the one who governs the inner life. Krishna now explains the exact physical and mental steps one must take at the moment of death to reach that ruler.

en/8-9-intro-395003f1.mp3.text: Arjuna has learned how to fix his mind at the moment of death. Now Krishna describes the reality he is meant to hold in mind. Listen to how the divine is defined.

en/9-1-body-5f505cc0.mp3.text: The Blessed Lord says: I will now tell you this most secret knowledge, joined with direct realization, to you who are not envious. Knowing it, you will be freed from all that is harmful. Listen to the word anasyave, without envy. Krishna offers a guarded secret, knowledge joined with realization, to a student who is free from hostility. He calls it the king of all secrets, supremely pure and directly knowable.

en/9-1-intro-29cf31a2.mp3.text: Krishna carries on by saying he will reveal the deepest teaching, but only because Arjuna has no envy.

en/9-10-body-fd3cb649.mp3.text: Nature, under my supervision, brings forth all moving and unmoving beings. Because of this, the world keeps changing, O son of Kunti. The reason the world keeps turning is hetuna anena, because of this. Krishna says that nature itself gives birth to everything under his watch, and that is why the world changes. Next, Krishna continues.

en/9-10-intro-ed1cb8bb.mp3.text: Krishna is answering Arjuna's deepest confusion. After saying he is not bound by creation, he now explains how the world actually keeps turning. Listen for the reason.

en/9-11-body-243f5674.mp3.text: Fools despise Me when I dwell in a human form, not knowing My higher nature as the great Lord of all beings. The deluded see only a human body, mam, and despise Me, missing My parambhavam, My higher nature, as the great Lord of all beings. Krishna next describes the confused minds of those who take shelter in deluding and demonic nature.

en/9-11-intro-c919bdb1.mp3.text: Krishna continues by naming the ones who fail to see him, and how they see him.

en/9-12-body-36d79416.mp3.text: Those whose hopes, actions, and understanding are all wasted, confused minds take shelter in deluding, demonic, and shadowy nature. Notice that the verse repeats a single root idea three times. moha means wasted, and the verse strings moha-asha, moha-karman, and moha-jnana together to show that a confused mind makes every hope, every action, and every thought go to waste. Krishna now turns to the great-minded ones, the ones who rely on a divine nature and worship him with single-pointed minds.

en/9-12-intro-7149bb17.mp3.text: Why do some people turn away from truth? Krishna answers with a pattern of collapse. Listen for three words that all mean the same thing: wasted.

en/9-13-body-301f9c19.mp3.text: But, Arjuna, the great-minded ones, relying on the divine nature, worship Me with one-pointed minds, knowing Me as the unborn and imperishable source of all beings. Ananyamanasah means minds fixed on nothing else. The great-minded do not scatter their attention; they hold it on Krishna alone and worship him as the imperishable source of all beings. Krishna then describes how these steadfast souls worship him through chanting, striving, and bowing.

en/9-13-intro-97820a7f.mp3.text: Krishna contrasts the deluded with the great-minded. Listen for the kind of mind that can truly see him.

en/9-14-body-0d785e86.mp3.text: Ever united with Me, steadfast in vows, they worship Me by chanting, striving, and bowing with devotion. The word kritayantah, chanting, comes second, but the first action is kritayantah, chanting. Krishna places the chanting of his name at the very start of the practice. Krishna then describes a second way these devotees worship him, through the sacrifice of knowledge.

en/9-14-intro-cc8444fc.mp3.text: Krishna asks you to listen for the first action that comes in this list of devotion. Hear how the verse begins.

en/9-15-body-165519cf.mp3.text: Others worship Me through the sacrifice of knowledge, seeing Me as one, as separate, or as the all-facing form. The word ananye, others, tells us that Krishna is adding another kind of worshipper to the list, one who comes not with flowers but with understanding. Krishna now speaks of the all-facing form, the one who sees everything at once.

en/9-15-intro-f13a3890.mp3.text: Arjuna has watched Krishna teach many paths. Now Krishna names the path of understanding. Listen for how many ways he says a person can know him.

en/9-16-body-3c28e9a8.mp3.text: I am the sacrifice, I am the ritual, I am the offering, I am the herb, I am the mantra, I am the ghee, I am the fire, and I am the act of offering. I am the sacred syllable Om, the Vedas, the father, mother, supporter, grandfather, object of knowledge, purifier, and imperishable seed of this world. Krishna says he is the fire, the ghee, the herb, and the act of offering, so the worshipper, the worship, and the object of worship are all one. He continues to say he is the father, the mother, and the grandfather of this world.

en/9-16-intro-ef1b8635.mp3.text: Last time Krishna said people worship him in many ways, and now he names every part of the sacred fire ritual.

en/9-17-body-564f458e.mp3.text: I am the father of this world, the mother, the supporter, and the grandfather. I am the object of knowledge, the purifier, the sacred syllable Om, and also the Rig, Sama, and Yajur Vedas. Listen to how the verse moves from family to scripture: father, mother, grandfather, and then the Rig, Sama, and Yajur. He is not only the world’s ancestor but also the knowledge that gives it order. Krishna then continues to name himself as the goal, the shelter, and the final resting place of all things.

en/9-17-intro-0a404e3e.mp3.text: The Gita has been listing what Krishna is. Now he moves from the ritual to the source. What is the answer to the question of where everything comes from?

en/9-18-body-f95da7a4.mp3.text: I am the goal, the supporter, the lord, the witness, the refuge, the friend, the source, the dissolution, the resting place, the treasure, and the imperishable seed. Krishna lists eleven roles and claims them all. He is the goal, the supporter, the lord, the witness, the dwelling, the refuge, the well-wisher, the source, the dissolution, the resting place, the treasure, and the imperishable seed. Krishna then says he heats the world as the sun, holds back the rain, and is both immortality and death.

en/9-18-intro-a9241b5b.mp3.text: Krishna now lists eleven roles he fills, from the start of creation to its end. Listen to how he names himself as the goal, the shelter, and the seed.

en/9-19-body-50f7d8ef.mp3.text: I heat the world as the sun, I hold back the rain and send it forth. I am immortality and death, being and non-being, Arjuna. The words amritam, immortality, and mrityuh, death, sit side by side. This is not a choice between them, but one reality holding both the welcome and the feared side of life. Krishna then turns to those who seek heaven through sacrifice, and to what they truly find there.

en/9-19-intro-9d5d3d5d.mp3.text: Krishna asks Arjuna to feel two forces in the world that shape everything, and to hear how they are named.

en/9-2-body-ffe87de4.mp3.text: This is the king of all knowledge, the king of all secrets. It is supremely pure, directly knowable, aligned with dharma, easy to practice, and imperishable. The word rajaguhyam, king of secrets, marks this knowledge as supreme. It is also abhyayam, imperishable, meaning it never fades away. Krishna then warns those who lack shraddha, trust, in this dharma and remain bound to rebirth.

en/9-2-intro-79557489.mp3.text: Krishna has promised a secret that frees the listener. Now he describes its nature. What makes this knowledge different from ordinary learning?

en/9-20-body-77ee72e6.mp3.text: Those who know the three Vedas, drink soma, and are purified by sacrifice pray for heaven. Having earned merit, they enjoy the divine pleasures of the realm of the radiant beings. Listen to the reward they ask for, heaven, and the pleasures they enjoy there. They reach the realm of the radiant beings, but their enjoyment is only the result of accumulated merit. Once their merit runs out, they fall back to the mortal world, caught in repeated coming and going.

en/9-20-body-834a6dd7.mp3.text: Those who know the three Vedas, drink soma, and are purified by sacrifice pray for heaven. Having earned merit, they enjoy the divine pleasures of the realm of the radiant beings. Soma-drinkers who pray for heaven do get it, and Krishna treats that as a limited bargain. Krishna then reveals what happens when their earned merit finally runs out.

en/9-20-intro-19b213bd.mp3.text: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna about the limits of ritual. He describes a group of people who perform sacrifices and ask for a specific reward. Listen to what they seek.

en/9-20-intro-5c510635.mp3.text: Krishna speaks to Arjuna about a specific group of ritualists. Listen to how he describes their worship and its reward.

en/9-21-body-c9c95959.mp3.text: After enjoying the vast heaven-world, they return to the mortal world when their merit is exhausted. Thus, those who follow the ritual path of the three Vedas and seek pleasures gain repeated coming and going. Heaven bought with merit runs out, Krishna says, and the buyer comes back down to earth. He then turns to those who fix their minds on him alone, offering a different kind of security.

en/9-21-body-ca2f051e.mp3.text: After enjoying the vast heaven-world, they return to the mortal world when their merit is exhausted. Thus, those who follow the ritual path of the three Vedas and seek pleasures gain repeated coming and going. The Sanskrit word क्षीणे, exhausted, describes merit that runs out. The seeker enjoys vast pleasures, but once the account is empty, they return to the mortal world to begin the cycle again. Krishna now points to those who worship him alone, and promises to carry their welfare himself.

en/9-21-intro-086344ea.mp3.text: Krishna continues his warning about the limits of reward-seeking religion, showing what happens to those who aim for heaven.

en/9-21-intro-2d4005c8.mp3.text: Krishna describes the heaven-world as a vast reward that ends. Listen for the moment when the soul must return to the mortal world.

en/9-22-body-3b98027f.mp3.text: Those who think of me alone and worship me with unwavering focus, I carry their welfare and security. The word ananyah means with no other focus, and Krishna promises to personally carry the welfare and security of those who keep their mind on him alone. He then addresses those who worship other radiant beings and says they still end up worshipping him, but in the wrong way.

en/9-22-intro-b1aa50be.mp3.text: Krishna has just exposed the limits of the ritual path. Now he makes a direct promise to those who turn to him with undivided attention.

en/9-23-body-f790edb7.mp3.text: Even those who, filled with trust, worship other radiant beings, worship Me alone, but in the wrong way, O son of Kunti. The word mamam eva, Me alone, appears in the second half. Krishna says that even those who worship other gods are in fact worshipping him alone, though they do not know the true way. Yet the next verse warns that because they do not know him in truth, their worship ultimately falls away.

en/9-23-intro-99d87ae2.mp3.text: Krishna turns to those who worship other radiant beings, showing that their trust still reaches him.

en/9-24-body-d6d6bf60.mp3.text: For I am the enjoyer and lord of all sacrifices. But those people do not know me in truth, and so they fall away. The hinge of the verse is the word abhijananti, they know. Krishna says that because people do not know him in truth, they fall away. Krishna then states that those who worship other beings reach those beings, but those devoted to him come to him.

en/9-24-intro-fa98fa14.mp3.text: Krishna says he is the one who receives every sacrifice. Listen to the word that captures what happens when people miss that truth.

en/9-25-body-7a8af1fb.mp3.text: Those devoted to the radiant beings reach the radiant beings. Those devoted to the ancestors reach the ancestors. Those devoted to spirits reach the spirits. But those devoted to me come to me. The verb yaanti, go or reach, is repeated four times to show that people reach exactly where they aim their devotion, and only those who aim at me reach me. Krishna then says that he accepts even a leaf, a flower, or water offered with devotion.

en/9-25-body-903f9491.mp3.text: Those devoted to the radiant beings reach the radiant beings. Those devoted to the ancestors reach the ancestors. Those devoted to spirits reach the spirits. But those devoted to me come to me. Listen to the word mamam, me, at the end of the verse. It is the destination for those whose devotion is aimed only at me, while other devotions reach other ends. Krishna then says he accepts even a simple leaf, flower, fruit, or water, if offered with devotion.

en/9-25-intro-3c7a02b1.mp3.text: Krishna has just said he is the true lord of all worship, and that people who do not know him fall away. Now he explains where different kinds of worship lead.

en/9-25-intro-e57ae6c3.mp3.text: Krishna has just said that all worship is aimed at him, yet people still worship many gods. Now he draws a clear line between them.

en/9-26-body-4b1b73ae.mp3.text: Whoever offers me a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water with devotion, I accept that devoted offering from the pure-hearted. The word I accept is a form of the verb to eat, and Krishna says he consumes whatever a pure-hearted person offers, from a leaf to water. Krishna then tells Arjuna to dedicate every action, meal, and gift to him.

en/9-26-intro-f6ad2528.mp3.text: Krishna continues to describe the relationship that can hold a life together, now turning to the smallest gifts a person can offer.

en/9-27-body-11d4fbc7.mp3.text: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer, whatever you give, and whatever austerity you practice, offer it to me. Yat means whatever. Krishna lists five acts, from doing to eating to giving, and tells Arjuna to make every one of them an offering to me. When every act is given back to him, Krishna says, you are freed from the bonds of action and its results.

en/9-27-intro-f6b1f9f1.mp3.text: Krishna asks how to turn daily life into worship. Listen for the one word that turns every act into an offering.

en/9-28-body-7d8b075f.mp3.text: In this way, you will be freed from the bonds of action and its results. Given over to renunciation-yoga, released, you will come to me. The word mamam kritva, by making it mine, means that the secret of this yoga is to surrender your actions to me. This act of surrender is what frees you. Krishna now reveals that this surrender leads to a direct communion with him, where he and the devotee dwell together.

en/9-28-intro-ef3660e0.mp3.text: Krishna has just told Arjuna to offer every action and its fruits to the divine. Listen to how this offering changes his very being.

en/9-29-body-66d2d83f.mp3.text: I am equal toward all beings. No one is hated by me, and no one is especially dear. But those who worship me with devotion dwell in me, and I dwell in them. The word samah means equal, and it reveals the divine stance as impartial. Then Krishna adds that even though he is equal to all, those who worship him with devotion find him dwelling within them. Krishna then widens this to say that even the worst person is counted righteous if they offer undivided devotion.

en/9-29-body-c2c72ebb.mp3.text: I am equal toward all beings. No one is hated by me, and no one is especially dear. But those who worship me with devotion dwell in me, and I dwell in them. Listen for the word समः, equal. The divine is not partial or biased, yet it is precisely this equal stance that allows the devotee to dwell within the divine and the divine to dwell within them. Krishna now turns to the person of bad conduct who worships with undivided devotion, saying they must be regarded as righteous.

en/9-29-intro-2a5e6d7f.mp3.text: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield about a divine presence that is everywhere and yet deeply personal.

en/9-29-intro-c969adb1.mp3.text: Krishna is telling Arjuna that the divine does not play favorites. Listen for the exact word that makes this claim.

en/9-3-body-81c182c6.mp3.text: O conqueror of foes, people without trust in this dharma do not reach Me and keep returning on the path of repeated death and rebirth. Listen to the word asradaddhanah, without trust. Krishna says people who lack this trust do not reach him and remain on the path of repeated death and rebirth. He then explains that the entire universe is pervaded by his unmanifest form, yet he does not dwell in beings.

en/9-3-intro-96bb1906.mp3.text: Krishna has just called this teaching the king of all secrets. Now he warns what happens to those who receive it without trust.

en/9-30-body-b8a15abe.mp3.text: Even if a person of very bad conduct worships Me with undivided devotion, that person must be regarded as righteous, for the resolve is rightly made. Krishna calls even a su-durachara, one of very bad conduct, a sadhu, a righteous person. The word that matters is samyak, properly, because the resolve is rightly made. Krishna now promises that devotion brings lasting peace and that his devotee never perishes.

en/9-30-intro-b5501950.mp3.text: Krishna has just said he is equal toward all beings, with no one hated or especially dear. Now he adds a startling condition. Listen to how he redefines righteousness.

en/9-31-body-97827155.mp3.text: One who is devoted to Me quickly becomes righteous and attains lasting peace. O son of Kunti, declare it boldly: My devotee never perishes. Krishna tells Arjuna to declare boldly. The Sanskrit word is pratijanihi, a public promise, and the promise is that the devotee never perishes. Krishna then names exactly who can take this refuge, leaving no one outside its reach.

en/9-31-intro-184a6530.mp3.text: Krishna asks Arjuna to make a promise to the world. Listen to the exact words he uses to seal this guarantee.

en/9-32-body-7a0d689b.mp3.text: O Partha, even those born in difficult circumstances, and women, merchants, and workers, can reach the highest state by taking refuge in me. The verse lists women, merchants, and workers, and those born in difficult circumstances, to show that none of these birth or social categories bar the way. The word vyapashritya, having taken refuge, is the single condition that opens the highest state to all. Krishna then asks what to speak of you, since even the most exalted have reached the same goal.

en/9-32-intro-4a9e75c4.mp3.text: The Gita has been speaking of devotion and refuge. Now, listen closely to who exactly Krishna includes in that promise of the highest state.

en/9-33-body-8a3b18ea.mp3.text: If even pure Brahmins and royal sages devoted to the divine reach the highest state, what to speak of you? So, having come into this impermanent and joyless world, worship Me. Krishna calls this world impermanent and joyless, and tells Arjuna to worship Him while he is in it. Krishna tells Arjuna to fix his mind on Him and bow to Him, promising union in return.

en/9-33-intro-741e3caf.mp3.text: Krishna compares Arjuna to the greatest devotees and rulers, then makes a final invitation. Listen to how he names this world.

en/9-34-body-70e76ece.mp3.text: Fix your mind on me. Be devoted to me. Worship me. Bow to me. United with me in this way, and fully oriented toward me, you will come to me. Krishna names four actions: fixing the mind, becoming a devotee, worshipping, and bowing. He then gives one promise that unites all four, showing that the entire path leads to him alone. Krishna opens the next chapter by promising a supreme word spoken for Arjuna's welfare because Arjuna is deeply dear to him.

en/9-34-intro-d8e7d2b7.mp3.text: Krishna asks Arjuna to direct four different actions toward him, and promises that this will bring Arjuna to him. Listen for how these four actions connect.

en/9-4-body-3ccb9200.mp3.text: All this universe is pervaded by my unmanifest form. All beings dwell in me, but I do not dwell in them. Listen to the word avyaktamurti, unmanifest form. It names the very ground that holds the entire world, yet it is not a thing you can look at or touch. Krishna then turns to the paradox of how all beings rest in him, while he remains beyond them.

en/9-4-intro-299b5830.mp3.text: Krishna describes his form not as a shape you can see, but as an unseen presence. Listen to the word that names this unseen presence.

en/9-5-body-a2a0d5bd.mp3.text: Behold My divine power: beings are not in Me, and yet I sustain all beings. Krishna offers a direct paradox: My self is not situated in beings, yet I am the source and nourisher of all beings. Krishna then offers the wind and space as an example of how beings rest in him.

en/9-5-intro-509bcae3.mp3.text: Krishna has just told Arjuna that the universe is pervaded by his unmanifest form. Now he asks Arjuna to look closer at how beings relate to his self.

en/9-6-body-ab7555a3.mp3.text: As the great wind, moving everywhere, always rests in space, so all beings rest in Me. The wind is everywhere, yet it never leaves the space it moves through, and the verse asks Arjuna to see every being resting in Krishna just as the wind rests in space. Krishna then explains what happens to all beings when a cosmic cycle ends and begins again.

en/9-6-intro-d9a28750.mp3.text: Krishna continues the thread of divine presence by giving a physical image. Listen to the wind and the space and what they mean.

en/9-7-body-2f2bbed9.mp3.text: O son of Kunti, at the end of a cosmic cycle all beings enter my nature; at its beginning, I send them forth again. Kunteya, O son of Kunti, is the address, and it turns a cosmic law into a conversation between teacher and student. Krishna tells Arjuna that all beings rest in his nature at the end of a kalpa and he sends them forth again at its start. He then explains that he takes hold of his own nature to create this multitude of beings again and again.

en/9-7-intro-48c9775e.mp3.text: Krishna asks Arjuna to look beyond the single war to the rhythm of the cosmos. Listen to the two moments that frame every life.

en/9-8-body-26b9853c.mp3.text: Taking hold of my own nature, I repeatedly create this entire multitude of beings, helpless under the sway of nature. The word prakritim swam, taking hold of my own nature, shows that Krishna does not force the world into being; he simply uses his own power to set the cycle in motion. He then explains that these repeated acts of creation do not bind him at all.

en/9-8-intro-1fdfb8b2.mp3.text: Krishna widens the view from one battlefield to the whole of creation. Listen for the cycle he describes.

en/9-9-body-a42ba29d.mp3.text: Those actions of creation do not bind me, Dhananjaya, because I remain detached and indifferent to them. Listen for the word asakta, unattached. Krishna says he remains asakta, unattached, in those actions, which means he does not cling to the creation he himself releases into the world. He follows this by saying he sits as a spectator, udasinavat, like one who is indifferent to what unfolds before him.

en/9-9-intro-c13618fa.mp3.text: Krishna has just described how he creates the world again and again. Now he tells Arjuna that these actions do not bind him. Listen for the word that shows how he stands apart.

hi/1-1-body-784378e3.mp3.text: धृतराष्ट्र पूछते हैं, हे संजय, धर्मभूमि कुरुक्षेत्र में युद्ध की इच्छा से इकट्ठे हुए मेरे और पाण्डु के पुत्रों ने क्या किया? मामकाः का अर्थ है मेरे। पाण्डव उनके भाई के बेटे हैं, उन्हीं के घर में पले, फिर भी इस एक शब्द से वे परिवार को मेरे और उनके में बाँट देते हैं। संजय का उत्तर राजा के अपने बेटे दुर्योधन से शुरू होता है, जो पाण्डवों की सेना को देख रहा है।

hi/1-1-intro-ca26d8e4.mp3.text: एक नेत्रहीन राजा अपने महल में बैठे दो सेनाओं के बारे में एक सवाल पूछते हैं।

hi/1-10-body-0adf3377.mp3.text: दुर्योधन कहता है कि भीष्म जिसकी रक्षा कर रहे हैं, हमारी वह सेना पाण्डवों को जीतने में अपर्याप्त है, और भीम जिसकी रक्षा कर रहे हैं, पाण्डवों की यह सेना हमें जीतने में पर्याप्त है। गीता प्रेस के अनुवाद के अनुसार इसका कारण यह है कि भीष्म दोनों पक्षों से स्नेह रखते हैं, जबकि भीम पूरे मन से अपने पक्ष के साथ हैं। शब्द अपर्याप्तम् का अर्थ है अपर्याप्त। दुर्योधन खुलेआम कहते हैं कि उनकी सेना, जिसकी रक्षा भीष्म कर रहे हैं, अपर्याप्त है, जबकि पाण्डवों की सेना, जिसकी रक्षा भीम कर रहे हैं, पर्याप्त है। वे फिर आदेश देते हैं कि हर तरफ से भीष्म की रक्षा की जाए।

hi/1-10-body-b0175841.mp3.text: दुर्योधन कहते हैं, भीष्म की रक्षा में हमारी सेना अपर्याप्त है, परन्तु भीमा की रक्षा में पाण्डवों की सेना पर्याप्त है। दुर्योधन अपनी ही सेना को अपर्याप्त और पाण्डवों की सेना को पर्याप्त कहते हैं। उन्हें अपने बल पर संदेह है क्योंकि उनकी तरफ भीष्म हैं और दूसरी तरफ भीम। वे अपने सेनापतियों को आदेश देते हैं कि वे हर ओर से भीष्म की रक्षा करें।

hi/1-10-intro-0ea8f9d4.mp3.text: सुनिए वह शब्द जिसे दुर्योधन अपनी सेना के लिए इस्तेमाल करते हैं, जो भीष्म के प्रति उनके मन के संदेह को उजागर करता है।

hi/1-10-intro-2e5d2c36.mp3.text: सुनिए, युद्ध शुरू होने से पहले दुर्योधन दोनों सेनाओं को परखते हुए कौन से शब्द इस्तेमाल करता है।

hi/1-11-body-b53ffe86.mp3.text: दुर्योधन कहता है, आप सभी मोर्चों पर अपनी-अपनी जगह पर दृढ़ता से स्थित रहें और चारों ओर से पितामह भीष्म की ही रक्षा करें। सब अपने मोर्चे पर डटकर भीष्म की ही रक्षा करें संजय फिर धृतराष्ट्र को बताते हैं कि पितामह भीष्म शेर की तरह दहाड़े और अपना शंख जोर से बजाया, जिससे दुर्योधन खुश हो गया।

hi/1-11-intro-159f568b.mp3.text: दोनों सेनाओं को देखने के बाद, दुर्योधन अपना पहला आदेश देता है। सुनिए, कैसे वह एक ही व्यक्ति को पूरी युद्ध-योजना के केंद्र में रखता है।

hi/1-12-body-f2232bdf.mp3.text: दुर्योधन की बातों में छिपी घबराहट भीष्म समझ गए। उन्होंने शब्दों में उत्तर देने के बजाय सिंह की तरह ऊँची गर्जना की और ज़ोर से अपना शंख बजाया। भीष्म कोई बात नहीं करते। वे सिंह की तरह दहाड़ते हैं और ज़ोर से शंख बजाते हैं, और उनकी इस आवाज़ से दुर्योधन का मन खुशी से भर जाता है क्योंकि बूढ़े सेनापति ने राजा का डर पढ़ लिया है और युद्ध का इशारा दे दिया है। तभी दोनों सेनाओं की ओर से एक साथ शंख, नगाड़े और तुरही बजने लगते हैं और उनकी आवाज़ बादलों की गड़गड़ाहट जैसी हो जाती है।

hi/1-12-intro-cacfb899.mp3.text: दुर्योधन अपने सैनिकों को भीष्म की रक्षा करने का आदेश देता है, और बूढ़े सेनापति का जवाब अपने शंख के एक प्रहार से आता है।

hi/1-13-body-56ba04d4.mp3.text: भीष्म के शंखनाद के बाद कौरव पक्ष के सारे वाद्य अचानक एक साथ बज उठे। उनकी मिली-जुली आवाज़ बड़ी भयंकर थी। सहसा एव का अर्थ है एक साथ, और यह बताता है कि पूरी सेना अचानक एक साथ अपने सेनापति के पीछे बज उठी। फिर माधव और पांडव अपने महान रथ पर बैठकर अपने दिव्य शंख बजाते हैं।

hi/1-13-intro-ef2cf660.mp3.text: संजय उस क्षण का वर्णन करते हैं जब युद्धभूमि ध्वनि से गूंज उठती है, और भीष्म के आह्वान पर हर वाद्य एक साथ बज उठता है।

hi/1-14-body-26426186.mp3.text: ततः श्वेतैर्हयैर्युक्ते महति स्यन्दने स्थितौ । माधवः पाण्डवश्चैव दिव्यौ शङ्खौ प्रदध्मतुः । माधव और पाण्डव, दो नाम हैं पर दोनों एक ही रथ पर बैठे हैं। श्लोक में दोनों का नाम एक साथ आता है, जो बताता है कि वे एक साथ आगे बढ़ रहे हैं। कृष्ण ने पांचजन्य और अर्जुन ने देवदत्त शंख बजाया, जिससे कौरवों के शोर का उत्तर उनके अपने दिव्य नाद से मिला।

hi/1-14-intro-39941277.mp3.text: कौरव पक्ष का शोर अभी गूँजा ही था कि अब दूसरे पक्ष से दो शंख एक साथ उत्तर देते हैं। सुनिए, इन्हें कौन बजा रहा है।

hi/1-15-body-46166c9a.mp3.text: हृषीकेश भगवान श्रीकृष्ण ने पाञ्चजन्य, धनञ्जय अर्जुन ने देवदत्त, तथा भीमकर्मा वृकोदर ने पौण्ड्र नामक महाशंख बजाया। यहाँ हर शंख का अपना एक नाम है, पाञ्चजन्य, देवदत्त और पौण्ड्र। ये पाण्डव पक्ष के तीन सबसे बड़े योद्धाओं के नाम वाले साज़ हैं। अब अन्य पाण्डव भाइयों के शंखों का जिक्र आता है, जो सेना की पूरी तैयारी दिखाते हैं।

hi/1-15-intro-3e993b3e.mp3.text: युद्ध शुरू होते ही जो शंख बजते हैं, उनके नाम सुनिए। यहाँ तीन महान योद्धाओं का जिक्र है।

hi/1-16-body-43e08ece.mp3.text: राजा कुन्तीपुत्र युधिष्ठिर ने अनन्तविजय नाम का शंख बजाया। नकुल और सहदेव ने सुघोष और मणिपुष्पक नाम के शंख बजाए। इस श्लोक में तीन भाइयों का नाम एक साथ आया है, लेकिन क्रम महत्वपूर्ण है। सबसे बड़े, राजा युधिष्ठिर, पहले अनन्तविजय बजाते हैं, और उनके बाद जुड़वाँ भाई नकुल और सहदेव अपने शंख बजाते हैं। अगले श्लोक में उन योद्धाओं का नाम आता है जो पाण्डव भाइयों के पीछे युद्धभूमि में उतरते हैं।

hi/1-16-intro-5cfa8c77.mp3.text: पाण्डवों के शंख पहले ही बज चुके हैं। अब बाकी तीन भाई भी अपनी आवाज़ में शामिल होते हैं। सुनिए कौन-सा शंख कौन बजाता है।

hi/1-17-body-40a48c35.mp3.text: हे राजन् श्रेष्ठ धनुषवाले काशिराज और महारथी शिखण्डी तथा धृष्टद्युम्न एवं राजा विराट और अजेय सात्यकि ने भी अपने-अपने शंख बजाए। शिखण्डी और धृष्टद्युम्न एक ही परिवार के हैं, फिर भी वे पाण्डव पक्ष में खड़े हैं। इससे यह स्पष्ट होता है कि युद्ध ने पंचाल राज्य को भी बाँट दिया है। राजा द्रुपद, द्रौपदी के पुत्र और बलवान अभिमन्यु ने भी अलग-अलग अपने शंख बजाए।

hi/1-17-intro-8f8f3b9a.mp3.text: पाँचों पाण्डवों के बाद, संजय उन साथियों के नामों का वर्णन करते हैं जो युद्ध के लिए तैयार हैं। ध्यान से सुनिए।

hi/1-18-body-80adcfc8.mp3.text: राजन्, राजा द्रुपद, द्रौपदी के पाँचों पुत्र, और लंबी भुजाओं वाले सुभद्रापुत्र अभिमन्यु ने सब ओर से अलग-अलग अपने-अपने शंख बजाए। द्रुपद, द्रौपदी के पुत्र और अभिमन्यु अलग-अलग शंख बजाते हैं उस भयानक ध्वनि ने धृतराष्ट्र के पक्ष के हृदयों को चीर दिया, जो आकाश और पृथ्वी में गूँज उठी।

hi/1-18-intro-360e85ed.mp3.text: संजय ने पाण्डव सेना के महान योद्धाओं का नाम लिया है, अब वे उस ध्वनि का वर्णन करते हैं जो ये सब मिलकर कर रहे हैं।

hi/1-19-body-28ee54af.mp3.text: पाण्डव सेना के शंखों की वह भयंकर आवाज़ आकाश और पृथ्वी को गुँजाती हुई धृतराष्ट्र के पुत्रों के हृदय चीर गई। व्यदारयत् शब्द का अर्थ है फाड़ देना। पाण्डवों के शंखों की आवाज़ ने कौरवों के दिलों को फाड़ दिया, इससे पहले कि कोई हथियार छूटा भी नहीं। फिर भी अर्जुन, जो इस शोर के कारण हैं, खुशी से नहीं खड़े हैं। वे अपना धनुष उठाते हैं, युद्ध शुरू करने के लिए।

hi/1-19-body-5a8ba53a.mp3.text: संजय कहते हैं, पाण्डवों के शंखों की वह भयंकर आवाज़ आकाश और पृथ्वी को गुँजाती हुई धृतराष्ट्र के पुत्रों के हृदय चीर गई। पाण्डवों के शंखनाद ने कौरवों के हृदय विदीर्ण कर दिए अर्जुन अपने शत्रु पक्ष को देखकर युद्ध के लिए धनुष उठाते हैं।

hi/1-19-intro-00fb1b0d.mp3.text: पाण्डव सेना अपने शंख बजाती है। सुनिए कि वह आवाज़ दूसरी तरफ कैसे असर करती है।

hi/1-19-intro-d68bb00a.mp3.text: पाण्डव सेना के शंख बजते हैं और वह शोर इतना भयंकर है कि जैसे धरती ही हिल जाए। ध्यान से सुनिए कि यह शोर किसे डरा रहा है।

hi/1-2-body-d308cb5f.mp3.text: संजय कहते हैं, उस समय व्यूह में सजी पाण्डव सेना को देखकर राजा दुर्योधन अपने आचार्य द्रोणाचार्य के पास गए और उनसे बात करने लगे। इस पंक्ति में दुर्योधन अपने आचार्य द्रोणाचार्य के पास जाते हैं और उनसे बात करने लगे। वे अपने दादा भीष्म या अपने पिता धृतराष्ट्र के पास नहीं जाते। वे अपने गुरु के पास जाते हैं, जो उनके लिए सबसे भरोसेमंद व्यक्ति हैं। दुर्योधन सेना को दिखाते हुए द्रोणाचार्य से कहते हैं कि वे इस पाण्डव सेना को देखें।

hi/1-2-intro-ba8ff24e.mp3.text: संजय राजा के सवाल का जवाब देते हुए उनके बेटे दुर्योधन की तरफ मुड़ते हैं। सुनिए, दुर्योधन सबसे पहले किस व्यक्ति के पास जाता है।

hi/1-20-body-86dff5a7.mp3.text: तब, युद्ध की तैयारी और शस्त्रों के चलने से ठीक पहले, अर्जुन ने अपने गाण्डीव धनुष को उठाया। कपिध्वज शब्द पर ध्यान दें, जिसका अर्थ है हनुमान जी के चिह्न वाली ध्वजा। यह भक्ति का प्रतीक है जो उस युद्ध के मुहाने पर है, जिसे वह ही नष्ट करने वाले हैं। अर्जुन श्रीकृष्ण से कहते हैं कि वे रथ को दोनों सेनाओं के बीच रोकें ताकि वे उन लोगों को देख सकें जिनसे उन्हें युद्ध करना है।

hi/1-20-body-c4738628.mp3.text: हे महीपते, अब शस्त्रों के चलने की तैयारी हो ही रही थी कि उस समय अन्यायपूर्वक राज्य को धारण करनेवाले राजाओं और उनके साथियों को व्यवस्थित रूप से सामने खड़े हुए देखकर कपिध्वज पाण्डुपुत्र अर्जुन ने अपना गाण्डीव धनुष उठा लिया और अन्तर्यामी भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण से ये वचन बोले। इस श्लोक में हिंसा शुरू होने से ठीक पहले का क्षण बताया गया है, प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसंपाते, जब शस्त्रों के चलने की तैयारी हो ही रही थी। धृतराष्ट्र के पुत्रों को व्यवस्थित रूप से खड़ा देखकर अर्जुन ने अपना धनुष उठा लिया, पर उन्होंने अभी कोई बाण नहीं छोड़ा। अर्जुन अब बोलते हैं, और श्रीकृष्ण से अपने रथ को दोनों सेनाओं के बीच रखने के लिए कहते हैं।

hi/1-20-intro-880d5f31.mp3.text: सुनिए उस क्षण को जब पहला प्रहार होने ही वाला है। संजय हमें हिंसा की दहलीज पर ले आते हैं और उस योद्धा का नाम लेते हैं जो हिचकिचा रहा है।

hi/1-20-intro-b6d9bf8d.mp3.text: गीता के ठीक उस पल पर ध्यान दीजिए जब युद्ध शुरू होने ही वाला है। हनुमान जी के चिह्न और धनुष पर गौर करें।

hi/1-21-body-ab2e9e48.mp3.text: संजय बताते हैं कि हे राजन, तब अर्जुन ने श्रीकृष्ण से यह वचन कहा: हे अच्युत, मेरे रथ को दोनों सेनाओं के बीच में खड़ा कीजिए। अर्जुन अच्युत, यानी जो कभी न डिगने वाले हों, को पुकारते हैं और उनसे रथ दोनों सेनाओं के बीच में रखने को कहते हैं ताकि वे उन लोगों को देख सकें जिनके साथ उन्हें युद्ध करना है। अर्जुन फिर श्रीकृष्ण से कहते हैं कि वे रथ को रोक दें ताकि वे वहाँ खड़े हुए उन लोगों को देख सकें जो युद्ध के लिए आए हैं।

hi/1-21-intro-6df57b1e.mp3.text: अर्जुन ने अपना धनुष उठा लिया है, लेकिन अब वे रुक जाते हैं। वे अपने सारथी से रथ घुमाने और उन्हें मैदान के लोगों को दिखाने के लिए कहते हैं।

hi/1-22-body-a2695129.mp3.text: अर्जुन कहते हैं, हे अच्युत, मेरे रथ को तब तक दोनों सेनाओं के बीच में रखिए जब तक मैं इन योद्धुकामान् (युद्ध की इच्छा रखने वाले) योद्धाओं को न देख लूँ, ताकि जान सकूँ कि इस रणसमुद्यमे (युद्ध के अवसर पर) मुझे किनके साथ युद्ध करना है। अर्जुन फिर से शत्रुओं को देखने की इच्छा रखते हैं। यहाँ 'योद्धुकामान्' शब्द उनके योद्धा मन को दर्शाता है, जो अभी भी केवल युद्ध के बारे में सोच रहा है। वे उन योद्धाओं को देखना चाहते हैं जो दुर्योधन के लिए लड़ने के लिए एकत्र हुए हैं।

hi/1-22-body-ab507353.mp3.text: अर्जुन कहते हैं, हे अच्युत, इस युद्ध के अवसर पर मुझे किन-किन के साथ युद्ध करना है, यह जानने के लिए आप मेरे रथ को दोनों सेनाओं के बीच में तब तक रोके रखिए, जब तक मैं युद्ध की इच्छा से खड़े इन लोगों को देख न लूँ। ध्यान दीजिए, शब्द है कैः, यानी किसके साथ। अर्जुन यह जानना चाहते हैं कि उन्हें इस रण-प्रयास में किन-किन के साथ युद्ध करना है। वे उन लोगों को देखना चाहते हैं जो यहाँ एकत्रित हुए हैं और दुर्योधन को प्रसन्न करने के लिए युद्ध करने को उत्सुक हैं।

hi/1-22-intro-5aea82a0.mp3.text: अर्जुन अपनी वही बात दोहराते हुए कृष्ण से कहते हैं कि रथ को वहीं रोकिये, ताकि मैं इन योद्धाओं को ध्यान से देख सकूँ।

hi/1-22-intro-602987dd.mp3.text: रथ को बीच में रखने की बात को आगे बढ़ाते हुए, अर्जुन अपनी शर्त दोहराते हैं और देखने से पहले एक और बात कहते हैं।

hi/1-23-body-f4837c1c.mp3.text: अर्जुन कहते हैं कि दुष्टबुद्धि दुर्योधन का युद्ध में भला चाहने वाले जो ये राजालोग इस सेना में आये हुए हैं, युद्ध करने को उतावले हुए इन सबको मैं एक बार देख लूँ। अर्जुन उन्हें शत्रु नहीं कहता। वे दुर्योधन के लिए यहाँ आए उन लोगों को देखते हैं जो युद्ध करने को उतावले हुए हैं। संजय धृतराष्ट्र को बताते हैं कि कृष्ण ने रथ को भीष्म, द्रोण और सभी राजाओं के सामने दोनों सेनाओं के बीच खड़ा कर दिया।

hi/1-23-intro-9a24ff08.mp3.text: अर्जुन ने कृष्ण से रथ दोनों सेनाओं के बीच रोकने को कहा था। अब वे शत्रु पक्ष को देखते हैं और दूसरे पक्ष के लोगों को पहचानते हैं। वे क्या देखते हैं?

hi/1-24-body-01161964.mp3.text: संजय कहते हैं: हे भरतवंशी राजन, निद्रा को जीतने वाले अर्जुन के ऐसा कहने पर श्रीकृष्ण ने उस उत्तम रथ को दोनों सेनाओं के बीच में खड़ा कर दिया। इस श्लोक में हृषीकेश और गुडाकेश नाम आए हैं। भगवान ने दोनों सेनाओं के बीच में, पितामह भीष्म और आचार्य द्रोण तथा सभी राजाओं के सामने सबसे उत्तम रथ को खड़ा कर दिया। संजय आगे कहते हैं कि श्रीकृष्ण ने रथ को भीष्म और द्रोण के सामने खड़ा किया और फिर अर्जुन से कहा कि इन इकट्ठे हुए कुरुवंशियों को देख।

hi/1-24-intro-2eca856e.mp3.text: युद्ध का मैदान तैयार है। श्रीकृष्ण ने रथ को दोनों सेनाओं के बीच ले जाकर रोक दिया है। सुनिए, उन्होंने इसे कहाँ खड़ा किया।

hi/1-25-body-efe9ffbb.mp3.text: संजय कहते हैं, हे भरतवंशी राजन्, निद्राविजयी अर्जुन के द्वारा इस तरह कहने पर अन्तर्यामी भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण ने दोनों सेनाओं के मध्यभाग में पितामह भीष्म और आचार्य द्रोण के सामने तथा सम्पूर्ण राजाओं के सामने श्रेष्ठ रथको खड़ा करके इस तरह कहा कि हे पार्थ इन इकट्ठे हुए कुरुवंशियों को देख । कृष्ण 'पश्य' कहते हैं। वे 'लड़ो' या 'हमला करो' नहीं कहते। वे केवल देखने को कहते हैं, ताकि अर्जुन कोई भी कदम उठाने से पहले उन चेहरों को देख ले। कृष्ण दोनों सेनाओं के बीच रथ रोककर राजाओं के सामने अर्जुन से कहते हैं कि इन इकट्ठे हुए कुरुवंशियों को देखो।

hi/1-25-intro-098ab85b.mp3.text: सुनिए वह एक शब्द जो श्रीकृष्ण अर्जुन को युद्ध से पहले सामने देखने को कहते हैं।

hi/1-26-body-11cccb16.mp3.text: तत्रापश्यत्स्थितान्पार्थः पितृ़नथ पितामहान् । आचार्यान्मातुलान्भ्रातृ़न्पुत्रान्पौत्रान्सखींस्तथा । तत्र अर्जुन ने देखा कि पिता, पितामह, आचार्य, मामा, भाई, पुत्र, पौत्र, ससुर, मित्र और सुहृद वहाँ पर खड़े हैं। इन सभी सम्बन्धियों को देखकर अर्जुन शोक में डूब गए और भयभीत होकर बोले।

hi/1-26-intro-ca30172e.mp3.text: कृष्ण ने रास्ता दिखा दिया है, अब अर्जुन देखते हैं। युद्ध के मैदान पर वे जो देखते हैं, वह युद्ध को एक पारिवारिक त्रासदी बना देता है।

hi/1-27-body-a7a1fd37.mp3.text: संजय बताते हैं कि अर्जुन ने दोनों सेनाओं में अपने ससुरों, हितैषियों और सभी बंधुओं को देखा। इस दृश्य से अर्जुन का हृदय शोक में डूब गया और वे भयभीत होकर बोले। अर्जुन दोनों ओर देखते हैं और उन्हें सेनाओं में केवल अपने सगे-संबंधी, मित्र और हितैषी दिखाई देते हैं। वे शत्रुओं को नहीं, अपनों को ही युद्ध के लिए तैयार खड़े देखते हैं। अर्जुन कृष्ण से कहते हैं कि अपने लोगों को यहाँ देखकर वे करुणा और शोक से भर गए हैं।

hi/1-27-intro-d7484d3e.mp3.text: संजय आगे की कथा बताते हैं कि अर्जुन सेनाओं को देखकर क्या देखते हैं।

hi/1-28-body-0afdd953.mp3.text: अर्जुन कहते हैं, हे कृष्ण, इस कुटुम्बसमुदाय को अपने सामने उपस्थित देखकर जो मैं देखता हूँ उससे मुझे परम करुणा और शोक हो रहा है। अर्जुन सीधे कृष्ण से इस भावना का नाम लेते हैं: मैं परायः कृपया आविष्टः हूँ, यानी मैं परम करुणा से भर गया हूँ, और विषीदन् हूँ, यानी मैं शोक कर रहा हूँ। वे छिपाते नहीं हैं कि दृष्ट्वा इमं स्वजनम्, यानी अपने ही लोगों को देखकर वे शोक में डूब गए हैं। फिर वे उस शारीरिक पतन का वर्णन करते हैं जो इस करुणा और शोक के कारण उनके शरीर में हो रहा है।

hi/1-28-intro-39e97e5c.mp3.text: अर्जुन ने दोनों ओर के चेहरों को पहचान लिया है। अब वे कृष्ण से अपनी भावना का नाम लेते हैं। सुनिए, वे कैसे बोलते हैं।

hi/1-29-body-b8304b0d.mp3.text: अर्जुन कहते हैं: मेरे अङ्ग शिथिल हो रहे हैं, मुँह सूख रहा है, शरीर काँप रहा है और रोंगटे खड़े हो रहे हैं। यहाँ शरीर के हर हिस्से का नाम एक के बाद एक आता है। पहले पैर ढीले पड़ते हैं, फिर मुँह सूखता है, शरीर काँपता है और अंत में रोंगटे खड़े हो जाते हैं। यह हार मन से पहले शरीर में दिख रही है। इसके बाद वे कहते हैं कि हाथ से गाण्डीव धनुष गिर रहा है और त्वचा जल रही है, यानी पतन पूरा हो चुका है।

hi/1-29-body-e19131ee.mp3.text: अर्जुन कहते हैं: मेरे अंग ढीले पड़ रहे हैं, मुँह सूख रहा है, शरीर काँप रहा है और रोंगटे खड़े हो रहे हैं। शब्द गात्राणि का अर्थ अंग होता है। एक योद्धा के ये अंग यहाँ ढीले पड़ रहे हैं। उनके रोंगटे खड़े हो रहे हैं, लेकिन सबसे पहले उनके हाथ-पैर ही जवाब दे रहे हैं। वे अपने हाथ से गाण्डीव धनुष नहीं थाम पा रहे हैं और त्वचा जल रही है।

hi/1-29-intro-30ee65d7.mp3.text: अर्जुन सामने खड़ी सेना को देख रहे हैं। उनका शरीर उनके मन से पहले ही हार मानने लगा है।

hi/1-29-intro-75769dcd.mp3.text: अर्जुन युद्धभूमि पर अपने ही स्वजन को देख रहे हैं। उनका शरीर मन से पहले जवाब देने लगता है।

hi/1-3-body-1549ffb6.mp3.text: हे आचार्य, पाण्डुपुत्रों की इस विशाल सेना को देखिए, जिसे आपके ही बुद्धिमान शिष्य द्रुपदपुत्र ने व्यूहरचना से सजाया है। दुर्योधन उन्हें आचार्य कहकर पुकारते हैं, फिर शत्रु सेना की ओर इशारा करते हुए बताते हैं कि उनके सेनापति उनके ही शिष्य हैं। वे जान-बूझकर यह याद दिलाते हैं कि सामने वाला सेनापति उन्हीं की विद्या का छात्र है। फिर दुर्योधन पाण्डव सेना में खड़े उन महान योद्धाओं का नाम लेते हैं, जो भीम और अर्जुन के बराबर हैं।

hi/1-3-intro-ba5cc206.mp3.text: दुर्योधन अपने सेनापति के सामने खड़े होकर शत्रु सेना की ओर इशारा करते हैं। वे बताते हैं कि उनके सेनापति कौन हैं।

hi/1-30-body-9517a346.mp3.text: अर्जुन कहते हैं: गाण्डीव धनुष मेरे हाथ से फिसल रहा है, त्वचा जल रही है, मैं खड़ा भी नहीं रह पा रहा और मेरा मन चक्कर खाता-सा लग रहा है। गाण्डीव धनुष हाथ से फिसल रहा है। यह वही धनुष है जिसके बल पर अर्जुन अनेक युद्ध जीत चुके हैं, पर आज शोक ने उनके हाथ की पकड़ और मन दोनों ढीले कर दिए हैं। इसके बाद वे अपने शरीर में हो रहे बदलावों का वर्णन करते हैं, जैसे त्वचा का जलना और मन का चकराना।

hi/1-30-intro-adcf2001.mp3.text: अर्जुन हमेशा से महान योद्धा रहे हैं। ध्यान से सुनिए कि उनकी ताकत कहाँ से टूटने लगती है।

hi/1-31-body-cb0be7d1.mp3.text: हे केशव, मैं केवल विपरीत लक्षण देख रहा हूँ और मुझे युद्ध में अपने ही लोगों को मारकर कोई कल्याण भी नहीं दिखाई दे रहा है। अर्जुन कहते हैं कि उन्हें विपरीतानि, यानी विपरीत या अशुभ लक्षण दिख रहे हैं, और वे स्वजनम्, अपने ही लोगों को मारने में कोई श्रेयः, कोई भलाई नहीं देखते। अर्जुन कहते हैं कि उन्हें न तो जीत चाहिए, न राज्य, और न ही सुख।

hi/1-31-intro-6b10f602.mp3.text: अर्जुन ने अभी कृष्ण को बताया कि उनका शरीर कांप रहा है। अब वे कृष्ण को बताते हैं कि उन्हें चारों ओर क्या दिख रहा है।

hi/1-32-body-f0d5db41.mp3.text: हे कृष्ण, मैं न तो विजय चाहता हूँ, न राज्य और न सुख। हे गोविन्द, हमें ऐसे राज्य से, भोगों से या जीने से भी क्या लाभ? गोविन्द शब्द और 'हमें राज्य से क्या लाभ' को सुनिए। अर्जुन लक्ष्य को इसलिए नकारते हैं क्योंकि इसे पाने के लिए उन्हीं को मारना है जो उनके अपने हैं। वे अब उन लोगों की ओर देखते हैं जो सामने खड़े हैं, जिनके लिए ही उन्होंने कभी यह राज्य चाहा था।

hi/1-32-intro-b4542965.mp3.text: अपनी बात को आगे बढ़ाते हुए, अर्जुन अब युद्ध के मुख्य लक्ष्यों को ही नकार देते हैं। सुनिए वे उन्हें किस तरह नकारते हैं।

hi/1-33-body-5a357eae.mp3.text: जिनके लिए हम राज्य, भोग और सुख चाहते हैं, वही सब अपने प्राणों और धन की आशा छोड़कर यहाँ युद्ध में खड़े हैं। जिन लोगों के लिए हम राज्य और सुख चाहते थे, वही सब यहाँ अपने प्राण और धन त्यागने के लिए खड़े हैं। यही बात अर्जुन को अंदर से तोड़ देती है। अब वे दोनों सेनाओं में खड़े अपने स्वजनों, गुरुजनों और बड़ों के चेहरों को और करीब से देखते हैं।

hi/1-33-intro-111e639d.mp3.text: अर्जुन शत्रु सेना की ओर देखते हैं और पूछते हैं कि यह युद्ध वास्तव में किसके लिए है। सुनिए, वहाँ कौन खड़ा है।

hi/1-34-body-e2b1568f.mp3.text: आचार्य, पिता, पुत्र और इसी प्रकार पितामह, मामा, ससुर, पौत्र, साले तथा अन्य जितने भी सम्बन्धी हैं। वे एक-एक करके नाम लेते हैं, आचार्य, पिता, पुत्र, पितामह, मामा, ससुर, पौत्र, साले, और अंत में सभी सम्बन्धी। इस सूची के साथ युद्धभूमि एक पारिवारिक सभा बन जाती है जिस पर प्रहार करना वे सहन नहीं कर सकते। वे कहते हैं कि वे इनको मारना नहीं चाहते, भले ही ये उन्हें मार डालें, तो त्रिलोक के राज्य के लिए तो और भी नहीं।

hi/1-34-intro-ee54c000.mp3.text: अर्जुन युद्धभूमि पर अपने परिचित चेहरों को देखते हैं और एक-एक करके उनका नाम लेते हैं।

hi/1-35-body-60a143a7.mp3.text: अर्जुन कहते हैं: हे मधुसूदन, ये मुझ पर प्रहार करें तब भी मैं इन्हें मारना नहीं चाहता। तीनों लोकों का राज्य मिले तब भी नहीं, फिर इस पृथ्वी के राज्य के लिए तो बात ही क्या। एक वाक्यांश सुनिए, घ्नतोऽपि, यानी यदि वे मुझे मार भी दें। अर्जुन केवल डर नहीं रहे हैं, वे कह रहे हैं कि उनके जीवन का कोई मूल्य नहीं है और वे इसे तीनों लोकों के राज्य के लिए नहीं देंगे। तदनन्तर वे श्रीकृष्ण से पूछते हैं कि धृतराष्ट्र के पुत्रों को मारने से उन्हें क्या आनंद मिल सकता है।

hi/1-35-intro-55532430.mp3.text: अर्जुन अपने स्वजनों को देखकर अपना धनुष रोक देते हैं और पूछते हैं कि यदि इसकी कीमत उन्हें अपनी जान देकर चुकानी पड़े, तो इस राज्य से क्या लाभ। सुनिए वे अपने जीवन की तुलना कैसे करते हैं।

hi/1-36-body-163540df.mp3.text: हे जनार्दन, धृतराष्ट्र के पुत्रों और उनके साथियों को मारकर हमें क्या प्रसन्नता मिलेगी? ये आततायी हैं, फिर भी इन्हें मारने से हमें पाप ही लगेगा। धृतराष्ट्र के पुत्रों को मारकर क्या सुख, पाप ही लगेगा वे फिर पूछते हैं, अपने ही बंधुओं को मारकर हम कैसे खुश हो सकते हैं, हे माधव?

hi/1-36-intro-f2c1a7b0.mp3.text: अर्जुन ने अभी अपने परिवार और गुरुओं को मैदान में देखा है। वे शत्रुओं को पहचानते हैं, पर उनका मन इसमें नहीं है। सुनिए, वे क्या कीमत गिनते हैं।

hi/1-37-body-2f1f8300.mp3.text: धृतराष्ट्र के पुत्रों, जो हमारे अपने बान्धव हैं, उन्हें मारने के लिये हम योग्य नहीं हैं, क्योंकि अपने ही लोगों को मारकर हम कैसे सुखी होंगे? हे माधव। अपने बांधवों को मारना हमें उचित नहीं, फिर सुख कैसे मिलेगा फिर भी अर्जुन देखते हैं कि उनके विरोधी परिवार को नष्ट करने में गलती नहीं देखते।

hi/1-37-body-3880cccb.mp3.text: अतः हम अपने ही बंधुओं, धृतराष्ट्र के पुत्रों को मारने के योग्य नहीं हैं, क्योंकि हे माधव अपने ही लोगों को मारकर हम कैसे सुखी हो सकते हैं। अर्जुन शत्रुओं को स्वजनं, यानी अपने ही लोग, कहते हैं और फिर पूछते हैं कि उनके वध के बाद कोई सुख कैसे मिल सकता है। वे कहते हैं कि लालच ने धृतराष्ट्र के पुत्रों को अंधा कर दिया है, इसलिए वे परिवार नष्ट करने के अपराध को नहीं देख रहे।

hi/1-37-intro-7c5c634a.mp3.text: अर्जुन अब अंतिम सीमा खींचते हैं, और युद्ध के बदले अपने लोगों के सुख को चुनते हैं। एक शब्द पर ध्यान दें जो उनके इनकार को पक्का करता है।

hi/1-37-intro-8d3feacb.mp3.text: पिछले श्लोक में अर्जुन ने कहा कि मारने से केवल पाप लगेगा। अब वे पूछते हैं कि इसमें कैसी खुशी मिल सकती है।

hi/1-38-body-b850f56a.mp3.text: अर्जुन कहते हैं कि यद्यपि लोभ के कारण जिनका विवेकविचार लुप्त हो गया है, ऐसे ये दुर्योधन आदि कुल का नाश करने से होनेवाले दोष को और मित्रों के साथ द्वेष करने के पाप को नहीं देखते, तो भी हे जनार्दन कुल का नाश करने से होनेवाले दोष को ठीकठीक जाननेवाले हमलोग इस पाप से निवृत्त होने का विचार क्यों न करें एक वाक्यांश सुनिए, लोभोपहतचेतसः, यानी लोभ से अंधे हुए। कौरवों की आँखें इसलिए नहीं देख पातीं क्योंकि उनका मन लोभ से ढँक गया है, जिससे वे कुल के नाश का दोष और मित्रों के साथ द्वेष का पाप नहीं देख पाते। वह पूछते हैं कि चूँकि हम कुल के नाश का दोष स्पष्ट रूप से देख रहे हैं, तो हम इस पाप से दूर होने का विचार क्यों न करें।

hi/1-38-intro-013fb509.mp3.text: अर्जुन ने कहा कि वे अपने ही परिवार को नहीं मारेंगे। यहाँ वह बताते हैं कि दूसरी तरफ के लोग नुकसान को क्यों नहीं देख पा रहे हैं। सुनिए कि उनके अंधेपन का कारण क्या है।

hi/1-39-body-3b1d81c4.mp3.text: अर्जुन कहते हैं: हे जनार्दन, भले ही वे न देखें, पर कुल के नाश से होने वाले दोष को हम तो साफ़ देख रहे हैं। फिर हमें इस पाप से पीछे हटने का विचार क्यों नहीं करना चाहिए? वे दूसरे पक्ष के सहमत होने का इंतज़ार नहीं करते। वे कहते हैं कि भले ही वे न देखें, पर कुल के नाश का दोष हम तो साफ़ देख रहे हैं, और इसलिए हमें इस पाप से पीछे हट जाना चाहिए। वे चेतावनी देते हैं कि जब परिवार बिखर जाता है, तो उसकी प्राचीन परंपराएँ भी नष्ट हो जाती हैं।
